PREAMBLE TO THE DESCRIPTION: The following specification particularly describes the nature of this invention and the manner in which it is to be performed. A PROCESS FOR SEPARATION AND PURIFICATION OF RECYCLED LITHIUM CARBONATE FIELD OF THE INVENTION: The present invention relates to a field of chemical engineering. More particularly, the present invention provides an efficient process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION: The following background discussion includes information that may be useful in understanding the present invention. It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed invention, or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art. The growing global demand for lithium-ion batteries driven by the rise of electric vehicles, renewable energy storage, and portable electronics has placed increasing pressure on lithium resources, particularly lithium carbonate, a critical raw material in battery production. As lithium reserves are limited and primarily concentrated in a few countries, recycled lithium carbonate offers a more sustainable and secure alternative to mining. Recycling not only reduces environmental impact by minimizing the need for extraction and preventing battery waste, but it also supports circular economy goals and helps stabilize supply chains. With rising lithium prices and stricter sustainability regulations, recycled lithium carbonate is becoming both an ecological and economic necessity. JP3671148B2, the Japanese publication discloses a method for producing high purity lithium carbonate, The first impure Li2CO3 in an aqueous solution is reacted with CO2, dissolved LiHCO3, a step of producing a second aqueous solution containing dissolved compounds and insoluble compounds, wherein dissolve compound and the insoluble compound impure and which contains the impurities from the Li2CO3; A step of separating the unreacted CO2 and insoluble compounds from a second aqueous solution; By removing the dissolved impurities including the second aqueous solution is contacted with the ion-selective medium of divalent and trivalent ions, and separating the dissolved impurities from the second aqueous solution; And precipitating Li2CO3 from the second aqueous solution. WO2012083678A1, the PCT publication discloses method for preparing high-purity lithium carbonate, which is characterized by the following steps: a. The battery-grade lithium hydroxide monohydrate is formulated into a lithium hydroxide solution having a Li2O concentration of 50-90 g L; b. a CO2 flow rate of 3 to 5 L/s is introduced into the lithium hydroxide solution of step a. Gas, when the concentration of Li2O in the solution drops to 40g / L, the flow rate of CO2 is reduced to 2 ~3L / s; when the concentration of Li2O in the solution drops to 20g / L, the flow rate of CO2 is reduced to 0.8~ 1.2L/s; when a large amount of solids appear in the solution, stop aeration to obtain a lithium carbonate slurry; The lithium carbonate slurry obtained in steps c and b is separated, and the solid is washed with water and dried to a moisture content of less than 0.1%. US10336624B2, the US publication discloses a method of producing high-purity lithium carbonate from low-purity crude lithium carbonate. The method includes: (a) producing crude lithium carbonate slurry by mixing crude lithium carbonate having a polycrystalline state and a size of 20 to 200 μm with water; (b) carbonating and dissolving the crude lithium carbonate slurry; (c) performing primary solid-liquid separation to obtain a filtrate; (d) adding soluble barium salts to the filtrate to deposit barium sulfate; (e) performing secondary solid-liquid separation for the filtrate containing the deposited barium sulfate to obtain a filtrate; (f) mixing lithium carbonate seed crystals with the filtrate obtained from the secondary solid-liquid separation and precipitating lithium carbonate dissolved in the filtrate on surfaces of the lithium carbonate seed crystals to produce high-purity lithium carbonate slurry containing high-purity lithium carbonate by controlling a particle size; and (g) carbonating the high-purity lithium carbonate slurry to produce high-purity lithium carbonate. Further, the technical problem and drawbacks associated with existing technology/products/ process are mentioned below: • Environmental repercussions: The elevated temperatures employed in the existing process result in the emission of significant quantities of gases, which can adversely impact the environment and compromise air quality. • Requires a large amount of energy for heat, making the existing process energy-intensive if deriving lithium carbonate from spodumene. • Time consuming process.: The existing procedure necessitates considerable time investment during both the heating and cooling stages of the low purity lithium carbonate, which are critical for enabling subsequent reactions. The thermal cycles introduce delays that make the overall process more time-consuming and less efficient • High Energy Costs: The current existing technique necessitates substantial energy consumption to achieve and sustain these elevated temperatures, for deriving high purity lithium carbonate from spodumene, rendering the process both economically burdensome and unsustainable. • Harsh chemicals demonstrate a moderate level of corrosivity, particularly in relation to metallic substances, which may lead to the deterioration of equipment, pipelines, and storage containers. As a result, the utilization of corrosion-resistant materials becomes necessary, thereby increasing the operational expenses linked to its management and storage. • Reverse osmosis technology for the purification of lithium carbonate results in the high liquid-based waste generation. • High amount of water is consumed in the purification process to convert the lithium carbon into its purest form using sodium carbonate. • High CO2 emission during the purification procedure. Thus, there is a need for an efficient process for the separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate which provides a high purity Lithium Carbonate with less than 50 ppb impurity. There is a further need for an efficient process which has various advantages such as lower energy consumption, reduction in toxic emissions, more cost-effective and scalable Re-use ability of the Li washed solution again in the instant process, Zero liquid discharge and Zero direct CO2 emission. OBJECTIVE OF THE INVENTION: The primary objective of the present invention is to overcome the drawback associated with prior art. An objective of the present invention is to provide an efficient and effective process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate. Another objective of the present invention is to provide a cost effective and scalable process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate. Another objective of the present invention is to provide an efficient process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate resulted in reduction in Toxic Emissions. Another objective of the present invention is to provide an efficient and effective process involving low energy consumption in separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate Another objective of the present invention is to provide an efficient and effective process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate which can be implemented for re-use ability of the Li washed solution again in the ongoing process. Another objective of the present invention is to provide an efficient and effective process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate with zero liquid discharge Another objective of the present invention is to provide an efficient and effective process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate with zero direct CO2 emission. Another objective of the present invention is to provide an efficient and effective process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate can be implemented for selective removal of Impurities. Another objective of the present invention is to provide an efficient and effective process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate for obtaining a high purity lithium carbonate (Li2CO3) with less than 50 ppb impurity Another objective of the present invention is to provide an efficient and effective process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate can be implemented for selective removal of metal/ metal salts comprising Mn, Mg, Co, Cu, Ni, Fe, Al, Na, Zn, C, and K. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION: In an aspect the present invention provides an efficient and effective process for separation and purification of Recycled Lithium Carbonate, comprising steps: a) firstly, a low-purity lithium carbonate (Li₂CO₃) having concentration less than or equal to 15% of impurities and a demineralized (DM) water are mixed in a reaction vessel and heated to a temperature exceeding 60°C to obtain a lithium concentrated solution/slurry having lithium concentration above 18.78 grams per Liter thereafter, the resultant slurry undergoes continuous mechanical shear agitation at a rotational speed of 400-800 rpm maintaining a low pressure 0 to 2 bar at a consistent reaction temperature ranging 50-120 degree Celsius for a duration of 3 to 5 hours to obtain a effectively dissolved lithium concentration solution; b) in the second step, the obtained lithium concentration solution undergoes filter press at a pressure ranging 3-6 bar for removal of undissolved impurities such as Carbon, micro-plastic, undissolved particles of Sodium salt, cobalt salt, nickel salt, manganese salt, lithium phosphate, Iron salt, Aluminium salt, copper salt and Silica within the solution; c) in the third step, the filtered solution obtained in the previous step undergoes treatment with an alkali hydroxide and/or carbonates to salt out the impurities, wherein the solution is subjected to a high-shear agitation at a rate of 500 to 900 revolutions per minute (rpm) at a temperature ranging 60-100°C for a duration of 2-3 hours resulted in improving the purity of the solution by lowering the impurities within a range of 10 to 5 ppm by forming impurities into metal precipitates like Sodium salt, cobalt salt, nickel salt, manganese salt, lithium phosphate, Iron salt, Aluminium salt, copper salt, wherein the lithium and alkali hydroxide and/or carbonates are in the ratio of 1: 1.3 to 1.5 times;. d) in the fourth step, the obtained lithium concentration solution undergoes filter press process at a pressure ranging 3-6 bar for removal of the metal salt precipitate formed; e) in the fifth step, the filtered solution undergoes Organophosphorous complexing treatment with an organophosphorous compounds, wherein the solution is subjected to high-shear agitation at a rate of 500 to 900 revolutions per minute (rpm) at a temperature of 60-100°C for a duration of 2-3 hours resulted in improving the purity of the solution by lowering the impurities to a range less than 1 ppm by forming impurities into solid complex which is not dissolvable in water, wherein the impurities present and the organophosphorous compounds are in the ratio of 1: 1.5 to 1.7 times; f) in the sixth step, the obtained lithium concentration solution undergoes filter press process at a pressure ranging 3-6 bar for removal of the metal salt formed into solid complex; g) in the seventh step, the filtered solution undergoes selective adsorption process, wherein the filtered lithium concentration solution is directed made in contact with the adsorption polymers/polymer resin/organic solvent comprising iminodiacetic acid functional groups removes the metallic impurities including transition metals via chelation and forms a stable coordination complex resulting in lowering the impurities to a concentration of less than 500 ppb and provides a purified lithium solution ; wherein the adsorbate acts as a chelating ion exchange resin with iminodiacetic acid functional groups and the iminodiacetic acid functional group on the macroporous polymer matrix bind the metal ions via chelation and forms a stable coordination complex; h) in the eight step, the purified lithium solution undergoes thermal treatment, heated to a temperature exceeding 90-120°C to attain the optimised temperature, later an Aerial acid (H₂CO₃) and/or ammonium carbonate is added to the solution, wherein the aerial acid and/or ammonium carbonate reacts with the lithium ions, resulted in the formation of lithium carbonate (Li2CO3), followed by introducing carbon dioxide (CO2) into the solution at a pressure exceeding 4 atm and maintain the purging for a duration of 2.5-3 hours resulting in enhancing of the efficiency of lithium carbonate precipitation and aids in the removal of residual impurities and lowering the impurities to a concentration of less than 50 ppb and obtaining a high purity lithium carbonate (Li2CO3) with the rigorous purity standards necessary for high-value applications, such as battery-grade lithium compounds, wherein the lithium and Aerial acid (H₂CO₃) and/or ammonium are in the ratio of 1: 2 to 2.3 times. In another aspect the present invention provides a process, wherein the impurities in low purity lithium carbonate comprising metal/ metal salts such as Mn, Mg, Co, Cu, Ni, Fe, Al, Na, Zn, C, and K. In another aspect the present invention provides a process, wherein the filter press is a membrane comprising plate and frame, recessed chamber, and automatic filter presses having a flow rate ranging from 0.5 to 1 meter cube per hour. In another aspect the present invention provides a process, wherein a nylon-based filer cloth used in the filter press comprising polyester, polypropylene and having a pore size of filter cloth ranging 5-25 micron. In another aspect the present invention provides a process, wherein alkali hydroxide and/or carbonates comprising Na, K, ammonium, calcium. In another aspect the present invention provides a process, wherein the impurities precipitated in the third step and filtered in the fourth step comprising metal/ metal salts such as Fe, Cu, Al, Zn, Mn, Mg and Ni. In another aspect the present invention provides a process, wherein the organophosphorous compounds comprising Organophosphorus(V) compounds and Organophosphorus (III) compounds. In another aspect the present invention provides a process, wherein the impurities formed into solid complex in the fifth step and filtered in the sixth step comprising Al, Cu and Fe and other contaminants. In another aspect the present invention provides a process, wherein the iminodiacetic acid functional group on the macroporous polymer matrix which binds the metal ion via chelation by forming a stable coordination complex comprising Al, Fe, Cu, Ni, and Zn. This will dissolve all lithium present in the impure metal powder. Example-1 100 g of Impure lithium carbonate is dissolved in the 800 ml of pre-heated water at 60 oC with mechanical agitation in range between 400 rpm for above 3 hours. patents.abstract: The present disclosure relates to a passive cooling system for thermal management of a lithium-ion battery pack, particularly suitable for electric vehicle applications. The system comprises a battery pack having a plurality of battery cells, each surrounded by a capillary tube (104) with a sealed lower end and an open upper end. A sump (102) is positioned above the battery pack and is connected to the upper ends of the capillary tubes (104). The capillary tubes (104) and sump (102) are filled with a heat transfer fluid (110). Heat generated by the battery cells is transferred through conduction to the fluid (110) within the capillary tubes (104), and is transported upward to the sump (102) via natural convection, enabling cooling without any external power source. The system improves thermal regulation efficiency by utilizing micro-grooved capillary tubes (104) and strategic fluid circulation. The invention offers a reliable, energy-independent thermal management solution that enhances battery performance and safety during high-demand operation cycles.
patents.complete_specification: Description:FIELD OF INVENTION [0001] The present disclosure relates generally to the field of thermal management systems for energy storage devices, and more particularly, the present disclosure pertains to a passive cooling system for lithium-ion battery packs, especially suitable for electric vehicle applications. BACKGROUND [0002] Lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries are the backbone of electric vehicle (EV) propulsion technology due to their high energy density, long cycle life, and efficient power delivery. However, their performance and safety are significantly impacted by temperature. During high-rate charging and discharging cycles, battery cells tend to generate substantial heat due to internal chemical reactions and resistive losses. If this heat is not efficiently dissipated, the temperature of the battery pack can exceed safe operating limits typically above 45°C leading to degradation of battery capacity, reduced lifespan, or in extreme cases, thermal runaway, which may result in fires or explosions. [0003] To address these concerns, both active and passive cooling systems have been used in EV battery packs. Active systems include mechanisms such as pumps, fans, and refrigerants that forcibly remove heat from the battery module. While effective, these systems require external energy input, add mechanical complexity, increase system weight, and pose risks such as coolant leakage. On the other hand, passive cooling systems like phase change materials (PCMs), heat sinks, or metal matrices offer simpler designs without external energy input but often suffer from low heat transfer rates and slower response under high thermal loads. [0004] KR20230009158 (A) discloses a battery cooling apparatus that enhances cooling performance through the arrangement of upper and lower coolant passages surrounding the battery cells. The system employs a cooling fluid that flows through these passages to extract heat via forced convection. While the design improves heat exchange, it still depends on active circulation of coolant, making it energy-intensive, mechanically complex, and less suitable for weight-sensitive EV applications. [0005] KR102440189 (B1) describes an air cooling and heating system for EV battery packs using compressed air and a vortex generator to manage temperature. The system involves multiple components such as heat transfer pipes, cold air outlets, and separation chambers. However, air has poor thermal conductivity, and compressed air systems are inherently inefficient at removing heat quickly under high thermal loads. Moreover, reliance on moving parts and compressed gas systems increases complexity and energy requirements. [0006] KR20110090491 (A) relates to a cooling and heating device that uses oscillating heat pipes filled with working fluids in looped closed tubes. Though this approach is partially passive, it involves phase change and external heating or cooling units to drive circulation of the working fluid. Moreover, oscillating heat pipes require precise orientation and can suffer from performance degradation under variable gravitational or installation conditions. [0007] Hence, there is an urgent need for a simple, compact, and fully passive cooling system that overcomes the drawbacks of prior art by providing efficient thermal regulation of EV battery packs without external energy input, mechanical components, or reliance on forced convection. OBJECTS OF THE PRESENT DISCLOSURE [0008] Some of the objects of the present disclosure, which at least one embodiment herein satisfies are as listed herein below. [0009] An object of the present disclosure is to provide a passive cooling system for thermal management of a lithium-ion battery pack. [0010] Another object of the present disclosure is to enable efficient heat dissipation from battery cells without the use of any external power or mechanical device. [0011] Yet another object of the present disclosure is to employ capillary tubes wound around battery cells for uniform thermal conduction. [0012] Still another object of the present disclosure is to use micro-grooved capillary tubes to enhance heat transfer surface area and rate. [0013] A further object of the present disclosure is to utilize natural convection for the circulation of heat transfer fluid within the cooling system. [0014] Another object of the present invention is to maintain the battery temperature within the optimal operating range of 20°C to 45°C. [0015] Yet another object of the present invention is to minimize system complexity, size, and energy consumption in electric vehicle battery cooling. [0016] Still another object of the present invention is to increase the performance, safety, and lifespan of lithium-ion battery packs. [0017] A further object of the present invention is to provide a reliable and scalable passive thermal management solution for electric vehicle applications. SUMMARY [0018] This summary is provided to introduce a selection of concepts in a simplified form that is further described below in the detailed description section. This summary is not intended to identify key features or essential features of the claimed subject matter, nor is it intended to be used as an aid in determining the scope of the claimed subject matter. [0019] Aspects of the present disclosure relate to a passive thermal management system for lithium-ion battery packs, particularly designed for electric vehicles. The system employs capillary tubes wound around individual battery cells, filled with a heat transfer fluid, and connected to a sump located above the battery pack. Heat generated by the battery cells is transferred through the capillary tubes via conduction and is carried upwards to the sump through natural convection currents, without the need for any external energy input. The capillary tubes are micro-grooved to enhance the internal surface area and improve the rate of heat transfer, enabling consistent battery cooling, increased operational safety, and prolonged battery life. [0020] Accordingly, in an aspect, the present disclosure provides a passive cooling system for thermal management of a lithium-ion battery pack, the system comprising: (a) a battery pack comprising a plurality of battery cells; (b) a plurality of capillary tubes, each capillary tube being wound around a corresponding battery cell and having a sealed lower end and an open upper end; (c) a sump disposed above the battery pack and connected to the upper ends of the capillary tubes; and (d) a heat transfer fluid filled within the sump and the capillary tubes. The heat generated by the battery cells is transferred to the heat transfer fluid through the capillary tubes, and the heat is transported towards the sump via natural convection, thereby cooling the battery cells without the use of any external energy source. [0021] In some embodiments, each capillary tube is spirally wound over the corresponding battery cell. [0022] In some embodiments, the inner surface of each capillary tube comprises a plurality of micro-grooves. [0023] In some embodiments, the micro-grooves are selected from one or more geometries including U-shaped, sinusoidal, circular, triangular, or rectangular profiles. [0024] In some embodiments, the capillary tubes are made of a thermally conductive material selected from copper or aluminium. [0025] In some embodiments, heat transfer fluid comprises a fluid having high thermal conductivity, high specific heat, low viscosity, and high boiling point. [0026] In some embodiments, the cooling mechanism is solely driven by a combination of: a) heat conduction from the battery cell to the capillary tube; and b) natural convection circulation of the heat transfer fluid from the capillary tube to the sump and vice versa, without the assistance of any external power or mechanical device. [0027] In some embodiments, the sump is positioned vertically above the battery pack to facilitate natural convection flow maintaining the battery temperature within the range of 20°C to 45°C. [0028] In some embodiments, the battery pack has a length ranging from 5 to 200 cm, width ranging from 5 to 200 cm, and height ranging from 3 to 20 cm. [0029] In some embodiments, each of the battery cells has a diameter ranging from 0.5 to 5 cm and a height ranging from 2 to 15 cm; and each capillary tube has a diameter ranging from 0.01 to 0.1 cm and a height ranging from 1 to 50 cm; and the sump has a length ranging from 5 to 200 cm, a width ranging from 5 to 200 cm, and a height ranging from 1 to 10 cm. [0073] In various embodiments, the battery cells 106 are enclosed within a casing made of metal or non-metal materials, configured to support structural integrity and accommodate the capillary tube arrangement. [0074] In various embodiments, the heat transfer fluid 110 is selected to have thermal stability over repeated charge/discharge cycles, ensuring reliability under varying operational conditions. [0075] While the foregoing description discloses various embodiments of the invention, other and further embodiments of the invention may be devised without departing from the basic scope of the disclosure. The invention is not limited to the described embodiments, versions or examples, which are included to enable a person having ordinary skill in the art to make and use the invention when combined with information and knowledge available to the person having ordinary skill in the art. [0076] In an implementation of an embodiment, the effect of capillary tube 104 based natural convection cooling system is demonstrated on a single cell through computational simulations using ANSYS FLUENT software. The 18650 Li-ion cell was used for testing purpose. The cell has a diameter of 18 mm and a span of 65 mm. A sump 102 of size 50(L) × 50(W) × 20 (H) mm3 was kept 8.8 mm above the cell and filled with water as a heat transfer fluid 110. [0077] FIG 1 and 2 shows a geometrical view of the cell with the capillary tube 104 based natural convection cooling system. A copper tube of 1 mm diameter and 75 mm length is wound over the cell from the bottom of the sump 102 to the bottom of the cell. The tube remains in contact with the cell throughout the span. A heat generation rate of 15,000 W/m3 was considered for the cell. The following properties were used for Li-ion cell, heat transfer fluid 110 and capillary tube 104 while performing computational simulations. Property Heat Transfer Fluid (Water) Lithium-ion cell Capillary Tube (Copper) Thermal conductivity (W/m-K) 0.6 1.035 387.6 Density (kg/m³) 997 2604.92 8978 Specific heat (J/kg-K) 4186 894 381 [0078] FIG. 4 represents the temperature contours along the cell height without any cooling mechanism at a certain instant of time. The highest temperature was observed to be 328 K in the central part of the cell. [0079] FIG. 5 shows the temperature contours along the cell height after incorporating the capillary tube 104 based natural convection cooling system. The maximum temperature was reduced from 328 K to 307 K. Unlike without cooling case, the maximum temperature is observed at the bottom of the cell. [0080] FIG. 6 indicates the temperature distribution along the cell height with a measurement interval of 13 mm. It clearly shows the significant reduction in cell temperature after incorporating the capillary tube 104 based natural convection cooling system. The maximum and minimum reduction in cell temperature is 26 K and 16 K at the cell top and cell bottom, respectively. ADVANTAGES OF THE PRESENT DISCLOSURE [0081] The present disclosure provides a fully passive cooling system for lithium-ion battery packs, which operates without any external energy input, making it energy-efficient and suitable for electric vehicles where power consumption is critical. [0082] The use of capillary tubes wound around each battery cell ensures direct and uniform heat absorption from the cell surface, thereby promoting localized thermal control and reducing the risk of cell-specific overheating. [0083] The inner surface of the capillary tubes is provided with micro-grooves 112, which significantly increase the internal surface area and promote enhanced thermal conductivity, thereby facilitating faster heat transfer from the battery cells to the heat transfer fluid. [0084] The configuration of the system, with the sump placed above the battery pack, enables a natural convection cycle that allows continuous circulation of the heat transfer fluid, ensuring uninterrupted passive heat removal. [0085] The system eliminates the need for mechanical components such as fans, pumps, or blowers, thus minimizing the chances of mechanical failure, reducing maintenance, and enhancing system durability. [0086] The present disclosure enables temperature regulation within a safe operational range (20°C to 45°C) during fast charging or discharging, thereby preventing overheating and significantly reducing the likelihood of thermal runaway or battery damage. [0087] The system is compact, modular, and lightweight, allowing easy integration into existing EV battery architectures without significant changes to the overall design or space requirements. [0088] By maintaining thermal uniformity and eliminating temperature hotspots, the invention contributes to increased battery efficiency, longer service life, and consistent performance under varied operational conditions. [0089] The use of thermally conductive materials such as copper or aluminium for the capillary tubes, in conjunction with a specially selected heat transfer fluid having high thermal conductivity and specific heat, ensures a robust and high-performance thermal management system. [0090] The system is scalable and adaptable to a wide range of battery pack configurations, sizes, and applications, making it suitable for both commercial and high-performance electric vehicles. , Claims:1. patents.abstract: TITLE: PATTERNED LASER ABLATION OF LITHIUM IRON PHOSPHATE CATHODES FOR ENHANCED ELECTROCHEMICAL ENERGY STORAGE DEVICE PERFORMANCE A laser micro-texturing method for lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) cathode films is presented as shown in figure-1, using a pulsed nanosecond Nd:YAG laser to create precise linear and grid micro-channel patterns. Optimized laser parameters enable controlled surface modification with minimal thermal damage. Electrochemical testing in coin cells shows that textured electrodes, especially grid-patterned ones, exhibit enhanced lithium-ion transport, higher capacity, improved voltage stability, and better cycling performance compared to untextured cathodes. This method offers an effective approach to improve the performance of LiFePO₄-based lithium-ion batteries.
patents.complete_specification: Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION [0001] The present invention is related to a method for laser micro-texturing lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) cathode films more particularly to create precise micro-channel patterns to enhance electrochemical performance in lithium-ion batteries. BACKGROUND [0002] Laser micro-texturing of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode films has evolved as a cutting-edge technique to enhance the electrochemical performance of lithium-ion batteries. Initially, nanosecond laser annealing was used to modify the surface morphology of LFP films, effectively removing binder materials like polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) and creating micro-grooves and surface roughness that improve contact between the active material and the current collector. Over time, researchers have optimized laser parameters such as pulse duration, energy intensity, and scanning strategies to enhance mechanical adhesion and reduce stress at the electrode interface, thereby improving battery cycle life. Additionally, laser processing has been found to influence the microstructure of LFP films, enhancing their crystallinity and porosity, which translates to better ionic conductivity and overall battery efficiency. However, precise control is essential to avoid material degradation or unwanted phase changes. As this technology continues to develop, laser micro-texturing shows great promise for scalable manufacturing, allowing for tailored cathode surfaces that improve charge-discharge rates, cycle stability, and long-term battery performance. Despite challenges such as optimizing process uniformity and preventing damage, laser micro-texturing remains a highly promising approach to advancing lithium-ion battery technology. [0003] The existing invention discloses an electrochemical energy storage device, comprising first half cell having a cathode, second half cell having one anode, and one electrode electrolyte being adapted for providing an ion conducting path between the two half-cells, wherein the anode comprises an anode active material selected from Ce1-xMxO2, wherein M is one metal and 0.01 ≤ x ≤ 0.25. The doping of ceria CeO2 by the metal M has a highly beneficial impact on the potential use of ceria as the active material for lithium-ion and sodium-ion batteries and allows for capacity increases by a factor of two to three compared to non-doped ceria. [0004] Furthermore, the other invention discloses cathode material comprising particles having a lithium metal phosphate core and a pyrolytic carbon deposit, said particles having a synthetic multimodal particle size distribution comprising fraction of micron size particles and one fraction of submicron size particles, said lithium metal phosphate having formula LiMPO4 wherein M is at least Fe or Mn. Said material is prepared by method comprising the steps of providing starting micron sized particles and starting submicron sized particles of lithium metal phosphate or of precursors of a lithium metal phosphate; mixing by mechanical means said starting particles; making a pyrolytic carbon deposit on the lithium metal phosphate starting particles before or after the mixing step, and on their metal precursor before or after mixing the particles; optionally adding carbon black, graphite powder or fibers to the said lithium metal phosphate particles before the mechanical mixing. [0005] The existing inventions have limitations: focuses primarily on improving cathode and anode materials through compositional modifications such as doping ceria anodes or applying pyrolytic carbon coatings on lithium metal phosphate particles with specific particle size distributions. However, these approaches do not address the microstructural optimization of electrode surfaces. Specifically, there is no disclosure of techniques for precise surface micro-texturing or patterning that can enhance lithium-ion diffusion and electrochemical kinetics. The absence of controlled surface morphology modification, such as laser-induced micro-channel formation, limits the ability to improve ion transport pathways and electrode-electrolyte interactions, resulting in comparatively lower capacity retention, cycling stability, and overall battery performance. Hence a laser micro-texturing method has been proposed in the present invention that enables the creation of finely controlled linear and grid patterns on lithium iron phosphate cathode films, significantly enhancing their electrochemical properties by increasing surface area and facilitating more efficient charge transfer. SUMMARY [0006] A method for laser micro-texturing lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode films is presented, involving a film composed of 88% LFP, 6% conductive carbon, and 4% PVDF binder coated onto a 16 µm aluminum substrate, with a total thickness of 70 µm. [0007] Using a pulsed nanosecond Nd:YAG laser at 266 nm wavelength and 10 Hz repetition rate, precise surface textures comprising linear and grid-shaped micro-channels (width ~216 µm, depth 30–42.5 µm) are created by scanning the laser over the film with controlled overlaps. [0008] The grid pattern features orthogonally intersecting channels spaced approximately 2.9 mm apart, with optimized laser parameters minimizing thermal damage and ensuring sharp edges. [0009] Electrochemical evaluation in CR2032 coin cells demonstrates that laser texturing significantly enhances performance compared to untextured electrodes. Line-patterned electrodes with 0% overlap maintain stable cycling with ~160 mAh/g capacity, while 50% overlap shows moderate capacity decline. [0010] Grid-patterned electrodes exhibit superior performance with higher specific capacity (~165 mAh/g), extended and symmetric charge-discharge plateaus, and minimal capacity fading, attributed to enhanced ion transport and active material utilization. [0011] Overall, surface texturing improves lithium-ion diffusion and charge storage, with overlap degree showing limited impact under slow cycling (0.1C). The grid architecture enables longer cycle life and better electrochemical stability, emphasizing the importance of engineered surface morphologies in optimizing battery electrode performance. OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION [0012] The main objective of the proposed invention is to develop a laser micro-texturing method for lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode films by creating precise linear and grid micro-channel patterns using a pulsed nanosecond Nd:YAG laser. [0013] It seeks to optimize laser parameters to produce well-defined surface textures with minimal damage and consistent features. The research evaluates how these patterns influence cathode morphology and electrochemical performance in coin cells, focusing on capacity, voltage stability, and cycling durability. [0014] The goal is to understand the impact of surface architecture on lithium-ion transport and demonstrate the superior performance of grid-patterned electrodes over line-patterned and untextured ones under low current conditions. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS [0015] Figure 1. illustrates the battery run time for textured and untextured electrodes. [0016] Figure 2. illustrates the galvanostatic charge discharge curves or textured and untextured electrodes. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION: [0017] A method for laser micro-texturing a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) or (LiFePO₄) cathode film, has been proposed in the present invention. The proposed invention comprises Step-1: a cathode electrode, a nanosecond pulsed Nd:YAG laser, a plano convex lens and a motorized translational stage. The proposed invention is characterized in that: step-2: the cathode electrode in step-1 comprises a lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) active material. The cathode electrode surface is irradiated with a nanosecond pulsed Nd:YAG laser in step-1 operating at a defined wavelength and pulse repetition. The pulsed laser is a nanosecond Nd:YAG laser operating at a wavelength of 266 nm and a repetition rate of 10 Hz. [0018] The laser pulse energy is optimized in the range 10 mJ to 20 mJ to achieve maximum ablation depth without plasma shielding and the high-energy pulsed laser wavelength ranges from 200 nm to 1200 nm and the pulse repetition rate between 1Hz and 1 MHz. The electrode of laser-textured line patterns has charge plateaus in the range 3.5 V to 4.0 V and discharge plateaus in the range 3.8 V to 3.2 V showing better charge retention. Step-3: a focused pulsed laser beam is directed onto the surface of the cathode electrode using the plano convex lens in step-1 to form a laser textured lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) cathode electrode. [0019] The relative movement between the pulsed laser beam and the cathode electrode is controlled using the motorized translational stage generates a surface texture on the laser textured lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) cathode electrode. The laser pulse overlap is controlled between 0% and 50% to adjust the surface texture density and uniformity. The surface texture of the laser textured lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) cathode electrode comprises linear textures and grid textures micro-channels. The surface modification forms micro-or nano-scale textures that are chosen from grooves ridges dimples and porous patterns. Step-3: The surface patterns comprise linear and grid micro-channel structures on the laser textured lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) cathode film surface. [0020] The cathode film or cathode textured surface roughness (Ra) of 50 nm to 5 µm allows for better electrolyte interaction. The linear micro-channels have a depth of about 41 µm defined by controlled overlap of adjacent laser passes. The line-patterned have widths of laser-etched grooves are around 216 µm and depths of around 30 µm. The overlap between adjacent laser passes is controlled to modulate surface roughness and structural integrity and overlap generates continuous surface modifications with cycling stability maintained at 0.1C. The grid pattern is formed by scanning the laser beam in two orthogonal directions with inter-step spacing greater than 2.5 mm in horizontal and vertical directions and exhibits an efficient specific capacity of over 165 mAh/g across many cycles. The grid intersection channels have ablation depths of 15 µm to 45 µm to maximize ion transport efficiency. [0021] Step-4: the linear textures are formed by the laser texturing over the surface on the laser textured lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) cathode electrode. The grid structures in step-3 are formed by scanning the laser beam orthogonally over the surface of the laser textured lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) cathode electrode. The micro-channels have ablation depths of 15 µm to 45 µm to enhance ion transport efficiency. The laser parameters are optimized to reduce thermal effects and to produce uniform micro-channels. The laser parameters are fluence and pulse energy. Step-5: the lithium-ion battery comprises the laser-textured lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) cathode electrode, a lithium metal anode, a glass fiber separator, a lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF₆) electrolyte, an argon-filled glovebox to evaluate the lifespan and electrochemical performance. [0022] A method for fabricating the electrochemical energy storage device or lithium-ion battery to evaluate the lifespan and electrochemical performance using the laser textured and untextured lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄) cathodes as shown in figure-1, comprise a 16 mm diameter electrochemical energy storage device in claim-1 casing. The laser-textured LiFePO₄ cathode film in step-3, the lithium metal anode which is a untextured lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO₄), the glass fiber separator having a thickness of about 680 µm, and the lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF₆) electrolyte in a volume of about 100 µL in step-4. The electrochemical energy storage device casing is assembled inside the argon-filled glovebox. The assembled electrochemical energy storage device comprises the laser textured lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode film and lithium metal anode separated by the glass fiber separator. [0023] The lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF₆) electrolyte is inserted into the electrochemical energy storage device to enhance ionic conductivity and electrochemical activity. The life span of the electrochemical energy storage device life span is evaluated through a galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD) cycling and to enhance the electrochemical performance. The electrochemical energy storage device with: the line-textured in step-3 exhibits enhanced cycling stability and the grid-textured exhibited longer charge–discharge plateaus, higher retained capacity and reduced polarization, indicating an extended lifespan. [0024] The grid-patterned electrode shows voltage symmetry and low irreversible capacity loss during repeated cycling at low current rate selecting a pitch greater than 1 mm but not exceeding 3 mm ensures high electrochemical performance whereas larger pitches result in decreased capacity and compromised cycling performance. The grid-patterned architecture achieves higher energy density and efficiency of operation compared to line-patterned or untextured counterparts. The micro/nano-architectured cathode surface provides high cycling stability with moderate capacity fade after repeated galvanostatic discharge cycles. the laser-textured area shows slight uniform thickness of about 30 µm and has a consistent laser-material interaction. [0025] The resulting surface morphology can be tailored to influence surface roughness, structural integrity and the extent of material removal in a predictable and reproducible manner by adjusting the degree of overlap. Profilometric analysis of the line pattern reveals a transverse channel width, as measured laterally across the depression with the channel depth. The laser fluence and pulse energy are adjusted to reduce thermal impact and maintain edge sharpness of the micro-channel. The electrochemical energy storage device improvement constitutes a minimum of a 20% increase in cycle life of a non-textured battery tested under the same conditions. [0026] The grid pattern includes a first set of parallel linear channels and a second set of parallel linear channels oriented orthogonally to the first set. The laser-textured cathode of the grid-patterned architecture minimizes polarization and presents charge-discharge plateaus of longer duration compared to an untextured cathode. The laser-induced surface structure improves ion transport within the cathode, reduces polarization effects, and enhances the duration of the charge–discharge plateau relative to an untextured cathode. The laser-textured architecture achieves a specific capacity exceeding 165 mAh/g and improves cycle life by at least 20 % relative to an untextured electrode under identical cycling conditions. [0027] The bidirectional scanning enabled precise ablation at the intersecting points, resulting in a well-defined network of micro-channels. The laser parameters were optimized to achieve efficient material removal while minimizing thermal effects on the surrounding material. At the intersections of the scanning paths, overlapping laser pulses produced a maximum channel depth. Between intersections, the linear channels exhibited a uniform depth of about 41 μm with sharply defined edges, demonstrating consistent laser-material interaction and precise feature control. [0028] A method is provided for improving the electrochemical performance and extending the lifespan of a lithium-ion battery. The method comprises irradiating the surface of a cathode film with a high-energy pulsed laser having a wavelength in the range of 200 nm to 1200 nm, a pulse duration between 1 picosecond and 1 microsecond, a fluence between 0.1 J/cm² and 10 J/cm², and a repetition rate between 1 Hz and 1 MHz. The laser irradiation modifies the cathode surface to form micro-or nano-scale textures such as grooves, ridges, dimples, or porous patterns, which enhance ion transport and electronic conductivity while reducing material degradation during repeated charge–discharge cycles. [0029] The configuration enables a controlled comparison of the influence of surface texturing on the lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode performance under consistent testing conditions. The grid pattern in the battery has a pitch between 1 mm and 3 mm, thereby ensuring high electrochemical performance and minimized capacity fade. The cathode in the battery cell comprises a hybrid grid-and-line patterned surface architecture providing enhanced ion transport and uniform current distribution during high-rate cycling. A systematic investigation of galvanostatic charge-discharge (GCD) profiles was conducted to evaluate the electrochemical performance of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathodes with varying surface architectures namely, untextured, line-patterned, and grid-patterned configurations. [0030] The analysis focused on low current rates and minimal energy input conditions to isolate the influence of surface texturing on charge storage behaviour. Comparative evaluation of the GCD curves reveals distinct differences attributable to the microstructural modifications introduced by laser texturing. These differences provide insight into the advantages and trade-offs associated with each pattern type in terms of capacity retention, voltage stability, and rate capability. Based on cyclic voltammetry (CV) results, a stable operating voltage window of 3.0 to 4.0 V was established for both charging and discharging cycles. [0031] Galvanostatic charge–discharge (GCD) characterization was conducted on cathodes as shown in figure-2 exhibiting different surface textures—namely, untextured, line-patterned, and grid-patterned architectures to evaluate the influence of surface morphology on electrochemical behaviour. The tests were performed at low current rates within a voltage window determined from cyclic voltammetry analysis. Untextured electrodes demonstrated shorter charge–discharge durations, reduced plateau regions, lower initial specific capacity, and diminished reversibility, attributed to solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) layer formation. In contrast, line-patterned electrodes exhibited enhanced cycling stability with consistent capacity and well-defined charge–discharge plateaus. Variation in laser pulse overlap within the line patterns affected capacity retention and polarization, with higher overlap ratios leading to increased capacity fade during cycling. [0032] Grid-textured electrodes demonstrate superior electrochemical performance characterized by highly symmetric and extended charge–discharge plateaus, indicative of enhanced ion accessibility and increased specific capacity. The interconnected curvature of the grid architecture facilitates unobstructed ion transport pathways and reduces polarization, thereby improving cycling reversibility. Compared to untextured and line-textured electrodes, the grid-patterned configuration exhibits significantly improved capacity retention and long-term stability. Comparative analysis confirms that laser-induced surface texturing enhances electrochemical behaviour by increasing the effective surface area and providing additional ion diffusion routes. [0033] The grid architecture introduces supplementary diffusion networks that yield superior energy storage performance while line-patterned electrodes maintain stable and efficient cycling regardless of overlap ratio. Within the overlap range tested, no substantial variation in voltage profiles or overall electrochemical efficiency was observed under low-rate cycling, underscoring the robustness of the grid design. The extended charge–discharge plateaus and improved capacity retention of grid-textured electrodes result in prolonged operational lifetimes relative to other surface architectures. [0034] The broad workable ranges for key parameters in laser texturing of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathodes include laser parameters such as the laser type (fiber laser, Nd:YAG laser, or femtosecond laser), wavelength (500–1100 nm), pulse duration (100 femtoseconds to 100 nanoseconds), laser power (1–50 W), pulse repetition rate (1 kHz to 500 kHz), scan speed (10–2000 mm/s), spot size (10–200 µm), and pulse overlap ratio (10%–90%). Cathode material parameters encompass a composition of 70–90 wt% LiFePO₄, 5–15 wt% conductive additives like carbon black, 3–10 wt% binder such as PVDF, and coating thickness ranging from 20 to 150 µm. [0035] Laser texturing can be performed in various environments including ambient air, argon, or nitrogen atmospheres, with substrate temperatures from room temperature up to 100°C if pre-heating is applied. Post-processing and cell assembly parameters include drying temperatures between 80–120°C, pressing pressures of 50–300 MPa if applicable, use of common electrolytes like 1M LiPF₆ in EC: DMC (1:1), polyolefin-based separators such as Celgard, and cell configurations including CR2032 coin cells or pouch cells. These ranges are based on experimental data, literature precedents, and practical considerations for scalability, with optimization tailored to specific texture patterns, laser systems, and battery designs. [0036] A comparative analysis of the electrode configurations confirms that the untextured cathode serves as a baseline, exhibiting the lowest electrochemical performance. In contrast, both the line-patterned and grid-patterned electrodes demonstrate significant improvements, primarily due to increased surface area and enhanced ion transport mechanisms. The line pattern delivers stable and efficient charge–discharge behavior across both 0% and 50% overlap configurations, while the grid pattern offers additional interconnected diffusion pathways, further improving ion accessibility and capacity retention. [0037] These results emphasize the critical role of electrode surface architecture in optimizing the performance of lithium-ion energy storage systems. Under slow cycling conditions (0.1C), the degree of pattern overlap (0% vs. 50%) shows minimal influence on the voltage profile or overall electrochemical efficiency. Voltage versus specific capacity curves for both overlap conditions remain highly consistent across repeated cycles, indicating robust and stable cycling behaviour. This suggests that, within the tested range, overlap optimization is not a decisive factor for performance in practical low-rate applications, allowing for design flexibility in laser patterning strategies. [0038] The superior performance of the grid architecture is primarily due to its enhanced ion transport pathways and increased effective surface area. These characteristics promote more uniform utilization of the active material, reduce internal resistance, and facilitate more efficient charge storage. In contrast, the untextured electrode exhibits short cycle durations, low capacity, and poor voltage symmetry, reflecting limited electrochemical activity. While the line-patterned electrode offers moderate improvements in capacity and cycling stability, it does not match the performance of the grid structure in terms of energy delivery and overall efficiency. , C , Claims:Claims: I/We Claim: 1. patents.abstract: Title: A High-Capacity, Stable Anode Material for Lithium-Ion Battery An anode material for lithium-ion battery formed using Cu(NO3)2.3H2O, AgNO3, 5M NaOH and double distilled water to form Ag2Cu2O3 nanomaterial as the anode material. The anode material for lithium-ion battery, wherein the exhibits discharge capacity of 653 mAh g-1 after 1400 cycle at very high current density of 500 mA g-1. A process of synthesising the Ag2Cu2O3 anode material comprising; (101): preparing a deep blue color solution containing Cu(NO3)2.3H2O, AgNO3 and double distilled water (DDW); (102): stirring the solution for 30 minutes; (103): adding NaOH dropwise to the stirred solution; (104) stirring the resultant mixture to convert the blue solution to dark green precipitate; (105): sonicating and stirring the obtained precipitate; (106) washing and drying of the sample.
patents.complete_specification: Description:FIELD OF INVENTION [0001] Embodiment of present invention relates to the field of Physics, more particularly it relates to the development of Ag2Cu2O3 (anode) material for lithium-ion battery applications, 5 where the Ag2Cu2O3 nanomaterial prepared by co-precipitation method, and are highly stable nanomaterial for long cycles. RELATED ART [0002] Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) have revolutionized the energy storage landscape due to their high energy density, extended cycle life, low self-discharge, and environmental 10 compatibility. They are widely utilized in a variety of applications, including portable electronics, electric vehicles (EVs), and renewable energy integration. The growing global energy demand, depletion of fossil fuel reserves, and environmental issues such as greenhouse gas emissions and climate change have driven the need for sustainable, high-performance, and cost-effective energy storage technologies. Graphite is the most commonly used commercial 15 anode material in LIBs due to its low cost, structural stability, and long cycle life. [0003] The performance and commercial viability of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are heavily influenced by the nature of the electrode materials, particularly the anode. Traditional anode materials such as graphite are constrained by a low theoretical capacity (~ 372 mAh g-1), limited rate performance, and structural instability under high cycling rates, which restrict their use in 20 high-energy and long-life applications such as electric vehicles and grid-scale storage systems. To address these limitations, significant research efforts have focused on transition metal oxides (TMOs) as alternative anode materials due to their higher theoretical capacities and diverse redox activity. However, many TMOs suffer from issues such as volume expansion, structural degradation, and poor long – term cyclic stability, which hinder their practical 25 application. [0004] Thus the present invention addresses this gap by providing a facile synthesis method for Ag2Cu2O3 (anode) material nanorods and demonstrating their superior performance as long-life, high-capacity anodes for advanced lithium – ion battery applications. 30 3 SUMMARY [0005] An anode material for lithium-ion battery formed using Cu(NO3)2.3H2O, AgNO3, 5M NaOH and double distilled water to form Ag2Cu2O3 nanomaterial as the anode material. The anode material for lithium-ion battery, wherein the exhibits discharge capacity of 653 mAh g-1 after 1400 cycle at very high current density of 500 mA g-1. 5 [0006] A process of synthesising the Ag2Cu2O3 anode material comprising; (101): preparing a deep blue color solution containing Cu(NO3)2.3H2O, AgNO3 and double distilled water (DDW); (102): stirring the solution for 30 minutes; (103): adding NaOH dropwise to the stirred solution; (104) stirring the resultant mixture to convert the blue solution to dark green precipitate; (105): sonicating and stirring the obtained precipitate; (106) washing and drying of 10 the sample. [0007] The process of synthesising the Ag2Cu2O3 anode material further comprising; preparing a deep blue color solution containing 0.7248g Cu(NO3)2.3H2O, 0.5096g AgNO3 and 5ml of double distilled water (DDW); stirring the solution for 30 minutes; adding 40ml NaOH (5M) dropwise to the stirred solution; stirring the resultant mixture around 600 rpm for 30 minutes 15 to convert the blue solution to dark green precipitate; sonicating for 3 hours and stirring for 21 hours the obtained precipitate; and washing with double distilled water for 8 – 10 times and drying for 16 to 18 hours at 50°C of the sample. [0008] Several aspects are described below, concerning diagrams. It should be understood that numerous specific details, relationships and methods are set forth to provide a complete 20 understanding of the present disclosure. Skilled personnel in the relevant art, however, will readily recognize that the present disclosure can be practiced without one or more of the specific details or with other methods etc. In other instances, well known structures or the operations are not shown in detail to avoid obscuring the details of the present disclosure. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF DRAWINGS 25 [0009] FIG.1 illustrates the process of synthesising the Ag2Cu2O3 anode material [0010] FIG.2 illustrates the XRD patterns of Ag2Cu2O3 of WS – ACO, 3HS – ACO and ACO – 3HS) nanomaterials. [0011] FIG.3 illustrates the FESEM image of Ag2Cu2O3; a) WS – ACO, b) 3HS – ACO and c) ACO – 3HS nanomaterials. 30 [0012] FIG.4 illustrates the HRTEM image of Ag2Cu2O3 (ACO – 3HS) nanomaterials. 4 [0013] FIG.5 illustrates the BET analysis of Ag2Cu2O3 (WS – ACO, 3HS – ACO & ACO – 3HS) nanomaterials. [0014] FIG.6 illustrates the; a) electrode preparation and b) cell fabrication using ACO – 3HS nanomaterial. [0015] FIG.7 illustrates the; a) Five cycles GCD curves, b) rate capability and c) long-term 5 cyclic stability graph of ACO – 3HS nanomaterial. [0016] FIG.8 illustrates the; a) CV and b) EIS curves of ACO – 3HS nanomaterial. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF PREFERRED EXAMPLES [0017] The present invention relates to a novel anode active material for lithium-ion batteries, comprising nanostructured Ag2Cu2O3 synthesized through a facile co-precipitation method, 10 producing high-performance anode materials with excellent electrochemical stability and long cycle life. [0018] The process of synthesising the Ag2Cu2O3 anode material comprising the steps of; (101): preparing a deep blue colour solution containing Cu(NO3)2.3H2O, AgNO3 and double distilled water (DDW); (102): stirring the solution for 30 minutes; (103): addition of NaOH 15 dropwise to the stirred solution; (104) stirring the resultant mixture to convert the blue solution to dark green precipitate; (105): sonicating and stirring the obtained precipitate; (106) washing and drying of the sample. [0019] Ag2Cu2O3 nanomaterials are synthesised through three different routes and are named accordingly as WS – ACO, 3HS – ACO and ACO – 3HS nanomaterials. The detailed synthesis 20 process of said nanomaterials are described in the following paragraphs. [0020] In an embodiment WS – ACO nanomaterial is synthesised and is as described; a deep blue solution emerged upon the slow, steady addition of 0.7248 g (or 3 mmol) Copper (Ⅱ) nitrate trihydrate [Cu(NO3)2.3H2O] and 0.5096 g (or 3 mmol) silver nitrate [AgNO3] in a beaker containing 5 ml of double distilled water (DDW), after which stirring for 30 minutes; thereafter, 25 the blue aqueous solution is converted into dark green precipitate form after the addition of 40 ml of sodium hydroxide [NaOH] (5M) dropwise and continuously stirred the entire solution around 600 rpm for 24 hours. The obtained precipitate is washed 8 – 10 times with double distilled water (DDW), followed by drying for 16 – 18 hours at 50°C, and after that sample is collected. 30 [0021] In another embodiment 3HS – ACO nanomaterial is synthesised and is as described; a deep blue solution emerged upon the slow, steady addition of 0.7248 g (or 3 mmol) Cu(NO3)2.3H2O and 0.5096 g (or 3 mmol) AgNO3 in a beaker containing 5 ml of double 5 distilled water (DDW), after which stirring for 30 minutes; thereafter, the blue aqueous solution is converted into dark green precipitate form after the addition of 40 ml of NaOH (5M) dropwise and continuously stirred the entire solution around 600 rpm for 30 minutes and then sonicated for 3 hours and then again stirred for 21 hours. The obtained precipitate is washed 8 – 10 times with double distilled water (DDW), followed by drying for 16 – 18 hours at 50°C, 5 and after that sample is collected. [0022] In certain another embodiment ACO – 3HS nanomaterial is synthesised as follows, a deep blue solution emerged upon the slow, steady addition of 0.7248 g (or 3 mmol) Cu(NO3)2.3H2O and 0.5096 g (or 3 mmol) AgNO3 in a beaker containing 5 ml of double distilled water (DDW), after which stirring for 30 minutes; thereafter, the blue aqueous solution 10 is converted into dark green precipitate form after the addition of 40 ml of NaOH (5M) dropwise and continuously stirred the entire solution around 600 rpm for 20 hours and then sonicated for 3 hours and then again stirred for 1 hour. The obtained precipitate is washed 8 – 10 times with double distilled water (DDW), followed by drying for 16 – 18 hours at 50° C, and after that sample is collected. 15 [0023] Various benefits and performance studies of three different routes of Ag2Cu2O3 nanomaterial are presented in the following paragraphs. [0024] X-ray Diffraction is a non-destructive analytical technique used to identify the crystalline structure of a sample by bombarding it with X-rays and analyzing the resulting diffraction pattern. X-ray diffraction (XRD) technique utilized to confirm the phase of all 20 prepared samples (WS – ACO, 3HS – ACO & ACO – 3HS). The phase of all samples well matched with JCPDS card no. 01–089–6378. The materials have tetragonal crystal system with space group of I41/amd and lattice parameters of a = b = 5.8857 Å, c = 10.6868 Å. The identified planes are (101), (103), (004), (202), (220), (224), (206), (400), (008), (422), and (228) as depicted in the FIG.2. 25 [0025] The morphological analysis of all samples is investigated via Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FESEM) technique as shown in the FIG.3. The figure 3(a) for WS – ACO, shows material have uniform nanorods morphology and figure 3(b) for 3HS – ACO, shows materials have uneven morphology, whereas figure 3(c) for ACO – 3HS, shows uniform nanorods base with nanoscale protrusions like morphology. 30 [0026] The High-Resolution Transmission Electron Microscopy (HRTEM) analysis reveals fine structural & morphological details of the nanomaterials. In HRTEM image, the observed morphology of ACO – 3HS, is nanorod with secondary nanoscale protrusions. The consistency 6 of morphology in HRTEM images is well agrees with FESEM results. FIG.4 shows the HRTEM image of Ag2Cu2O3 (ACO – 3HS) nanomaterials. [0027] The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) analysis utilized to evaluate the specific surface area (SSA) all samples via N2 adsorption–desorption isotherms. The specific surface area of ACO – 3HS is 7.06 m2 g-1 (highest) while for WS – ACO and 3HS – ACO is 5.10 m2 g-1 and 5 1.94 m2 g-1 respectively. Higher SSA, better electrode–electrolyte interaction & enhanced electrochemical performance. FIG.5 represents the BET analysis of Ag2Cu2O3 (WS – ACO, 3HS – ACO & ACO – 3HS) nanomaterials. [0028] Among the three routes of nanomaterials, ACO – 3HS nanomaterial showed best results and is used for electrode preparation and cell fabrication, explained in the following 10 paragraphs. [0029] Slurry is prepared by using synthesised anode material, carbon black, and PVDF (70:20:10) in N-Methyl-2-pyrrolidone (NMP). Slurry is coated on Cu foil via doctor blade; dried at 120 °C for 12 h under vacuum. Assembled CR2032 coin cells in Ar-filled glove box (MBRAUN). Employed 16 mm Li metal foil as counter/reference electrode, Whatman filter as 15 separator and 1 M LiPF6 in EC: DMC (1: 1 v/v) as electrolyte. FIG.6 illustrates the a) electrode preparation and b) cell fabrication using ACO – 3HS nanomaterial. [0030] FIG.7 (a) shows the five-cycle discharge capacity curve of ACO – 3HS, in which initial specific discharge capacity is observed of 804 mAh g-1 at 100 mA g-1 current density. FIG.7 (b) shows the rate capabilities of WS – ACO, 3HS – ACO & ACO – 3HS nanomaterials at 20 different current densities. From curve it is clear that the ACO – 3HS nanomaterial showing excellent rate capability in compared to other prepared samples. FIG.7(c) shows the cyclic stabilities of all samples, in which ACO – 3HS nanomaterials showing outstanding cyclic stability performance, after 1400 cycles the ACO – 3HS shows highest discharge capacity of 653 mAh g-1 at very high current density of 500 mA g-1, while WS – ACO have 341 mAh g-1 25 and 3HS – ACO have 228 mAh g-1. [0031] FIG.8 (a) shows the cyclic voltammetry (CV) curve of ACO – 3HS nanomaterial, the CV is performed within 0.01 – 3.0 V voltage range with scan rate 0.5 mV s-1. First cycle, four cathodic (reduction) peaks is observed at ~ 1.35 V, ~ 0.58 V, ~2.09 V, and ~0.95 V and three anodic (oxidation) peaks is observed at ~1.14 V, ~1.54 V and ~2.44 V. FIG. 8(b) shows the 30 electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) of all samples. The ACO – 3HS nanomaterial small semicircle correspondingly lowest charge transfer resistance (Rct = 57.76 Ω) and followed by higher conductivity and hence excellent performance for battery. 7 [0032] The above described ACO – 3HS nanomaterial may be applicable as an advanced anode material in lithium-ion batteries used in electric cars, scooters, buses, and hybrid vehicles due to its high specific capacity and long cycle life. Also it is suitable for grid-scale and residential energy storage systems integrated with solar and wind energy, owing to the material’s stability over extended cycling. 5 [0033] While various embodiments of the present disclosure have been described above, it should be understood that they have been presented by example only and not by limitation. Thus, the breadth and scope of the present disclosure should not be limited by any of the above discussed embodiments but should be defined only by the following claims and their equivalents. , Claims:I/We claim, 1. A process of synthesising the Ag2Cu2O3 anode material of claim 1 comprising; (101): preparing a deep blue color solution containing Cu(NO3)2.3H2O, AgNO3 and double distilled water (DDW); (102): stirring the solution for 30 minutes; (103): adding NaOH dropwise to the stirred solution; (104) stirring the resultant mixture to convert the blue solution to dark green precipitate; (105): sonicating and stirring the obtained precipitate; (106) washing and drying of the sample. 4. The process of synthesising the Ag2Cu2O3 anode material of claim 3 further comprising; preparing a deep blue color solution containing 0.7248g Cu(NO3)2.3H2O, 0.5096g AgNO3 and 5ml of double distilled water (DDW); stirring the solution for 30 minutes; adding 40ml NaOH (5M) dropwise to the stirred solution; stirring the resultant mixture around 600 rpm for 30 minutes to convert the blue solution to dark green precipitate; sonicating for 3 hours and stirring for 21 hours the obtained precipitate; and washing with double distilled water for 8 – 10 times and drying for 16 to 18 hours at 50° C of the sample. 5. Method, system and apparatus providing one or more features as described in the paragraphs of this specification.

patents.abstract: The Advanced Battery Management System For Safe Operation Of Lithium-Ion Cells Us With Relay Control And Cooling Fan Regulation is designed to monitor and protect lithium-ion batteries used in portable and renewable energy applications. The system consists of three lithium-ion batteries connected through five relays—three for battery switching, one for temperature monitoring, and one for cooling control. It uses three voltage sensors, a current sensor, and a temperature sensor to continuously measure the key parameters of the batteries. Two DC-DC buck converters are used to regulate voltage for different circuit sections. The Smart Shield BMS ensures safe charging and discharging operations by preventing overvoltage, overcurrent, and overheating conditions. This project aims to provide a cost-effective and reliable solution for multi­battery management and improve the overall efficiency, safety, and lifespan of lithium-ion battery system
patents.complete_specification: The Advanced Battery Management System For Safe Operation Of Lithium-Ion Cells With Relay Control And Cooling Fan Regulation is developed to ensure the safe and efficient operation of lithium-ion batteries used in various electronic and energy storage applications. As lithium-ion batteries are sensitive to voltage, current, and temperature variations, proper monitoring and control are essential to maintain their performance and longevity. This project focuses on designing a system that continuously monitors battery parameters such as voltage, current, and temperature, and provides automatic protection against faults like overcharging, overcurrent, and overheating. By integrating sensors, relays, and DC-DC converters, the Smart Shield BMS offers an intelligent, affordable, and reliable solution for modern power management needs The Advanced Battery Management System For Safe Operation Of Lithium-Ion Cells Using With Relay Control And Cooling Fan Regulation is designed to monitor and protect three lithium-ion batteries using voltage, current, and temperature sensors for efficient power management. It employs five relays for battery switching, temperature monitoring, and automatic cooling control through a CPU fan. Two DC-DC buck converters are used to maintain stable voltage levels for different circuit sections. The system continuously checks battery parameters to detect abnormal conditions such as overvoltage, overcurrent, or overheating, and automatically activates protective measures to prevent damage. The Smart Shield BMS not only ensures safe charging and discharging but also improves energy efficiency and battery lifespan. Its compact design, automation, and low cost make it a reliable solution for renewable energy systems, electric vehicles, and portable electronic applications. 1. Efficient monitoring of multiple lithium-ion batteries using voltage, current, and temperature sensors. 2. Automatic relay and cooling fan control for protection against faults. 3. Cost-effective and reliable solution for improved battery performance and lifespan.
