patents.abstract: A continuous leaching apparatus (102) for recovering metals from lithium-ion battery black mass. The apparatus (102) includes a series of at least two continuous stirred tank reactors (104) arranged in fluid communication, enabling sequential black mass slurry transfer. A feed inlet (202) introduces the black mass slurry into a first reactor (104A), while a lixiviant supply unit (204) introduces fresh lixiviant into a final reactor (104N). Each of the at least two CSTR (104) is equipped with a plurality of sensors (106) connected to a control unit (108). The control unit (108) is configured to monitor and regulate parameters. A reagent dosing unit (112) meters at least one of a reductant or an oxidant into the at least one reactor (104) based on data received from the control unit (108). A solid-liquid separation unit (110) is positioned downstream of the final reactor (104N) separates pregnant leach solution from solid residue. FIG. 1
patents.complete_specification: Description:TECHNICAL FIELD The present disclosure relates to a field of battery recycling technology. Moreover, the present disclosure relates to a continuous leaching apparatus and a method for recovering metals from lithium-ion battery black mass. BACKGROUND Lithium-ion batteries have wide range of applications including smartwatches, mobile phones, electric vehicles, and the like, due to various characteristics, such as high energy density, very low self-discharge rate, low maintenance, availability in various sizes and a prolonged lifespan. Due to an increase in the usage of lithium-ion batteries, the requirement of recycling is increased. However, the recycling of the lithium-ion batteries raises environmental concerns, such as improper recycling, improper separation of metals, availability of limited recycling resources, and the like. Recycling of the lithium-ion batteries involves various operations, but leaching acts as one of the major operations, which involves dissolving valuable metals from a battery's cathode into a liquid solution, typically an acid, in order to extract metals from the lithium-ion batteries. Conventional leaching methods and systems that are used for recycling includes a separate unit configured to perform leaching operations, which is controlled manually or in batch mode. Moreover, such conventional leaching methods and systems, have limited operational efficiency and scalability. For example, each batch cycle lasts between six to ten hours, resulting in reduced overall productivity and efficiency of the recycling plant. Additionally, such conventional leaching methods and systems exhibit poor adaptability to feed variability, resulting in fluctuating reagent requirements and inconsistent leaching kinetics, which adversely affects the overall stability and efficiency of the recycling plant. Thus, there exists a technical problem of how to recover metals from the lithium-ion battery black mass with reduced overall time consumption. Therefore, in light of the foregoing discussion, there exists a need to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks associated with the conventional leaching apparatuses and conventional methods for recovering metals from the lithium-ion battery black mass. SUMMARY The present disclosure provides a continuous leaching apparatus and a method for recovering metals from the lithium-ion battery black mass. The present disclosure provides a solution to a technical problem of how to recover metals from the lithium-ion battery black mass with reduced overall time consumption. An aim of the present disclosure is to provide a solution that overcomes at least partially the problems encountered in the prior art and provide an improved leaching apparatus and a method for recovering metals from black mass of the spent lithium-ion batteries. One or more objectives of the present disclosure are achieved by the solutions provided in the enclosed independent claims. Advantageous implementations of the present disclosure are further defined in the dependent claims. In one aspect, the present disclosure provides a continuous leaching apparatus for recovering metals from lithium-ion battery black mass. The continuous leaching apparatus includes a series of at least two continuous stirred tank reactors (CSTRs) arranged in fluid communication. The continuous leaching apparatus further includes a feed inlet configured to add black mass slurry into a first reactor of the series, a lixiviant supply unit configured to introduce fresh lixiviant into a final reactor of the series, and a control unit configured to monitor and regulate predetermined parameters in each reactor. Furthermore, the continuous leaching apparatus includes a solid-liquid separation unit positioned downstream of the final reactor. The solid-liquid separation unit is configured to separate pregnant leach solution (PLS) from solid residue and a reagent dosing unit configured to meter at least one of a reductant or an oxidant into at least one reactor based on data received from the control unit. Advantageously, the continuous leaching apparatus allows continuous leaching operation while maintaining controlled chemical conditions, such as by ensuring uninterrupted and continuous leaching operation in the series of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors. As a result, the series of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors, reduces the time consumption. Further, the continuous leaching apparatus is used to recover metals from the lithium-ion battery black mass with controlled residence time, and steady redox and temperature conditions. In another aspect, the present disclosure provides a continuous method for recovering metals from lithium-ion battery black mass. The method comprising introducing black mass slurry into a first reactor of a series of at least two continuous stirred tank reactors (CSTRs) arranged in fluid communication, introducing fresh lixiviant into a final reactor of the series, continuously monitoring predetermined parameters in each reactor using a plurality of sensors, and automatically regulating the predetermined parameters in each reactor based on data from the plurality of sensors. Furthermore, the method comprises metering at least one of a reductant or an oxidant into at least one reactor based on the monitored predetermined parameters, transferring slurry sequentially through the series of reactors to achieve progressive leaching of metals from the black mass, separating pregnant leach solution (PLS) containing dissolved metals from solid residue downstream of the final reactor, and recovering the PLS for further metal extraction processing. The continuous method for recovering metals from the lithium-ion battery black mass achieves all the advantages and technical effects of the continuous leaching apparatus of the present disclosure. It is to be appreciated that all the aforementioned implementation forms can be combined. All steps which are performed by the various entities described in the present application as well as the functionalities described to be performed by the various entities are intended to mean that the respective entity is adapted to or configured to perform the respective steps and functionalities. It will be appreciated that features of the present disclosure are susceptible to being combined in various combinations without departing from the scope of the present disclosure as defined by the appended claims. Additional aspects, advantages, features, and objects of the present disclosure would be made apparent from the drawings and the detailed description of the illustrative implementations construed in conjunction with the appended claims that follow. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS The summary above, as well as the following detailed description of illustrative embodiments, is better understood when read in conjunction with the appended drawings. For the purpose of illustrating the present disclosure, exemplary constructions of the disclosure are shown in the drawings. However, the present disclosure is not limited to specific methods and instrumentalities disclosed herein. Moreover, those skilled in the art will understand that the drawings are not to scale. Wherever possible, like elements have been indicated by identical numbers. Embodiments of the present disclosure will now be described, by way of example only, with reference to the following diagrams wherein: FIG. 1 is a block diagram illustrating a continuous leaching apparatus for recovering metals from lithium-ion battery black mass, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure; FIG. 2 is an exemplary diagram of the continuous leaching apparatus comprising a plurality of continuous stirred tank reactors for recovering metals from lithium-ion battery black mass, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure; FIG. 3 is a diagram of a first continuous stirred tank reactor of the plurality of continuous stirred tank reactors of the continuous leaching apparatus, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure; and FIG. 4 is a flowchart depicting a method for recovering metals from lithium-ion battery black mass, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF EMBODIMENTS The following detailed description illustrates embodiments of the present disclosure and ways in which they can be implemented. Although some modes of carrying out the present disclosure have been disclosed, those skilled in the art would recognize that other embodiments for carrying out or practising the present disclosure are also possible. FIG. 1 is a block diagram illustrating a continuous leaching apparatus for recovering metals from lithium-ion battery black mass, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. With reference to FIG. 1, there is shown a block diagram 100 of the continuous leaching apparatus 102, which includes a series of at least two continuous stirred tank reactors (CSTRs) 104 arranged in fluid communication, a solid-liquid separation unit 110, a reagent dosing unit 112, and a control unit 108. The series of at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104 allows sequential transfer of black mass slurry from one continuous stirred tank reactor to another continuous stirred tank reactor. The black mass slurry refers to a mixture of cathode material from spent lithium-ion batteries suspended in aqueous medium, having particle size of 5-200 µm and solid-to-liquid ratio of 80-200 g/L. For example, the black mass slurry is transferred from a first continuous stirred tank reactor 104A to a second continuous stirred tank reactor 104B. Moreover, the fluid communication may be through piping, channels, or the likes, to allow the fluid to transfer from one continuous stirred tank reactor to another continuous stirred tank reactor while maintaining fluid isolation allowing independent control of operating conditions in each of the series of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104. In an example, each of the continuous stirred tank reactor 104 is an agitated reactor that receives continuous feed input and provides continuous discharge output. It should be noted that the number of continuous stirred tank reactors may vary depending upon different application attributes. In an implementation, the continuous leaching apparatus 102 includes three continuous stirred tank reactors 104. In another implementation, the continuous leaching apparatus 102 includes four continuous stirred tank reactors 104. In yet another implementation, the continuous leaching apparatus 102 includes five continuous stirred tank reactors 104. The control unit 108 refers to a computational element that is configured to monitor and regulate predetermined parameters in each of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104. Examples of the control unit 108 may include but are not limited to, a hardware processor, a digital signal processor (DSP), a microprocessor, a microcontroller, a complex instruction set computing (CISC) processor, an application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) processor, a reduced instruction set (RISC) processor, a very long instruction word (VLIW) processor, a state machine, a data processing unit, a graphics processing unit (GPU), and other processors or control circuitry. The solid-liquid separation unit 110 refers to a processing component configured to separate the pregnant leach solution (PLS) containing dissolved metal ions from the solid residue remaining after leaching. For example, the solid-liquid separation unit 110 includes at least one separation device selected from the group consisting of a thickener, a filter press, a centrifuge, a vacuum filter, and a hydrocyclone. The reagent dosing unit 112 refers to a controlled metering system configured to introduce precise quantities of chemical reagents, such as oxidants, reductants, into the at the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104. The reagent dosing unit 112 operates in coordination with the control system, receiving input signals from the plurality of sensors 106 that monitor parameters such as pH, oxidation-reduction potential (ORP), and temperature within each of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104. There is provided the continuous leaching apparatus 102 for recovering metals from lithium-ion battery black mass. The continuous leaching apparatus 102 is configured to enable continuous operation and eliminate the need for batch-based leaching processes used in conventional leaching apparatus. As a result, the continuous leaching apparatus 102 reduces overall time consumption for recovering metals from the lithium-ion battery black mass. Furthermore, the continuous leaching apparatus 102 includes a series of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors (CSTRs) 104 arranged in fluid communication. The arrangement allows sequential transfer of black mass slurry from first continuous stirred tank reactor 104A to a second continuous stirred tank reactor 104B. In an implementation, a series of three continuous stirred tank reactors 104 may be arranged in fluid communication. In an implementation, each of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104 includes a heating jacket or internal heating coils configured to maintain a desired temperature, and an agitation mechanism configured to maintain uniform suspension of solid particles. Furthermore, the continuous leaching apparatus 102 includes a feed inlet 202 configured to add black mass slurry into a first reactor 104A of the series. In other words, the feed inlet 202 allows the black mass slurry to enter into the first reactor 104A. The feed inlet 202 at the first reactor 104A allows independent control of concentration of the black mass slurry into the continuous leaching apparatus 102. In an implementation, the feed inlet 202 may be configured to receive the black mass slurry from a slurry reservoir (not shown) positioned upstream of the first reactor 104A. Subsequently, the lixiviant flows from the final reactor 104N towards the first reactor 104A. In accordance with an embodiment, the lixiviant is configured to flow in a counter current direction relative to the black mass slurry. In such case, the black mass slurry progresses sequentially from the first reactor 104A to the final reactor 104N, while the lixiviant flows from the final reactor 104N towards the first reactor 104A. In such counter current flow, the most depleted slurry contacts the fresh lixiviant, and the most metal-rich slurry encounters the partially spent lixiviant. The counter-current flow of the lixiviant relative to the flow of the black mass slurry creates a counter-current contact between the black mass slurry and the lixiviant. The control unit 108 is configured to monitor and regulate predetermined parameters in each of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104. As a result, the control unit 108 helps in managing compositional heterogeneity and variability inherent in the black mass slurry in different pretreatment conditions in each of the at least two continuous stirred tanks 104. In accordance with an embodiment, the plurality of sensors 106 comprises pH sensors, oxidation-reduction potential (ORP) sensors, and temperature sensors installed in each of the at least two continuous stirred tanks 104. The predetermined parameters comprise pH, oxidation-reduction potential (ORP), and temperature. In accordance with an embodiment, the control unit 108 is configured to receive sensor data from each of the plurality of sensors installed in each of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors (CSTRs) 104. The plurality of sensors 106 is installed in each of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors (CSTRs) 104. Such configuration of the plurality of sensors 106 ensures comprehensive monitoring throughout the process instead of relying on single-point measurements that cannot capture variations in black mass slurry. In accordance with an embodiment, the pH is maintained in a range of 0.5 to 4.0, the ORP is maintained in a range of-200 mV to +800 mV versus a standard hydrogen electrode, and the temperature is maintained in a range of 40°C to 95°C. In an implementation, the control unit 108 can adjust reagent dosing, heating input, or slurry flow rate to maintain predetermined parameters, such as the pH in the range of 0.5 to 4.0, the ORP in the range of-200 mV to +800 mV versus, and a temperature between 40°C and 95°C. Furthermore, the continuous leaching apparatus 102 includes the solid-liquid separation unit 110 positioned downstream of the final reactor 104N configured to separate pregnant leach solution (PLS) from solid residue. The solid-liquid separation unit 110 is positioned downstream of the final reactor 104N to separate the pregnant leach solution (PLS) containing dissolved metal ions from the solid residue. Such separation may be accomplished by filtration, thickening, or decantation, and the clarified PLS may subsequently be directed to solvent extraction, precipitation, or crystallization stages for recovery of lithium, cobalt, nickel, manganese, and the like. In accordance with an embodiment, the reductant comprises at least one compound selected from the group consisting of hydrogen peroxide, sodium metabisulfite, ascorbic acid, ferrous sulphate, and sodium thiosulfate. The continuous leaching apparatus 102 achieves twenty to thirty percent reduction in energy consumption. With reference to FIG. 2, there is shown an exemplary diagram 200 of the continuous leaching apparatus 102, which includes the feed inlet 202 and the lixiviant supply unit 204. The feed inlet 202 is configured to add black mass slurry into the first reactor 104A of the series of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104. In other words, the feed inlet 202 allows the black mass slurry to enter into the first reactor 104A. The feed inlet 202 at the first reactor 104A allows independent control of concentration of the black mass slurry into the continuous leaching apparatus 102. The lixiviant supply unit 204 is configured to introduce fresh lixiviant into the final reactor 104N of the series of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104. The lixiviant is configured to flow in a counter current direction relative to the black mass slurry. In such counter current flow, the most depleted slurry contacts the fresh lixiviant, and the most metal-rich slurry encounters the partially spent lixiviant. The counter-current flow of the lixiviant relative to the flow of the black mass slurry creates a counter-current contact between the black mass slurry and the lixiviant. Progressive leaching occurs as the black mass slurry advances through each of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104, with the lixiviant introduced counter-currently to enhance dissolution efficiency. Such operation also stabilizes redox and pH gradients across the series of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104, improving selective metal dissolution and minimizing impurity co-leaching. In an example, the specified range of pH 0.5 to 4.0 accommodates different chemical requirements of various reactor stages. Lower pH values around 0.5 to 1.5 typically applied in later stages of the at least two continuous stirred tank reactors 104, where fresh concentrated lixiviant contacts depleted solid material requiring strong acid to extract residual metals. Higher pH values around 2.0 to 4.0 typically applied in earlier stages where partially spent lixiviant contacts fresh black mass feed material with readily leachable metal content. In a preferred embodiment, the leaching operation typically runs under solids concentrations of in a range of 80 and 200 g/L, at temperatures ranging from 20 to 80 °C and pressures from ambient to about 1 barg. The pH is maintained below 1.5 proximal to the first reactor 104A and gradually relaxes towards the final reactor 104N, with ORP set points between +250 and +550 mV (Ag/AgCl). The total residence time across the series of the plurality of continuous stirred tank reactors 104 may range from 1.5 to 6 hours. The configuration of the continuous leaching apparatus 102 ensures the freshest lixiviant contacts the most depleted solids in the final reactor 104N, while the spent lixiviant exits the first reactor 104A and can be directed for neutralization or recycling. The continuous leaching apparatus 102 is compatible with various pre-processing routes depending on the composition of the black mass slurry. The black mass slurry has a particle size of 5-200 µm and a moisture content of in a range of between 2 to 15wt%. Optional pre-treatments may include aqueous defluorination and conditioning at 40°C to 60°C with mild alkaline wash (pH 9 to 10) to hydrolyze LiPF6 residues and precipitate fluorine as CaF2, followed by rinsing to near-neutral pH. Alternatively, reductive calcination under a low-oxygen atmosphere at a range between 250°C to 600°C may be used to decompose organics and improve wettability. Attritioning for 10 to 30 minutes can also be employed to expose active cathode surfaces and detach graphite or foil fines. In a first step of the method, the black mass was collected from spent NMC batteries. Subsequently, a sulphuric acid solution was prepared by diluting concentrated sulphuric acid with water to achieve concentrations ranging from 1M to 4M. The collected black mass was then immersed in the prepared sulphuric acid solution, maintaining a solid-to-liquid (S/L) ratio ranging from 80 g/L to 180 g/L for complete immersion. The leaching process was conducted at varying temperatures between 20°C and 80°C, with the oxidation-reduction potential (ORP) controlled at set-points ranging from 250 mV to 550 mV. An oxidant was added to the leaching solution at doses ranging from 0 to 5 wt% to enhance the dissolution of metal values. The black mass underwent a leaching period with residence time per stage varying from 30 minutes to 120 minutes to ensure the complete extraction of valuable metals. After leaching, the pregnant leach solution (PLS) and residue were separated through filtration. Following the separation, samples were collected for subsequent analysis to measure extraction efficiency of lithium (Li), nickel (Ni), cobalt (Co), and manganese (Mn) in the solution. The acid and oxidant consumption were calculated in kg per tonne of black mass processed. The filtered residue (graphite-rich material) obtained from the previous step was then analysed to determine the graphite grade and purity. The filtered residue (graphite-rich material) obtained from the previous step was then dried and analysed using X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) to determine phase evolution, Particle Size Distribution (PSD) analysis, and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area analysis for carbon and sulphur content to assess the graphite grade and purity. Additionally, the pregnant leach solution was analysed using Ion-Selective Electrode (ISE) to measure the concentration of fluorine (F) in mg/L to assess the leaching selectivity. Example 2: Let's consider an example illustrating the leach kinetics study of mixed black mass containing varying fractions of LFP material. In a first step of the method, the black mass was collected from a mixture of spent NMC and LFP batteries with LFP content ranging from 0% to 50% by weight. Subsequently, sulphuric acid solutions were prepared with varying initial acidity levels to accommodate the mixed chemistry of the black mass. The collected mixed black mass was then subjected to multi-stage leaching processes, with the number of stages varying from 2 to 5 stages to optimize metal extraction and selectivity. The timing of reductant and oxidant addition was controlled at different points during the leaching process to manage the dissolution of different metal species selectively. The leaching was designed to achieve extraction of lithium while directing phosphate into a solid phase. After each leaching stage, the pregnant leach solution (PLS) and residue were separated through filtration. Following the separation, samples were collected for subsequent analysis, involving Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectroscopy (ICP-OES) and Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometry (ICP-MS) to measure the extraction efficiency and selectivity of lithium (Li), iron (Fe), and phosphorus (P) in the solution. The hydrogen peroxide was monitored and optimized to achieve reduction in oxidant consumption compared to single-chemistry processing. The phosphate distribution between liquid and solid phases was quantified through chemical analysis. Calcium fluoride (CaF₂) was added to precipitate fluorine from the leach solution, and the resulting CaF₂ sludge mass was measured and recorded. The filtered residue obtained from the final leaching stage was then dried and analysed using X-Ray Diffraction (XRD) to determine phase evolution and identify phosphate-containing phases, Particle Size Distribution (PSD) analysis, and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area analysis for carbon and sulphur content. The pregnant leach solution was analysed using Ion-Selective Electrode (ISE) to measure the concentration of fluorine (F) in mg/L. patents.abstract: A lithium extraction apparatus for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solutions. The apparatus comprises feed-conditioning unit configured to receive a leach solution and remove heavy-metal impurities. The apparatus further comprises pre-concentration evaporator configured to concentrate the conditioned leach solution. The apparatus further comprises a primary crystallizer, which comprises jacketed vessel configured to maintain the concentrated solution within controlled temperature range, an agitation unit configured to maintain uniform suspension of crystals, and a controlled cooling profile configured to induce selective crystallization of Li2SO4·H2O while maintaining sodium sulfate in a dissolved state. Apparatus further comprises separation unit configured to separate lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals from mother liquor, a secondary crystallizer configured to receive mother liquor and induce crystallization of Na2SO4 as by-product, and drying unit configured to receive and dry the separated lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals below 120 °C to maintain a moisture content of less than 0.5 wt %. patents.complete_specification: Description:TECHNICAL FIELD The present disclosure relates to a field of hydrometallurgical recovery and purification of lithium compounds. Moreover, the present disclosure relates to an apparatus and method for recovering high-purity lithium sulfate monohydrate from lithium-bearing leach solutions. BACKGROUND Lithium compounds such as lithium Sulfate and lithium carbonate are key intermediates in the production of cathode materials for lithium-ion batteries. The global increase in demand for electric vehicles and energy storage systems has intensified research into the efficient recovery of lithium from both primary mineral sources and secondary sources, such as spent batteries. The hydrometallurgical processes are commonly employed for extracting lithium from black-mass residues generated during battery recycling. The hydrometallurgical processes usually involve the leaching of lithium-bearing materials, followed by concentration and purification steps to obtain lithium compounds of high purity suitable for battery applications. Conventional processes describe lithium recovery from aqueous leachates through evaporation, precipitation, solvent extraction, or ion-exchange operations. For example, conventional lithium extraction methods utilise high-temperature evaporative crystallization (often above 120 °C) to recover lithium sulfate or lithium carbonate. Other conventional approaches employ organic solvent extraction or ion-exchange resins to separate lithium ions from impurities and other metal ions selectively. Some industrial practices use multi-stage heating and concentration sequences combined with chemical additives to control pH and precipitation. The known processes, while capable of producing lithium compounds of moderate purity, require high thermal energy, involve multiple purification stages, and generate secondary waste streams that complicate large-scale implementation. However, the conventional lithium recovery and purification processes rely heavily on energy-intensive operations, complex chemical handling, and non-selective crystallization behaviour. The high-temperature conditions often lead to decomposition of process components, increased Total Organic Carbon (TOC) content in the product, and variable crystal morphology. The solvent extraction and ion-exchange routes require expensive reagents and resins, involve challenging regeneration cycles, and add to the overall capital and operational costs. Moreover, the crystallization steps employed in existing methods generally lack precise control of temperature gradients, resulting in mixed precipitation of lithium and sodium salts and reduced product purity. Thus, there exists a technical problem in achieving selective crystallization of lithium sulfate from sodium sulfate-rich hydrometallurgical leachates under controlled low-temperature conditions while maintaining high purity, low TOC, and reduced energy consumption. Therefore, in light of the foregoing discussion, there exists a need to overcome the aforementioned drawbacks associated with the conventional high-temperature and solvent-based lithium recovery methods. SUMMARY The present disclosure provides an apparatus and method for recovering high-purity lithium sulfate monohydrate from lithium-bearing leach solutions. The present disclosure provides a solution to the technical problem of how to recycle spent lithium-ion batteries and improve the efficiency of valuable material recovery, particularly lithium. An aim of the present disclosure is to provide a solution that overcomes at least partially the problems encountered in the prior art and provides an improved low-temperature lithium extraction apparatus and method that enables selective crystallization of lithium sulfate monohydrate in a controlled crystallization environment, while maintaining sodium sulfate in the dissolved state. One or more objectives of the present disclosure are achieved by the solutions provided in the enclosed independent claims. Advantageous implementations of the present disclosure are further defined in the dependent claims. In one aspect, the present disclosure provides a lithium extraction apparatus for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solutions. The apparatus comprises a feed-conditioning unit configured to receive a leach solution and remove heavy-metal impurities. The apparatus further comprises a pre-concentration evaporator configured to concentrate the conditioned leach solution. The apparatus further comprises a primary crystallizer. The primary crystallizer comprises a jacketed vessel configured to maintain the concentrated solution within a controlled temperature range. The primary crystallizer further comprises an agitation unit configured to maintain uniform suspension of crystals, and a controlled cooling profile configured to induce selective crystallization of lithium sulfate monohydrate (Li2SO4·H2O) while maintaining sodium sulfate in the dissolved state. Moreover, the apparatus further comprises a separation unit configured to separate lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals from mother liquor, a secondary crystallizer configured to receive the mother liquor and induce crystallization of sodium sulfate (Na2SO4) as a by-product; and a drying unit configured to receive and dry the separated lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals below 120 °C to maintain a moisture content of less than 0.5 wt %. Advantageously, the lithium extraction apparatus of the present disclosure enables efficient and high-purity recovery of lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solutions through a sequence of integrated, performance-enhancing stages. The inclusion of the feed-conditioning unit ensures removal of heavy-metal impurities at an early stage, resulting in a cleaner feed stream that minimises contamination and improves the overall product quality. The pre-concentration evaporator enhances process efficiency by reducing solvent volume and energy demand in subsequent crystallization stages, thereby lowering operational costs. The primary crystallizer provides precise thermal control and uniform mixing conditions that promote consistent crystal growth, allowing lithium sulfate monohydrate to form selectively while preventing co-precipitation of sodium sulfate. The controlled crystallization yields uniform particle size and exceptional purity. The downstream separation unit enables effective isolation of the lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals, ensuring high recovery rates and reduced process losses. The secondary crystallizer not only maximises material utilisation by recovering sodium sulfate as a valuable by-product but also contributes to waste minimisation and improved process economics. Finally, the low-temperature drying unit preserves product integrity, minimises thermal degradation, and ensures that the resulting lithium sulfate monohydrate meets stringent battery-grade moisture and purity specifications. Collectively, the features provide a low-energy, high-efficiency, and environmentally sustainable lithium recovery system capable of delivering consistent, high-purity output suitable for advanced energy-storage applications. In another aspect, the present disclosure provides a method for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solutions. The method comprises conditioning the leach solution to remove heavy-metal impurities. Further, the method comprises concentrating the conditioned leach solution, inducing selective crystallization of lithium sulfate monohydrate (Li2SO4·H2O) while maintaining sodium sulfate in the dissolved state. Furthermore, the method comprises separating lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals from mother liquor, receiving the mother liquor and inducing crystallization of sodium sulfate (Na2SO4) as a by-product, and drying the separated lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals below 120 °C to maintain a moisture content of less than 0.5 wt %, wherein the method produces lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals having a purity of at least 99.9 % and a total organic carbon (TOC) content of less than 10 ppm. The method achieves all the advantages and technical effects of the lithium extraction apparatus of the present disclosure. It is to be appreciated that all the aforementioned implementation forms can be combined. All steps which are performed by the various entities described in the present application as well as the functionalities described to be performed by the various entities are intended to mean that the respective entity is adapted to or configured to perform the respective steps and functionalities. It will be appreciated that features of the present disclosure are susceptible to being combined in various combinations without departing from the scope of the present disclosure as defined by the appended claims. Additional aspects, advantages, features, and objects of the present disclosure would be made apparent from the drawings and the detailed description of the illustrative implementations construed in conjunction with the appended claims that follow. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS The summary above, as well as the following detailed description of illustrative embodiments, is better understood when read in conjunction with the appended drawings. For the purpose of illustrating the present disclosure, exemplary constructions of the disclosure are shown in the drawings. However, the present disclosure is not limited to specific methods and instrumentalities disclosed herein. Moreover, those skilled in the art will understand that the drawings are not to scale. Wherever possible, like elements have been indicated by identical numbers. Embodiments of the present disclosure will now be described, by way of example only, with reference to the following diagrams wherein: FIG. 1 is a block diagram of a lithium extraction apparatus for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solutions, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure; FIG. 2 is a flowchart depicting a method for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solution, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure; and FIG. 3 illustrates a process of a lithium extraction apparatus for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solutions, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF EMBODIMENTS The following detailed description illustrates embodiments of the present disclosure and ways in which they can be implemented. Although some modes of carrying out the present disclosure have been disclosed, those skilled in the art would recognize that other embodiments for carrying out or practising the present disclosure are also possible. FIG. 1 is a block diagram of a lithium extraction apparatus for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solutions, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. With reference to FIG. 1, there is shown a block diagram 100 of a lithium extraction apparatus 102. The lithium extraction apparatus 102 includes a feed-conditioning unit 104, a pre-concentration evaporator 106, a primary crystallizer 108, a separation unit 110, a secondary crystallizer 112, and a drying unit 114. Furthermore, the primary crystallizer 108 includes a jacketed vessel 116, an agitation unit 118, and a controlled cooling profile 120. The lithium extraction apparatus 102 generally refers to a system or assembly of interconnected units configured for the extraction, purification, and recovery of lithium compounds from lithium-containing solutions, such as hydrometallurgical leachates obtained from ores or spent lithium-ion batteries. The lithium extraction apparatus 102 is designed to facilitate operations such as impurity removal, concentration, crystallization, separation, and drying to produce high-purity lithium compounds suitable for industrial applications. The feed-conditioning unit 104 may be referred to as a component configured to prepare and purify the incoming leach solution prior to lithium recovery operations. The feed-conditioning unit 104 functions to adjust the chemical composition and physical characteristics of the leachate by removing suspended solids, heavy-metal impurities, and other contaminants that may interfere with subsequent crystallization or concentration steps. The feed-conditioning unit 104 may include, but is not limited to, components such as filtration modules, neutralisation reactors, pH control systems, precipitation tanks, and settling or clarification units. The pre-concentration evaporator 106 may be referred to as a subsystem designed to increase the concentration of lithium ions in the conditioned leach solution before the crystallization stage. The pre-concentration evaporator 106 operates by partially removing water or solvent under controlled temperature and pressure conditions, thereby enhancing the lithium sulfate concentration to a level suitable for efficient and selective crystallization. The pre-concentration evaporator 106 may include, but is not limited to, a vacuum evaporator, falling-film or forced-circulation evaporator, or a multi-effect evaporation system equipped with heat exchangers and condensate recovery mechanisms. The primary crystallizer 108 may be referred to as a subsystem configured to facilitate the selective crystallization of lithium sulfate monohydrate (Li2SO4·H2O) from the pre-concentrated leach solution under controlled thermal and mixing conditions. The primary crystallizer 108 is designed to exploit the solubility difference between lithium sulfate and other co-dissolved salts, such as sodium sulfate, to achieve targeted precipitation of lithium sulfate while maintaining impurities in the dissolved phase. The separation unit 110 may be referred to as a subsystem configured to isolate the crystallised lithium sulfate monohydrate solids from the remaining liquid phase, commonly referred to as the mother liquor, following the primary crystallization process. The separation unit 110 enables efficient solid–liquid separation to recover lithium sulfate crystals with high purity and minimal loss of product. The separation unit 110 may include, but is not limited to, equipment such as vacuum filters, pressure filters, centrifuges, decanter systems, or filtration membranes, depending on the process scale and slurry characteristics. In some implementations, the separation unit 110 may also incorporate washing stages to remove residual impurities or dissolved salts from the crystal surface, further enhancing product quality. The secondary crystallizer 112 may be referred to as a subsystem configured to process the mother liquor obtained after separation of lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals, enabling further recovery of valuable by-products such as sodium sulfate (Na2SO4). Examples of the secondary crystallizer 112 may include, but are not limited to, a cooling crystallizer, batch crystallizer, or continuous mixed-suspension crystallizer equipped with a cooling jacket, agitation mechanism, and temperature control system for maintaining uniform crystal growth conditions. In some implementations, the secondary crystallizer 112 may incorporate sensors and automation controls for monitoring slurry concentration, temperature, and crystal size to ensure efficient recovery of sodium sulfate with desired purity and particle morphology. The drying unit 114 may be referred to as a subsystem configured to remove residual moisture from the separated lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals to obtain a stable, high-purity, battery-grade product. The examples of the drying unit 114 may include, but are not limited to, a tray dryer, rotary vacuum dryer, fluidised-bed dryer, or belt dryer, depending on the scale and process requirements. In some implementations, the drying unit 114 may incorporate heat-recovery mechanisms that transfer residual thermal energy to other parts of the process, such as the pre-concentration evaporator. The jacketed vessel 116 may be referred to as a component of the crystallization subsystem that provides precise thermal control over the crystallization process by regulating heat transfer between the process fluid and a surrounding heat exchange jacket. Examples of the jacketed vessel 116 may include, but are not limited to, a stirred-tank crystallizer, Mixed-Suspension Mixed-Product-Removal (MSMPR) reactor, or batch cooling crystallizer equipped with an external or internal jacket through which a heating or cooling medium circulates. The agitation unit 118 may be referred to as a subsystem incorporated within the lithium extraction apparatus 102 to maintain uniform suspension and mixing of solids and liquids during the crystallization process. The agitation unit 118 ensures homogeneity in temperature, concentration, and supersaturation levels throughout the crystallizer, thereby promoting controlled nucleation and consistent crystal growth of lithium sulfate monohydrate. Examples of the agitation unit 118 may include, but are not limited to, mechanical impellers, turbine agitators, paddle mixers, or magnetic stirrers, driven by variable-speed motors to adjust mixing intensity based on process requirements. The controlled cooling profile 120 may be referred to as a process parameter configured to regulate the rate and sequence of temperature reduction within the crystallization stage to achieve selective and uniform crystal formation. Examples of the controlled cooling profile 120 may include, but are not limited to, programmable temperature control systems, automated heat-exchange loops, or Process Logic Controllers (PLCs) that adjust cooling media flow, jacket temperature, and time-based temperature ramping according to predefined setpoints. In some implementations, the controlled cooling profile 120 is designed to lower the solution temperature from approximately 65 °C to 45 °C in a regulated manner. There is provided the lithium extraction apparatus 102 for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solutions. The lithium extraction apparatus 102 comprises the feed-conditioning unit 104 configured to receive a leach solution and remove heavy-metal impurities. The feed-conditioning unit 104 serves as the initial purification stage within the lithium extraction apparatus 102. The feed-conditioning unit 104 is configured to receive the raw leach solution containing dissolved lithium along with unwanted impurities such as iron, manganese, nickel, cobalt, and aluminium compounds, and to remove such impurities before the solution undergoes concentration and crystallization. The feed-conditioning unit 104 functions through controlled chemical and physical treatment of the incoming leach solution. The feed-conditioning unit 104 operates by adjusting pH and redox potential to precipitate heavy metals as insoluble hydroxides or sulfates, followed by solid–liquid separation using filtration or clarification. The feed-conditioning unit 104 may also include sensors and automated control systems to monitor key process parameters such as pH, turbidity, and conductivity to maintain stable operation. As a result, the conditioned solution exiting the feed-conditioning unit 104 contains lithium predominantly in soluble form and is free from solid impurities, enabling efficient and selective crystallization in the subsequent processing stages. The lithium extraction apparatus 102 comprises the pre-concentration evaporator 106 configured to concentrate the conditioned leach solution. The pre-concentration evaporator 106 operates by circulating the conditioned leach solution through a heat-transfer system, such as a falling-film or forced-circulation evaporator, where controlled heating causes partial vaporisation of the solvent under reduced pressure. The vapour generated is condensed and recovered, while the concentrated lithium sulfate solution is directed to the primary crystallizer 108. The pre-concentration evaporator 106 is usually equipped with temperature, pressure, and flow control systems to maintain stable operation and avoid overheating or scaling. Through the pre-concentration evaporator 106 process, the lithium sulfate concentration is increased to approximately 120 g/L, creating a feed solution with the ideal composition for subsequent low-temperature crystallization and high-purity lithium sulfate recovery. In accordance with an embodiment, the pre-concentration evaporator 106 operates under vacuum at 60 °C to 80 °C to concentrate the leach solution to approximately 120 g/L lithium sulfate (Li2SO4) concentration. The pre-concentration evaporator 106 achieves the operation through a controlled heat-transfer and pressure-regulated process. The conditioned leach solution is introduced into an evaporation chamber, such as a falling-film or forced-circulation evaporator, where indirect heating under vacuum causes partial vaporisation of water. The vapour is condensed and recovered, while the concentrated lithium sulfate solution is continuously withdrawn and transferred to the crystallization stage. The temperature and pressure within the pre-concentration evaporator 106 are monitored and adjusted using automated control systems to maintain stable operation within the 60 °C to 80 °C range. The controlled process not only ensures the target lithium sulfate concentration of approximately 120 g/L but also contributes to consistent feed quality, reduced energy consumption, and prevention of fouling or salt deposition on heat-transfer surfaces. The lithium extraction apparatus 102 comprises the primary crystallizer 108. The primary crystallizer 108 comprises the jacketed vessel 116 configured to maintain the concentrated solution within a controlled temperature range. The jacketed vessel 116 achieves temperature regulation by circulating a controlled heat-transfer medium, such as chilled water, brine, or thermal oil, through an outer jacket that surrounds the crystallization chamber. The setup allows precise adjustment of the internal temperature through automated process controls linked to temperature sensors and flow regulators. The primary crystallizer 108 may operate under a programmed temperature profile, gradually reducing the solution temperature to initiate and sustain crystal formation under steady-state conditions. The continuous agitation within the jacketed vessel 116 ensures homogeneous distribution of heat and solute concentration, preventing localised supersaturation and enabling uniform crystal growth. Through the combination of controlled heat exchange, automated monitoring, and uniform mixing, the jacketed vessel 116 maintains the crystallization conditions, resulting in high-purity lithium sulfate monohydrate suitable for battery-grade applications. In accordance with an embodiment, the primary crystallizer 108 is configured to operate at a temperature range of 40 °C to 70 °C. The temperature range of 40 °C to 70 °C is maintained through an integrated thermal control system within the jacketed vessel 116 of the primary crystallizer 108. The circulating heat-transfer medium (such as chilled water or thermal oil) flows through the jacket surrounding the crystallization chamber, allowing precise regulation of internal temperature. The automated process controllers monitor temperature sensors placed within the primary crystallizer 108 and adjust the flow or temperature of the circulating medium to maintain the desired range. The cooling process may follow a gradual or stepwise temperature reduction, ensuring steady-state supersaturation conditions that favour uniform nucleation and crystal growth. In accordance with an embodiment, the primary crystallizer 108 comprises a jacketed Mixed-Suspension Mixed-Product-Removal (MSMPR) reactor. The primary crystallizer 108 operates as the jacketed MSMPR reactor by circulating a temperature-controlled heat-transfer medium through the external jacket to maintain the primary crystallizer 108 contents within the desired low-temperature range (40 °C to 70 °C). The internal agitation keeps the suspension well mixed, ensuring uniform distribution of supersaturation and preventing sedimentation. As crystals form, the mixed slurry is continuously withdrawn at a controlled rate, while fresh pre-concentrated leach solution is simultaneously introduced to maintain constant reactor volume and composition. The steady inflow and outflow support the establishment of a stable crystallization environment where nucleation and growth occur at predictable rates. The jacketed MSMPR reactor configuration provides fine control over temperature profiles, mixing intensity, and residence time, enabling selective crystallization of lithium sulfate monohydrate with reproducible purity, morphology, and yield. The primary crystallizer 108 further comprises the agitation unit 118 configured to maintain a uniform suspension of crystals. The agitation unit 118 operates by continuously mixing the crystallizer contents using mechanical impellers, turbine agitators, or similar mixing devices. The impeller speed and design are selected to maintain sufficient turbulence to suspend crystals evenly without causing excessive shear or crystal breakage. By distributing heat, solute concentration, and suspended solids uniformly, the agitation unit 118 maintains a consistent supersaturation level that promotes controlled crystal formation. The integrated process controls may adjust agitation speed based on slurry density or crystallization stage to enhance performance. Through the continuous and uniform mixing, the agitation unit 118 supports efficient, selective, and reproducible crystallization of lithium sulfate monohydrate within the primary crystallizer 108. The primary crystallizer 108 further comprises the controlled cooling profile 120 configured to induce selective crystallization of lithium sulfate monohydrate (Li2SO4·H2O) while maintaining sodium sulfate in the dissolved state. The controlled cooling profile 120 functions through a combination of thermal management systems, such as a temperature-controlled jacket around the crystallizer and automated process controllers that regulate the flow of cooling media. The sensors inside the primary crystallizer 108 continuously monitor the temperature, and a programmed cooling strategy gradually reduces the solution temperature from around 65 °C to 45 °C to establish the optimal supersaturation for lithium sulfate crystallization. The controlled descent avoids sudden temperature drops that could trigger unwanted nucleation events or impurity precipitation. By ensuring predictable and stable thermal conditions throughout the crystallization cycle, the controlled cooling profile 120 enables selective formation of lithium sulfate monohydrate while maintaining sodium sulfate in dissolved form, thereby supporting high-purity lithium recovery in the primary crystallizer 108. In accordance with an embodiment, the controlled cooling profile 120 is configured to cool the temperature of the concentrated solution from 65 °C to 45 °C. The controlled cooling profile 120 achieves the 65 °C to 45 °C temperature reduction through automated thermal regulation systems integrated into the primary crystallizer 108. The temperature interval from 65 °C to 45 °C represents a programmed and gradual cooling sequence that governs when and how lithium sulfate monohydrate (Li2SO4·H2O) begins to crystallise. Cooling the concentrated solution from 65 °C to 45 °C is required because the temperature range aligns with the solubility characteristics of lithium sulfate relative to sodium sulfate. At around 65 °C, lithium sulfate remains largely dissolved, while reducing the temperature to 45 °C lowers the solubility enough to initiate selective nucleation and controlled crystal growth. The sodium sulfate, however, maintains higher solubility across the same temperature band, allowing the sodium sulfate to stay dissolved and preventing co-precipitation. By precisely managing thermal gradients and supersaturation levels during the descent from 65 °C to 45 °C, the controlled cooling profile 120 ensures stable and selective formation of lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals with consistent morphology and high purity. The lithium extraction apparatus 102 comprises the separation unit 110 configured to separate lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals from mother liquor. The separation unit 110 operates through mechanical solid–liquid separation techniques such as filtration, centrifugation, pressure-driven separation, or vacuum-assisted extraction. As the slurry from the primary crystallizer 108 enters the separation unit 110, the solid lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals are retained by a filter medium or separated using centrifugal force, while the liquid mother liquor is drained or discharged for further processing. The separation unit 110 may incorporate features such as washing stages to remove residual impurities from the crystal surfaces, moisture-control mechanisms to enhance downstream drying, and automation sensors to monitor slurry flow, pressure, and cake formation. By efficiently isolating the lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals from the mother liquor, the separation unit 110 ensures consistent product quality, enhanced purity, and reliable throughput within the lithium extraction apparatus 102. In accordance with an embodiment, the lithium extraction apparatus 102 comprises a recycle stream configured to return mother liquor from the separation unit 110 to the feed-conditioning unit 104. The recycle stream allows the liquid remaining after lithium sulfate monohydrate crystallization to be reintegrated into the earlier stage of the process. The recycle stream functions through a controlled piping and pumping system that transfers the mother liquor from the separation unit 110 back to the feed-conditioning unit 104. Flow control valves, sensors, and automated process logic regulate the quantity and timing of the recycled flow to maintain stable operating conditions and consistent solution composition. The recycled liquid enters the feed-conditioning unit 104, where the feed-conditioning unit 104 undergoes the same impurity removal operations, such as pH adjustment, precipitation, and filtration, as the incoming leach feed. The feed-conditioning unit 104 ensures that any accumulated impurities or dissolved salts are managed effectively before the solution re-enters the pre-concentration and crystallization stages. By integrating the recycle stream into the process loop, the lithium extraction apparatus 102 achieves steady-state operation, improved material efficiency, and enhanced control over solution chemistry throughout the lithium extraction process. The lithium extraction apparatus 102 comprises the secondary crystallizer 112 configured to receive the mother liquor and induce crystallization of sodium sulfate (Na2SO4) as a by-product. The secondary crystallizer 112 operates by cooling the mother liquor to a lower temperature range, around 20 °C to 30 °C, where sodium sulfate solubility decreases sufficiently to trigger the crystallization. The secondary crystallizer 112 may employ a cooled jacket, chilled water loop, or refrigeration-based heat exchanger to achieve and maintain the desired temperature. The agitation may be used to ensure uniform temperature distribution and consistent crystal growth. Once the sodium sulfate crystals form, the sodium sulfate crystal can be removed via downstream separation methods such as filtration or centrifugation. The sensors and automated controls regulate the cooling rate, slurry density, and residence time to optimise crystal quality and yield. Through the controlled thermal process, the secondary crystallizer 112 effectively recovers sodium sulfate as a by-product while supporting stable and efficient operation of the lithium extraction apparatus 102. In accordance with an embodiment, the secondary crystallizer 112 is configured to operate at a temperature below 30 °C to induce sodium sulfate crystallization. The operating temperature below 30 °C creates conditions where sodium sulfate becomes supersaturated and begins to form solid crystals, allowing sodium sulfate to be separated as a distinct by-product. The secondary crystallizer 112 achieves the low operating temperature by circulating a cooling medium, such as chilled water or glycol, through a cooling jacket or heat exchanger. The automated temperature control systems monitor the internal temperature and adjust cooling flow to maintain below 30 °C condition. As the mother liquor cools, sodium sulfate reaches supersaturation and begins to nucleate and grow as solid crystals. The agitation may be used to keep the crystal slurry uniform and prevent localized cold spots or agglomeration. Once sufficient crystallization occurs, the resulting sodium sulfate crystals are removed through a downstream separation step. The lithium extraction apparatus 102 comprises the drying unit 114 configured to receive and dry the separated lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals below 120 °C to maintain a moisture content of less than 0.5 wt %. The drying unit 114 operates by exposing the wet lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals to a controlled heat source, such as in a tray dryer, a vacuum dryer, a rotary dryer, or a fluidised-bed dryer, while regulating temperature so that it remains below 120 °C. Heat is transferred gently and uniformly to evaporate residual moisture without compromising the crystalline structure. Airflow, vacuum pressure, or agitation may be incorporated to enhance moisture removal and prevent localised overheating. The sensors and automated controllers monitor temperature, humidity, and drying time to ensure consistent operation and precise moisture reduction. Once the drying cycle is complete, the crystals are discharged with a controlled and uniform moisture content of less than 0.5 wt%. Through the regulated process, the drying unit 114 ensures the production of a stable, high-purity lithium sulfate monohydrate product suitable for battery-grade applications. In accordance with an embodiment, the lithium extraction apparatus 102 comprises a heat-recovery unit configured to recover thermal energy from the drying unit 114 and transfer the recovered thermal energy to the pre-concentration evaporator 106. The heat-recovery unit functions as an energy-integration subsystem that intercepts waste heat in the form of warm exhaust air, vapour, or residual thermal fluid from the drying unit 114. The heat-recovery unit operates by transferring thermal energy from the drying unit 114 to the pre-concentration evaporator 106 through heat-exchange mechanisms such as plate heat exchangers, shell-and-tube exchangers, recovery coils, or thermal oil circuits. As the drying unit 114 releases warm exhaust air or vapour, the heat-recovery unit captures the thermal stream and circulates the thermal stream through a heat-exchange interface where the energy is absorbed by a secondary heating medium (e.g., water, glycol, or thermal oil). The heated medium is then routed to the pre-concentration evaporator 106, where the pre-concentration evaporator 106 provides a portion of the thermal energy required for solvent evaporation. In accordance with an embodiment, the lithium extraction apparatus 102 is configured to produce lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals having a purity of at least 99.9 % and a Total Organic Carbon (TOC) content of less than 10 ppm. The lithium extraction apparatus 102 achieves this high level of purity and low TOC content of less than 10 ppm through a carefully integrated process design. The feed-conditioning unit 104 removes heavy metals and suspended impurities, ensuring a clean initial solution. The pre-concentration evaporator 106 concentrates lithium sulfate without introducing decomposition products because the pre-concentration evaporator 106 operates under controlled temperatures and vacuum. The primary crystallizer 108, equipped with the jacketed vessel 116, the agitation unit 118, and the controlled cooling profile 120, selectively precipitates lithium sulfate monohydrate while keeping sodium sulfate and other impurities dissolved. The separation unit 110 efficiently removes mother liquor, preventing impurity carryover. The secondary crystallizer 112 lowers sodium sulfate levels in the recycled streams, preventing impurity buildup. The drying unit 114 removes moisture at temperatures below 120 °C, preserving crystal structure and preventing thermal decomposition or organic contamination. Throughout the process steps, the use of low-temperature operation, controlled crystallization profiles, and closed-loop recycling minimises organic ingress and ensures consistent removal of contaminants. Through the engineered combination of purification mechanisms, the lithium extraction apparatus 102 reliably produces lithium sulfate monohydrate with ≥99.9% purity and TOC <10 ppm. FIG. 2 is a flowchart depicting a method for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solution, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. FIG. 2 is described in conjunction with the elements of the FIG. 1. With reference to FIG. 2, there is shown a flowchart of a method 200 for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solution. The method includes the steps 202 to 212. At step 202, the method 200 comprises conditioning the leach solution to remove heavy-metal impurities. The leach solution contains dissolved lithium along with impurities originating from processed or recycled lithium-bearing materials such as black-mass residues, ore leachates, or hydrometallurgical intermediate solutions. The conditioning refers to a purification step in which the leach solution undergoes chemical treatment, such as pH adjustment, controlled precipitation, and redox stabilisation, to convert heavy metals, including iron, manganese, nickel, cobalt, and aluminium, into insoluble forms. The conditioned slurry is subsequently filtered or clarified to obtain a purified solution enriched in dissolved lithium sulfate. The conditioning step stabilises the chemical composition of the solution, minimises impurity carryover, and prepares the feed for efficient downstream concentration and crystallization. At step 204, the method 200 comprises concentrating the conditioned leach solution. The concentration step is performed using a vacuum-assisted pre-concentration evaporator, which removes a portion of the water at controlled temperatures and pressures. The purpose of the concentration step is to increase the lithium sulfate content to an optimal level, typically around 120 g/L, improving supersaturation kinetics required for selective crystallization. Operating under vacuum enables solvent removal at moderate temperatures, preventing thermal decomposition of dissolved species and avoiding premature precipitation. The concentration phase enhances the efficiency of the subsequent crystallization stage by reducing solution volume, improving energy utilisation, and establishing the chemical conditions required for controlled nucleation of lithium sulfate monohydrate. At step 206, the method 200 comprises inducing selective crystallization of lithium sulfate monohydrate (Li2SO4·H2O) while maintaining sodium sulfate in the dissolved state. The concentrated solution is introduced into the primary crystallizer 108 equipped with controlled temperature regulation and agitation. The primary crystallizer 108 follows the controlled cooling profile 120, decreasing the temperature from approximately 65 °C to 45 °C, a range where lithium sulfate monohydrate becomes supersaturated and begins to crystallise. The sodium sulfate, however, remains in solution due to the higher solubility within the temperature interval. The selective crystallization mechanism exploits the differential solubility characteristics of lithium and sodium sulfates, enabling controlled formation of high-purity lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals. At step 208, the method 200 comprises separating lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals from mother liquor. The crystallised slurry exiting the primary crystallizer 108 is subjected to mechanical solid–liquid separation using equipment such as a vacuum filter, pressure filter, or centrifuge. The separation step isolates solid lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals while allowing the liquid mother liquor, containing dissolved sodium sulfate and trace impurities, to pass through. The washing of the filtered crystals may be performed to remove residual soluble salts, thereby improving final product purity. The separation step ensures efficient crystal recovery, enhances process selectivity, and prepares the lithium sulfate monohydrate for subsequent drying. At step 210, the method 200 comprises receiving the mother liquor and inducing crystallization of sodium sulfate (Na2SO4) as a by-product. The mother liquor is transferred to the secondary crystallizer 112, where the temperature is lowered to below 30 °C to achieve supersaturation conditions for sodium sulfate. At the reduced temperature, sodium sulfate crystallises selectively due to the solubility profile, enabling recovery of a commercially valuable by-product. The controlled cooling and agitation ensure uniform crystal growth and prevent impurity incorporation. The recovered sodium sulfate enhances process efficiency by maximising material utilisation and reducing waste generation. The secondary crystallization also mitigates sodium accumulation in recycle streams, maintaining chemical balance within the overall extraction process. At step 212, the method 200 comprises drying the separated lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals below 120 °C to maintain a moisture content of less than 0.5 wt %, where the method 200 produces lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals having a purity of at least 99.9 % and a Total Organic Carbon (TOC) content of less than 10 ppm. The filtered lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals are transferred to the drying unit 114, such as a tray dryer, vacuum dryer, or fluidized-bed dryer, where gentle and uniform heating removes residual moisture without altering the crystal structure. Maintaining the drying temperature below 120 °C prevents thermal degradation, preserves the monohydrate form of lithium sulfate, and avoids organic contamination or elevated TOC levels. The controlled drying step provides the final lithium sulfate monohydrate product that meets stringent quality specifications, including a purity of at least 99.9% and TOC content below 10 ppm, suitable for battery-grade material production. FIG. 3 illustrates a process of a lithium extraction apparatus for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solutions, in accordance with an embodiment of the present disclosure. FIG. 3 is described in conjunction with elements of the FIGs. 1 and 2. With reference to FIG. 3, there is shown a process 300 of the lithium extraction apparatus 102 for recovering battery-grade lithium from hydrometallurgical leach solutions. The process 300 includes a series of operations 302 to 318. At operation 302, the process 300 commences with the introduction of black mass into a leaching unit. The black mass comprises pulverised cathode and anode materials generated from the mechanical processing of spent lithium-ion batteries At operation 304, the black mass is treated with an aqueous leachant under controlled thermal conditions represented by the temperature control block 306. At operation 308, the regulated temperature environment promotes dissolution of lithium and other soluble metal species into the leach solution, enabling the formation of a lithium-rich liquid phase while leaving undissolved residues suspended. At operation 310, the process 300 involves transferring the leached slurry to a filter unit, which performs a solid–liquid separation. The filtration operation removes insoluble components such as graphite, copper and aluminium fragments, polymeric separator residues, and other particulate matter. At operation 312, the clarified solution is processed through a purification unit, corresponding functionally to the feed-conditioning unit 104. The purification operation removes dissolved heavy-metal impurities, including nickel, manganese, cobalt, iron, and aluminium, through controlled precipitation, pH adjustment, and redox-based chemical reactions. The purification outputs a lithium-enriched purified solution, which serves as the refined input for selective crystallization. At operation 314, the purified lithium-containing solution is introduced into a crystallization unit or the primary crystallizer 108. The primary crystallizer 108 is equipped with the jacketed vessel 116 and temperature-control features, represented by the heat-exchange symbol. The controlled cooling profile 120 is applied to induce selective nucleation and growth of lithium sulfate monohydrate (Li2SO4·H2O). The cooling regime is optimised so that sodium sulfate remains dissolved, enabling the selective formation of lithium sulfate crystals. The agitation unit 118 within the primary crystallizer 108 maintains uniform suspension, preventing local supersaturation and ensuring controlled particle morphology. At operation 316, the crystallised slurry from the primary crystallizer 108 is directed to the separation unit 110. The solid lithium sulfate monohydrate crystals are isolated from the mother liquor using filtration or centrifugation. The separated solids constitute the intermediate lithium product, while the mother liquor containing dissolved sodium sulfate is forwarded to the secondary crystallization 112. At operation 318, the mother liquor is processed through the secondary crystallizer 112, where the mother liquor undergoes further cooling to temperatures favourable for the crystallization of sodium sulfate (Na2SO4). The solubility of sodium sulfate decreases at lower temperatures, enabling the selective formation of sodium sulfate crystals. The recovered sodium sulfate constitutes a by-product stream of the process 300, improving overall material utilisation and reducing waste accumulation in the recycling loop. Thereafter, the conditioned solution was supplied to the pre-concentration evaporator 106, which was operated under vacuum at 150 mbar and at a temperature range of 60–80 °C.
