patents.abstract: The present disclosure relates to an advanced mechanical vapor recompression (MVR) evaporation system for concentrating lithium hydroxide (LiOH) solution with improved energy efficiency, purity, and operational reliability. The system includes a titanium alloy impeller with labyrinth sealing and steam-flush protection, a vapor separator integrated with a crystal trap for selective sodium chloride precipitation, and a condensate heat recovery loop that preheats both feed and auxiliary utilities. Operating under vacuum (250–300 mmHg) and moderate temperatures (80–95 °C), the process suppresses lithium carbonate precipitation and reduces fouling. Inline conductivity and density sensors provide automated concentration control by adjusting compressor load. This configuration achieves up to 95% efficiency, minimizes scaling, enables zero-liquid discharge, and reduces energy costs compared to conventional multi-effect evaporation.
patents.complete_specification: Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION [0001] The present disclosure relates to the technical field of chemical process engineering and industrial evaporation technologies. More particularly, the present disclosure relates to an advanced mechanical vapor recompression (MVR) evaporation system and method for concentrating lithium hydroxide solution. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION [0002] Background description includes information that may be useful in understanding the present disclosure. It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed invention, or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art. [0003] Lithium hydroxide has emerged as a critical raw material for the manufacture of lithium-ion batteries, particularly for high-nickel cathode chemistries used in electric vehicles and energy storage systems. The increasing global demand for battery-grade lithium hydroxide has intensified the need for efficient, reliable, and cost-effective concentration technologies capable of producing high-purity lithium hydroxide solutions at industrial scale. [0004] Conventional lithium hydroxide concentration processes typically employ multi-effect evaporator (MEE) systems. While MEE technology is widely adopted, it is inherently energy-intensive due to its reliance on large quantities of external steam and electrical power. For example, a five-effect MEE plant generally consumes approximately 0.30 kg of steam to evaporate one liter of water, whereas a two-effect system may require around 0.55 kg of steam per liter. As a result, operating costs of MEE plants can be substantial, with estimates ranging from ₹25–30 per kiloliter to ₹90–100 per kiloliter or higher, depending largely on steam demand and power consumption. Additional expenditures arise from chemical dosing, consumables, skilled manpower requirements, and periodic replacement of plant components, leading to complex maintenance and high lifecycle costs. [0005] Further, conventional MEE systems often operate at relatively high temperatures, which accelerates fouling, scaling, and corrosion. In lithium hydroxide processing, such conditions promote precipitation of lithium carbonate and other salts, resulting in reduced heat-transfer efficiency, frequent shutdowns for cleaning, and compromised product purity. [0006] Mechanical Vapor Recompression (MVR) evaporation technology is recognized as a more energy-efficient alternative to steam-driven evaporation, as it reuses latent heat from process vapor and substantially reduces external steam requirements. However, direct implementation of conventional MVR technology in lithium hydroxide concentration systems presents significant technical challenges. [0007] Lithium hydroxide solutions exhibit a strong tendency toward scaling, particularly due to lithium carbonate precipitation under certain temperature and concentration regimes. Additionally, vapor streams generated during lithium hydroxide processing can be highly corrosive, reducing equipment lifespan and increasing maintenance costs. The presence of sodium chloride impurities in process streams further contributes to operational instability, including unwanted crystallization, fouling of heat-exchange surfaces, and reduced process control. Moreover, existing systems often lack integrated energy-recovery mechanisms capable of efficiently transferring heat between internal process streams, thereby limiting the achievable energy savings. [0008] Existing disclosures relating to MVR systems for lithium hydroxide processing primarily focus on basic vapor recompression approaches and do not adequately address the combined challenges of impurity-induced crystallization, corrosion resistance, process stability, and system-level heat integration. Consequently, there remains a need for an improved lithium hydroxide concentration system capable of minimizing scaling and fouling, improving energy efficiency, stabilizing operation, and enhancing product purity while reducing overall operating costs. OBJECTIVES OF THE INVENTION [0009] Some of the objects of the present disclosure, which at least one embodiment herein satisfies, are as follows. [0010] An object of the present disclosure is to provide an advanced mechanical vapor recompression (MVR) evaporation system (100) for concentrating lithium hydroxide solution. [0011] Another object of the present disclosure is to provide a process for concentrating lithium hydroxide solution. [0012] Further object of the present disclosure is to provide an energy-efficient evaporation system for concentrating lithium hydroxide solutions, which overcomes the limitations of conventional evaporation technologies by reducing steam consumption, minimizing fouling, and improving operational stability. [0013] Another object of the present disclosure is to provide an advanced MVR evaporation system configured to reuse process vapor as a heating medium through vapor recompression, thereby significantly reducing external thermal energy requirements. [0014] A further objective of the present disclosure is to provide an MVR system specifically adapted for lithium hydroxide processing, wherein the system operates within an optimized pressure and temperature window sufficient to suppress lithium carbonate precipitation and reduce scaling on heat-transfer surfaces. [0015] Another objective of the present disclosure is to provide an evaporation system incorporating a vapor separator integrated with a crystal trap configured to selectively capture sodium chloride crystals, thereby preventing downstream fouling and improving process stability. [0016] Still another objective of the present disclosure is to provide an integrated condensate heat-recovery arrangement configured to transfer latent heat from condensed vapor to incoming process streams, thereby maximizing internal heat utilization and improving overall thermal efficiency. [0017] Yet another objective of the present disclosure is to provide a process control system including inline conductivity and density sensors configured to dynamically regulate compressor load and circulation rates so as to maintain a predetermined lithium hydroxide concentration and ensure consistent product quality. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [0018] This summary is provided to introduce a selection of concepts in a simplified form that are further described below in the Detailed Description section. This summary is not intended to identify key features or essential features of the claimed subject matter, nor is it intended to be used as an aid in determining the scope of the claimed subject matter. [0019] An aspect of the present disclosure provides an advanced mechanical vapor recompression (MVR) evaporation system (100) for concentrating lithium hydroxide solution, the system comprising: a mechanical vapor recompressor (101) configured to recompress the vapor of an evaporator and reuse the compressed vapor as a primary heating medium within a closed loop evaporation circuit; at least one calandria heat-exchange unit (201, 301) fluidly connected to the mechanical vapor recompresspr (101) and configured to receive the compressed vapor for evaporating lithium hydroxide solution; at least one vapor separator (202, 302) arranged downstream of the calandria heat-exchange unit (201, 301) and configured to separate vapor from concentrated lithium hydroxide solution after evaporation, wherein at least one vapor separator (202, 302) integrated with a crystal trap and configured to selectively remove sodium chloride crystals from the process stream; [0037] The present disclosure is based on the advanced Mechanical Vapor Recompression (MVR) which is an energy-efficient evaporation technology that reuses the vapor generated from a liquid to provide the heat needed for continued evaporation. It achieves by compressing the vapor, raising its temperature and pressure, and then using it as the heat source—instead of fresh steam. The key advantages of an advanced Mechanical Vapor Recompression (MVR) over traditional evaporation systems (like single-effect or multi-effect evaporators), especially in applications like lithium hydroxide concentration or crystallization are as follows: [0038] Compressor Design: The compressor includes an impeller made of a titanium alloy, which provides excellent corrosion resistance, low density, and improved wear resistance, thereby extending equipment life. The compressor further comprises a non-contact labyrinth seal combined with a steam-flush purge arrangement, enabling reliable sealing and stable operation under vacuum conditions. Additionally, the compressor is equipped with bearings designed for long service life and reliable performance in corrosive, high-moisture vapor environments. [0039] Integrated Crystal Trap: The vapor separator is configured to incorporate an integrated crystal trap that selectively promotes precipitation and retention of sodium chloride crystals, thereby preventing crystal carryover and reducing fouling in downstream equipment. [0040] Optimized Operating Window: The evaporation process is carried out under a controlled vacuum of about 250–300 mmHg and at a temperature ranging from about 80 °C to 95 °C, thereby suppressing lithium carbonate scaling while enabling efficient and rapid concentration of the lithium hydroxide solution. [0041] Condensate Heat Recovery: The system further comprises a condensate heat-recovery arrangement configured such that the recovered condensate transfers heat to the incoming feed solution and to auxiliary process streams, including return water, thereby improving overall thermal integration and maximizing energy efficiency of the evaporation process. [0042] Smart Process Control: The system further comprises an automated process-control arrangement including at least one inline conductivity sensor and at least one density sensor configured to continuously monitor solution concentration and to dynamically regulate compressor load and liquid circulation rate, thereby maintaining a substantially constant target concentration of lithium hydroxide during operation. Example 1: Continuous Operation at Industrial Scale [0092] An advanced mechanical vapor recompression (MVR) evaporation system (100) as described in the present disclosure was operated under continuous industrial conditions for concentrating a lithium hydroxide solution. [0093] A lithium hydroxide feed solution having a lithium concentration of about 2–3 g/L (GPL) was stored in the feed tank (T-1) and introduced into the system using the feed pump (602). The feed solution was first passed through the plate heat exchanger (701) where it was preheated using recovered condensate heat from the process streams to obtain a preheated lithium hydroxide solution. [0094] The preheated lithium hydroxide solution was then circulated through the calandria heat-exchange units (201, 301) by means of the circulation pumps (203, 303) at a circulation rate approximately six times the feed flow rate. The compressed vapor generated by the mechanical vapor recompressor (101) was supplied to the shell side of the calandria heat-exchange units (201, 301), thereby transferring latent heat to the circulating solution and causing evaporation of solvent from the lithium hydroxide solution. [0095] The vapor generated during evaporation was directed to the vapor separators (202, 302) where vapor was separated from the concentrated lithium hydroxide solution. The vapor separators were provided with integrated crystal traps configured to selectively capture sodium chloride crystals, thereby preventing fouling of downstream equipment and allowing clean vapor to pass through the vapor path. [0096] The separated clean vapor was recompressed by the mechanical vapor recompressor (101), thereby increasing the vapor temperature and pressure, and the recompressed vapor was reused as the heating medium in the calandria heat-exchange units (201, 301) to sustain the evaporation cycle in a closed loop. [0097] The condensed vapor generated during the heat exchange process was collected through the condensate pot (501) and transferred by the condensate suction pump (502) for reuse within the system. A portion of the recovered condensate was directed to the heat exchanger (702) and plate heat exchanger (701) to recover thermal energy for preheating the incoming feed and auxiliary process streams. The remaining condensate was collected in the condensate tank (T-2) for reuse or discharge as required. [0098] The vacuum pump (601) was operated to evacuate the evaporation system and maintain a sub-atmospheric pressure by removing non-condensable gases, thereby enabling evaporation at reduced boiling temperatures and improving heat-transfer efficiency. [0099] The concentration of lithium hydroxide solution in the process was continuously monitored using inline conductivity and density sensors, which were operatively connected to the system control unit. Based on sensor feedback, the compressor load and liquid circulation rate were automatically adjusted to maintain the desired lithium hydroxide concentration. [00100] The system was operated at a feed flow rate of about 5–10 m³/h, an evaporation temperature of about 80–95 °C, and an operating pressure of about 0.20–0.40 bar. The mechanical vapor recompressor (101) operated with a compressor power of approximately 250 kW. [00101] Under these operating conditions, the process produced a lithium hydroxide slurry having a lithium concentration of about 18–20 g/L (GPL). [00102] The crystals obtained during the concentration process exhibited an average particle size in the range of about 220–320 µm, which was suitable for downstream separation and handling. [00103] After solid-liquid separation using a centrifuge, the recovered crystals exhibited a residual moisture content of about 2–5%. [00104] The overall specific energy consumption of the MVR evaporation system was approximately 10 kWh per ton of water evaporated, demonstrating high energy efficiency. [00105] Notably, the system exhibited no significant scaling or fouling during continuous operation for a period of about 60 days, indicating the effectiveness of the integrated crystal trap and optimized operating conditions for suppressing lithium carbonate and salt scaling. patents.abstract: The present invention relates to an integrated process for producing high-concentration lithium hydroxide and battery-grade lithium carbonate from a lithium sulfate feed solution. The process comprises subjecting a lithium sulfate feed solution having a concentration of 150–250 g/L Li₂SO₄ to a bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) process operated at a current density of 50–100 mA/cm² and a temperature of 35–55°C. The process concurrently produces a lithium hydroxide stream having a concentration of 80–100 g/L and a sulfuric acid stream having a concentration of 115–140 g/L. The lithium hydroxide stream is directly reacted with a carbon-containing gas to produce lithium carbonate without an intermediate concentration step, while the sulfuric acid stream is recycled for internal use. The invention enables elimination of energy-intensive concentration steps, efficient utilization of crude feedstock, and integrated production of battery-grade lithium compounds in an energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable manner.
patents.complete_specification: Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION [0001] The present invention relates to electrochemical processing of lithium salts and, more particularly, to an integrated bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) process for producing high-concentration lithium hydroxide from a lithium sulfate feed solution and its direct conversion to battery-grade lithium carbonate. The invention further relates to a closed-loop system enabling simultaneous generation and internal recycling of sulfuric acid. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION [0002] Background description includes information that may be useful in understanding the present invention. It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed invention or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art. [0003] The increasing demand for lithium-ion batteries, particularly in electric vehicles and energy storage systems, has led to a growing need for high-purity lithium compounds such as lithium hydroxide and lithium carbonate. Lithium hydroxide is widely used in the manufacture of high-nickel cathode active materials, while lithium carbonate remains an essential precursor for lithium iron phosphate batteries and other applications. [0004] Conventional methods for producing lithium hydroxide and lithium carbonate suffer from several drawbacks. For example, the lime causticization process used for converting lithium carbonate to lithium hydroxide is inefficient, generates significant solid waste, and requires multiple purification steps. Electrochemical methods, including bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED), have been explored as alternatives for producing lithium hydroxide from lithium sulfate solutions. However, such methods typically operate with relatively dilute feed solutions and produce lithium hydroxide at low concentrations, often below 40 g/L, primarily due to electro-osmotic transport of water across membranes. [0005] As a result, the lithium hydroxide produced by conventional BMED processes is not suitable for direct downstream applications and requires additional energy-intensive concentration steps such as evaporation or reverse osmosis. Similarly, the sulfuric acid generated in such processes is often of low concentration and limited utility, necessitating further processing or disposal. [0006] Further, many existing processes are optimized for high-purity feedstocks and are not suitable for crude lithium sulfate solutions obtained from mineral processing or recycling streams. These limitations increase capital and operational costs and reduce overall process efficiency. [0007] Accordingly, there exists a need for an improved process that can utilize crude lithium sulfate feedstock, produce high-concentration lithium hydroxide suitable for direct conversion, generate reusable sulfuric acid, and operate in an energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable manner. OBJECTS OF THE PRESENT INVENTION [0008] Some of the objects of the present invention, which at least one embodiment herein satisfies are as listed herein below. [0009] An object of the present invention to provide a process for producing lithium hydroxide from a lithium sulfate feed solution. [00010] Another object of the present invention to provide a process capable of producing lithium hydroxide at high concentrations suitable for direct downstream processing. [00011] Another object of the present invention to eliminate intermediate concentration steps required in conventional processes. [00012] Another object of the present invention to provide a process for direct conversion of lithium hydroxide to battery-grade lithium carbonate. [00013] Another object of the present invention to simultaneously generate sulfuric acid at concentrations suitable for internal reuse. [00014] Another object of the present invention to provide a closed-loop process with recycling of sulfuric acid. [00015] Another object of the present invention to provide a process capable of utilizing crude lithium sulfate feedstock. [00016] Yet another object of the present invention to reduce energy consumption, operational complexity, and environmental impact associated with lithium processing. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [00017] This summary is provided to introduce a selection of concepts in a simplified form that is further described below in the detailed description section. This summary is not intended to identify key features or essential features of the claimed subject matter, nor is it intended to be used as an aid in determining the scope of the claimed subject matter. [00018] The present invention provides a closed-loop process for producing lithium hydroxide and lithium carbonate from a lithium sulfate feed solution. [00019] In an aspect, the process comprises providing a lithium sulfate feed solution having a suitable concentration and subjecting the feed solution to a bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) process operated under a high-concentration operating regime. The operating regime comprises a current density in the range of 50 to 100 mA/cm², a temperature in the range of 35 to 55°C, and controlled flow conditions configured to reduce concentration polarization. [00020] The BMED process concurrently produces a lithium hydroxide stream having a concentration in the range of 80 to 100 g/L and a sulfuric acid stream having a concentration in the range of 115 to 140 g/L. The lithium hydroxide stream is directly reacted with a carbon-containing gas to precipitate lithium carbonate without an intermediate concentration step, while at least a portion of the sulfuric acid stream is recycled to an upstream process. [00021] In another aspect, the invention provides a bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) system configured to carry out the process, the system comprising a membrane stack, feed tank, base compartment, acid compartment, carbonation reactor, and a recycle loop. [00022] The present invention enables production of high-concentration lithium hydroxide and sulfuric acid, eliminates energy-intensive concentration steps, facilitates direct carbonation to battery-grade lithium carbonate, and provides an integrated closed-loop process suitable for crude lithium sulfate feedstocks. [00090] In a broad aspect, the present invention provides an integrated closed-loop process (100) for producing lithium hydroxide and lithium carbonate from a lithium sulfate feedstock, as schematically illustrated in Figure 1. [000109] In Step A, a lithium sulfate feed solution is provided, wherein the lithium sulfate feed solution has a concentration in the range of 150 g/L to 250 g/L Li₂SO₄. [000116] In an embodiment, the high-concentration operating regime is selected such that electro-osmotic water transport across the membranes is reduced relative to ionic flux, thereby enabling formation of concentrated lithium hydroxide and sulfuric acid streams. [000117] In an embodiment, the BMED process concurrently produces (i) a lithium hydroxide stream having a concentration in the range of 80 to 100 g/L and a purity of at least 99.5%, and (ii) a sulfuric acid stream having a concentration in the range of 115 to 140 g/L and a purity of at least 99.9%. [000129] In Step B, the conditioned lithium sulfate feed solution is introduced into a bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) system. In certain embodiments, the BMED stack comprises a plurality of repeating cell pairs, each cell pair comprising a bipolar membrane (BPM), a cation exchange membrane (CEM), and an anion exchange membrane (AEM). In a key embodiment, the BMED system is operated under a high-concentration operating regime comprising a feed concentration of 150–250 g/L Li₂SO₄, a current density in the range of 50–100 mA/cm², and a temperature in the range of 35–55°C. In an embodiment, operation under the above regime results in concurrent production of a lithium hydroxide stream having a concentration of 80–100 g/L with a purity of at least 99.5%, and a sulfuric acid stream having a concentration of 115–140 g/L with a purity of at least 99.9%. In a further embodiment, the lithium sulfate conversion is at least 85%. [000130] In a non-limiting embodiment, the process is operated such that ion migration rate exceeds electro-osmotic water transport, thereby enabling production of lithium hydroxide at concentrations greater than 40 g/L. In certain embodiments, flow velocity (30-40 cm/s) is maintained to induce turbulent flow, boundary layer thickness is minimized, and concentration polarization is reduced. In another embodiment, the BMED stack comprises at least 10 cell pairs to enhance concentration efficiency. [000131] In Step C, the sulfuric acid stream obtained from Step B, having a concentration in the range of 115–140 g/L, is recovered. [000132] In certain embodiments, the sulfuric acid stream is directly recycled to at least one of lithium ore leaching, lithium carbonate acidulation, or ion exchange resin regeneration. In a further embodiment, the process operates as a closed-loop system with minimal external acid requirement. [000133] In Step D, the lithium hydroxide stream obtained from Step B is directly transferred to a carbonation reactor without any intermediate concentration step. In another embodiment, the carbonation reaction comprises reacting lithium hydroxide with a carbon-containing gas. In certain embodiments, the reaction is carried out at a temperature in the range of 70°C to 85°C, with controlled carbon dioxide addition and agitation. In a further embodiment, the lithium carbonate produced has a purity of at least 99.7%, a whiteness of at least 98%, and a particle size (D50) of less than or equal to 6 µm. In a non-limiting embodiment, the mother liquor is recycled to the BMED base compartment. [000134] In an embodiment, the step of directly reacting the lithium hydroxide stream with a carbon-containing gas is carried out under controlled carbonation conditions comprising a temperature in the range of 60 to 90°C, preferably 70 to 85°C. [000135] In another embodiment, the carbon-containing gas comprises carbon dioxide supplied at a controlled flow rate to regulate the rate of precipitation of lithium carbonate. [000136] In certain embodiments, the carbonation step is carried out under agitation conditions sufficient to ensure uniform mixing and controlled crystal growth. [000137] In a further embodiment, the carbonation conditions are selected to obtain lithium carbonate having a purity of at least 99.7%, whiteness of at least 98%, and a particle size (D50) of less than or equal to 6 µm. [000138] In an embodiment, the bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) process is operated such that the energy consumption is in the range of 1.5 to 2.5 kWh per kg of lithium sulfate processed. [000139] In another embodiment, the high-concentration operating regime enables reduction in overall process energy consumption by eliminating downstream concentration steps including evaporation, reverse osmosis, or secondary electrodialysis. [000140] In certain embodiments, the process achieves improved energy efficiency due to increased ionic conductivity at higher feed concentrations and reduced overall unit operations. [000141] In an embodiment, the lithium sulfate feed solution comprises one or more impurities selected from iron, aluminum, magnesium, calcium, sodium, potassium, or combinations thereof. [000142] In another embodiment, the BMED process is configured to selectively transport lithium ions in the presence of said impurities to produce a lithium hydroxide stream having a purity of at least 99.5%. [000143] In certain embodiments, the process tolerates impurity levels typically associated with crude lithium sulfate feedstock derived from mineral leaching or recycling streams without requiring extensive upstream purification. [000144] In a further embodiment, the process achieves a lithium sulfate conversion of at least 85% while maintaining product purity. TECHNICAL ADVANCEMENT AND ADVANTAGES: [000145] The present invention provides a significant technical advancement in the field of electrochemical processing of lithium salts by enabling an integrated, high-efficiency, closed-loop process for producing high-concentration lithium hydroxide and battery-grade lithium carbonate from lithium sulfate feed solutions. [000146] In an embodiment, the invention operates using a lithium sulfate feed solution having a concentration in the range of 150 g/L to 250 g/L. Operation at such high feed concentrations is counterintuitive due to increased osmotic pressure, viscosity, and potential membrane fouling. However, the present invention successfully operates under these conditions, thereby enabling process intensification and forming the basis for achieving high product concentrations and improved overall efficiency. [000147] In another embodiment, the process is specifically configured for industrial-scale applicability, enabling lithium sulfate conversion of at least 85% while producing concentrated product streams. This represents an advancement over processes that are limited to dilute feeds or laboratory-scale objectives. [000148] In a further embodiment, the bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) process directly produces a lithium hydroxide stream having a concentration in the range of 80 g/L to 100 g/L. Such concentrations are commercially significant and are achieved without the need for intermediate concentration steps. This eliminates energy-intensive operations such as evaporation, reverse osmosis, or secondary electrodialysis, thereby reducing capital and operating costs. [000149] In another embodiment, the process concurrently produces a sulfuric acid stream having a concentration in the range of 115 g/L to 140 g/L with a purity greater than 99.9%. The generation of such a high-concentration and high-purity acid stream enables direct internal recycling without further purification, thereby minimizing reagent consumption and preventing accumulation of impurities within the process loop. [000150] In certain embodiments, the BMED process is operated at a current density in the range of 50 mA/cm² to 100 mA/cm². Operation at such elevated current densities enhances ion migration rates and enables the process to overcome electro-osmotic water transport effects, thereby facilitating the production of high-concentration lithium hydroxide and sulfuric acid streams. [000151] In a further embodiment, the lithium hydroxide stream produced is directly utilized in a carbonation step without intermediate concentration. The ability to directly convert lithium hydroxide to lithium carbonate simplifies the process flow, reduces energy consumption, and improves overall process economics. [000152] In another embodiment, the process produces lithium hydroxide having a purity of at least 99.5% and lithium carbonate having a purity of at least 99.7% with a whiteness of at least 98%, directly from crude lithium sulfate feedstock. This demonstrates the robustness of the process in handling impurity-containing feedstocks while still achieving high-purity, battery-grade products. [000153] In another embodiment, the process is compatible with crude lithium sulfate feedstocks containing impurities typically associated with mineral leaching or recycling streams. The process is capable of selectively transporting lithium ions in the presence of such impurities to produce a lithium hydroxide stream of high purity. This reduces dependency on high-purity raw materials and minimizes the need for extensive upstream purification steps, thereby lowering processing costs and enhancing overall process robustness and industrial applicability. [000154] In certain embodiments, the process is configured as an integrated closed-loop system wherein sulfuric acid generated in the BMED process is recycled to upstream operations. This reduces the requirement for fresh acid input, minimizes waste generation, and enhances environmental sustainability. [000155] In a further embodiment, the invention is characterized by a specific combination of interdependent process parameters, including high feed concentration, elevated current density, controlled temperature, and integrated process configuration. This combination operates synergistically to produce high-concentration lithium hydroxide and sulfuric acid streams, enable direct carbonation, and eliminate intermediate processing steps. [000156] Accordingly, the present invention provides an integrated and optimized solution that overcomes limitations associated with dilute feed operation, low product concentrations, inefficient acid utilization, and multi-step processing, thereby offering improved energy efficiency, reduced operational complexity, and enhanced industrial applicability. EXAMPLES [000157] The present invention is further explained in the form of the following examples. However, it is to be understood that the foregoing examples are merely illustrative and are not to be taken as limitations upon the scope of the invention. Various changes and modifications to the disclosed embodiments will be apparent to those skilled in the art. Such changes and modifications may be made without departing from the scope of the invention. Example 1: High-Concentration Integrated Process [000158] A crude lithium sulfate feedstock obtained from sulfuric acid leaching of lithium-bearing minerals was subjected to feed preparation and conditioning. The crude lithium sulfate solution exhibited impurity levels as determined by ICP analysis (Table 1: ICP Analysis of Crude Lithium Sulfate Solution). The feed solution was adjusted to a concentration in the range of 150–250 g/L Li₂SO₄, preferably 180–220 g/L Li₂SO₄, by controlled dilution or evaporation. The feedstock was subjected to impurity removal by pH adjustment to precipitate metal impurities including iron, aluminum, and magnesium, followed by filtration. In certain cases, ion exchange treatment was further employed to remove divalent cations such as calcium and magnesium. The BMED system was operated under a high-concentration operating regime, wherein the feed concentration was maintained at 150–250 g/L Li₂SO₄, the current density was maintained in the range of 60–100 mA/cm², and the temperature was controlled within 35–55°C. The system was further operated under controlled flow conditions to induce turbulent flow and reduce concentration polarization. [000160] Under these operating conditions, the process resulted in simultaneous generation of a lithium hydroxide stream and a sulfuric acid stream. The lithium hydroxide stream exhibited a concentration in the range of 80–100 g/L with purity exceeding 99.5%, while the sulfuric acid stream exhibited a concentration in the range of 115–140 g/L with purity exceeding 99.9%. The overall lithium sulfate conversion was observed to be greater than 85%. The energy consumption of the system was measured to be in the range of 1.5–2.5 kWh per kg of Li₂SO₄ processed. [000161] Without any intermediate concentration step, the lithium hydroxide stream was directly transferred to a carbonation reactor, where it was reacted with carbon dioxide gas under controlled conditions. The carbonation reaction was carried out at a temperature in the range of 70–85°C with controlled CO₂ addition and agitation. The reaction resulted in the formation of lithium carbonate precipitate having a purity of at least 99.7%, whiteness of at least 98%, and particle size (D50) of less than or equal to 6 µm. The mother liquor containing residual lithium hydroxide was optionally recycled back to the BMED base compartment. [000162] The sulfuric acid stream generated during the BMED process, having a concentration of 115–140 g/L, was directly recycled to upstream process units including lithium ore leaching and ion exchange resin regeneration, thereby establishing a closed-loop system with minimal external acid requirement. [000163] This example demonstrates that operation under the defined high-concentration operating regime enables ion migration rates to exceed electro-osmotic water transport, thereby achieving lithium hydroxide concentrations significantly greater than conventional limits and enabling direct downstream processing. Example 2: Moderate Ionic Strength Feed (Comparative Example) [000164] In a comparative embodiment, a crude lithium sulfate feed solution having a concentration in the range of 90–110 g/L Li₂SO₄ was subjected to processing in a bipolar membrane electrodialysis (BMED) system without employing the high-concentration operating regime of the present invention. The system was operated at a current density in the range of 40–70 mA/cm², with energy consumption in the range of 1.2–1.8 kWh per kg of Li₂SO₄ processed. [000165] Under these conditions, the process achieved high lithium sulfate conversion efficiency exceeding 95% and produced lithium hydroxide and sulfuric acid streams with purities exceeding 99.8%. However, the lithium hydroxide concentration was limited to 30–50 g/L, and the sulfuric acid concentration was limited to 40–60 g/L. [000166] Although the purity and conversion efficiency were satisfactory, the relatively low concentrations of lithium hydroxide and sulfuric acid rendered these streams unsuitable for direct downstream utilization. In particular, the lithium hydroxide stream required additional concentration steps such as evaporation or reverse osmosis prior to carbonation, while the sulfuric acid stream was not suitable for direct internal reuse and required further processing or neutralization. [000167] This comparative example highlights the limitations of conventional BMED operation and demonstrates the inability to achieve commercially viable product concentrations without additional energy-intensive unit operations. Example 3: Direct Carbonation Using High-Concentration Lithium Hydroxide [000168] The lithium hydroxide stream obtained from the high-concentration process described in Example 1, having a concentration of 80–100 g/L, was subjected to direct carbonation without any intermediate concentration step. [000169] The lithium hydroxide solution was introduced into a carbonation reactor and reacted with carbon dioxide gas under controlled conditions. The reaction was conducted at a temperature in the range of 70–85°C, with controlled CO₂ flow rate and continuous agitation to ensure uniform precipitation. [000170] The carbonation reaction proceeded efficiently to form lithium carbonate according to the reaction: 2LiOH + CO₂ → Li₂CO₃ + H₂O [000171] The resulting lithium carbonate precipitate exhibited a purity of at least 99.7%, whiteness of at least 98%, and particle size (D50) of less than or equal to 6 µm. The precipitation was rapid and uniform due to the high initial concentration of lithium hydroxide, eliminating the need for any pre-concentration step. [000172] The mother liquor remaining after precipitation was found to contain residual lithium hydroxide and was recycled back into the process, thereby improving overall lithium recovery. patents.abstract: The present invention relates to a selective hydrometallurgical process for producing high-purity copper sulphate pentahydrate from lithium-ion battery current collector scrap. The process comprises alkaline treatment to selectively remove aluminium, followed by washing and impurity suppression, and selective oxidative leaching of copper using an acid and an oxidizing agent to obtain a copper-rich leachate. The leachate is concentrated and crystallized to produce copper sulphate pentahydrate. The process is configured such that copper constitutes the predominant dissolved metal species, thereby enabling direct crystallization without intermediate purification steps. The invention further provides a system comprising an alkaline treatment unit, a leaching reactor, a separation unit, and a crystallization unit. The process is energy-efficient, scalable, and capable of producing copper sulphate pentahydrate with a purity of at least 99.5%.
patents.complete_specification: Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION [0001] The present invention relates generally to the field of hydrometallurgical processing and recycling of battery materials. More particularly, the invention relates to a selective hydrometallurgical process for recovering copper from lithium-ion battery current collector scrap and converting the recovered copper into high-purity copper sulphate pentahydrate. The invention further relates to a system and process integration for producing copper sulphate pentahydrate with high selectivity, yield, and industrial scalability. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION [0002] Background description includes information that may be useful in understanding the present invention. It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed invention or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art. [0003] The Lithium-ion batteries are extensively used in electric vehicles, portable electronics, and energy storage systems. With increasing adoption, large volumes of end-of-life lithium-ion batteries are generated, creating a need for efficient recycling technologies. [0004] Spent lithium-ion batteries contain valuable materials including lithium, cobalt, nickel, manganese, graphite, and metallic current collectors such as copper and aluminium. Conventional recycling processes primarily focus on recovery of cathode metals, while copper is often treated as a secondary material and recovered as metallic copper through pyrometallurgical or mechanical routes. [0005] Such conventional approaches are energy-intensive, involve high-temperature processing, and often yield products of limited value. In hydrometallurgical approaches, strong acids and oxidants are used to dissolve multiple metals simultaneously, resulting in complex mixed-metal solutions that require downstream separation processes such as solvent extraction, cementation, or electrowinning. [0006] For example, processes disclosed in WO2022267419A1 involve roasting and subsequent reduction steps for metal recovery, which significantly increase energy consumption and carbon footprint. Similarly, processes such as those described in WO2022101930A1 employ multi-stage separation and solvent extraction techniques for metal recovery, thereby increasing operational complexity, water consumption, and cost. [0007] Further, known processes do not provide a selective pathway for converting copper present in lithium-ion battery current collector scrap directly into a high-value chemical product such as copper sulphate pentahydrate. The lack of selectivity leads to co-dissolution of impurity metals, making it difficult to achieve high-purity crystallized products without extensive purification steps. [0008] Accordingly, there exists a need for a selective, energy-efficient, and scalable process that enables direct conversion of copper from lithium-ion battery current collector scrap into high-purity copper sulphate pentahydrate while minimizing impurity dissolution and downstream processing requirements. OBJECTS OF THE PRESENT INVENTION [0009] Some of the objects of the present invention, which at least one embodiment herein satisfies are as listed herein below. [00010] An object of the present invention is to provide a selective hydrometallurgical process for producing copper sulphate pentahydrate from lithium-ion battery current collector scrap. [00011] Another object of the present invention is to selectively remove aluminium, black mass, and associated impurities from the feed material prior to copper leaching. [00012] Yet another object of the present invention is to provide a process that enables copper-dominant leaching, wherein copper constitutes the predominant dissolved metal species in the leachate. [00013] Still another object of the present invention is to suppress dissolution of transition metals such as cobalt, nickel, manganese, and lithium during the leaching process. [00014] A further object of the present invention is to enable direct crystallization of copper sulphate pentahydrate from the leachate without requiring intermediate purification steps such as solvent extraction, electrowinning, or cementation. [00015] Another object of the present invention is to provide a process capable of producing copper sulphate pentahydrate having a purity of at least 99.5%, preferably at least 99.9%. [00016] Yet another object of the present invention is to provide an energy-efficient and environmentally sustainable process with reduced water consumption and carbon footprint. [00017] Still another object of the present invention is to provide a process that is scalable from laboratory to industrial scale while maintaining selectivity and yield. [00018] A further object of the present invention is to provide a system configured to implement the process in an integrated and continuous or semi-continuous manner. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [00019] This summary is provided to introduce a selection of concepts in a simplified form that is further described below in the detailed description section. This summary is not intended to identify key features or essential features of the claimed subject matter, nor is it intended to be used as an aid in determining the scope of the claimed subject matter. [00020] The present invention provides a selective hydrometallurgical process for converting lithium-ion battery current collector scrap into high-purity copper sulphate pentahydrate. [00021] In an aspect, the process comprises subjecting the feed material to an alkaline treatment to selectively dissolve aluminium, followed by washing and/or acid washing to remove or suppress impurities, and thereafter selectively leaching copper using an acid in the presence of an oxidizing agent to obtain a copper-rich leachate. [00022] In another aspect, the leaching conditions are controlled such that copper constitutes at least about 95 wt% of the dissolved metal species in the leachate, thereby enabling direct crystallization. [00023] In a further aspect, the copper-rich leachate is concentrated and subjected to crystallization to obtain copper sulphate pentahydrate crystals having high purity. [00024] In yet another aspect, the invention provides a system comprising an alkaline treatment unit, a leaching reactor, a solid–liquid separation unit, and a crystallization unit, optionally including a recycle loop for mother liquor. [00025] In another aspect, the process eliminates the need for intermediate purification steps such as solvent extraction, electrowinning, or cementation, thereby simplifying processing and reducing energy consumption. The drawings illustrate the steps of the present disclosure and, together with the description, serve to explain the principles of the present disclosure. [00044] Lithium-ion battery current collector scrap: Refers to metallic scrap derived from lithium-ion batteries, comprising predominantly copper and optionally aluminium, along with associated materials including black mass, polymeric binders, and residual electrolyte components. [00045] “Black mass” as used herein refers to a mixture of cathode and anode active materials including lithium-containing metal oxides, graphite, conductive carbon, and binder residues obtained from lithium-ion batteries. [00046] “Copper-enriched solid fractions” as used refers to the solid material obtained after alkaline treatment in which aluminium and soluble impurities are substantially removed, resulting in an increased proportion of metallic copper relative to the initial feed. [00047] “Copper-dominant leachate” refers to a leach solution in which copper constitutes the predominant dissolved metal species, typically at least 95 wt% of the total dissolved metals, with remaining metals present in minor or trace amounts. [00048] “Impurity suppression” refers to process conditions or steps that reduce or limit dissolution of non-copper metals, including but not limited to cobalt, nickel, manganese, lithium, iron, and aluminium, during leaching. [00051] “Mother liquor” refers to the residual liquid remaining after crystallization of copper sulphate pentahydrate, which may contain dissolved copper and/or impurities and may be recycled within the process [00052] “Selective leaching” used herein refers to dissolution of copper preferentially over other metals under controlled chemical conditions. [00053] System or unit refers to any apparatus, reactor, vessel, or equipment configured to perform a specific function within the process, including but not limited to tanks, reactors, separators, and crystallizers. [00055] Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are extensively used in electric vehicles, portable electronics, and energy storage systems, resulting in increasing volumes of end-of-life battery waste. Such waste contains valuable materials including copper current collectors, aluminium, black mass, polymeric binders, and transition metals such as cobalt, nickel, manganese, and lithium. Conventional recycling processes primarily focus on recovery of high-value cathode metals, while copper is typically recovered as metallic copper or treated as an impurity stream. [00091] In an aspect, referring to illustrative FIG. 1, the present invention provides a process (100) for producing copper sulphate pentahydrate from lithium-ion battery current collector scrap, wherein the process comprises sequential steps of material conditioning, selective dissolution, controlled leaching, and crystallization. [00092] In an embodiment, the process (100) comprises: • providing feed material comprising lithium-ion battery current collector scrap (101); • subjecting the scrap to alkaline treatment (102); • washing and/or acid washing (103); • selective oxidative leaching (104); • solid–liquid separation (105); • concentration of leachate (106); and • crystallization of copper sulphate pentahydrate (107). [00093] Feed introduction Step (101): In an embodiment, the step (101) comprises providing a feed material comprising copper current collector scrap derived from lithium-ion batteries. The feed typically includes metallic copper in the form of foils or flakes, along with aluminium, carbonaceous black mass, polymeric binders, and trace transition metals such as cobalt, nickel, manganese, lithium, and iron. [00094] Alkaline Treatment Step (102): In an embodiment, the step (102) comprises contacting the feed material with an aqueous alkaline solution, preferably sodium hydroxide, under conditions sufficient to selectively dissolve aluminium while retaining copper in metallic form. [00095] During this step, aluminium undergoes a chemical reaction with hydroxide ions to form soluble sodium aluminate species, while hydrogen gas may be evolved. Copper, being relatively inert under these alkaline conditions, remains undissolved as a solid phase. [00096] This step results in: • conversion of aluminium impurities into soluble species, • enrichment of the solid fraction in copper content, and • partial loosening of adhered black mass and surface contaminants. [00097] Washing and/or Acid Washing (Impurity Suppression) Step (103): In an embodiment, the step (103) comprises washing the alkaline-treated solid fraction with water to remove residual alkali and soluble species. [00098] In a further embodiment, an acid washing step using sulphuric acid is carried out either prior to or after alkaline treatment. During this step, loosely bound black mass, lithium salts, and surface-associated transition metal species are partially removed or conditioned. [00099] This step does not aim for complete dissolution of impurities but instead: • reduces their reactivity in subsequent leaching, • minimizes their co-dissolution, and • stabilizes impurity phases. [000100] Thus, the step (103) functions as an impurity suppression stage rather than a full purification step. [000101] Selective Oxidative Leaching Step (104): In an embodiment, the step (104) comprises contacting the treated copper-enriched solid fraction with sulphuric acid in the presence of an oxidizing agent, preferably hydrogen peroxide. [000102] During this step, copper is oxidized from its metallic state to Cu²⁺ ions and dissolves into solution as copper sulphate. The oxidation may proceed via intermediate formation of copper oxide species, which subsequently react with sulphuric acid. [000103] Simultaneously, process conditions including acid concentration, oxidant dosage, and reaction time are controlled such that: • copper dissolution is maximized, • dissolution of transition metals is minimized, and • impurity metals remain largely in the solid residue. [000104] As a result, a copper-dominant leachate is formed, wherein copper constitutes at least 95 wt%, preferably at least 98 wt%, of total dissolved metals. [000105] Solid–Liquid Separation Step (105): In an embodiment, the step (105) comprises separating the copper-containing leachate from the solid residue using filtration, decantation, or equivalent techniques. [000106] The solid residue typically comprises: • black mass, • polymeric materials, • undissolved impurity metals, and • inert components. [000107] The separation ensures that the leachate obtained is substantially free from suspended solids and suitable for downstream concentration and crystallization. [000108] Concentration of Leachate Step (106): In an embodiment, the step (106) comprises concentrating the copper-containing leachate to increase copper ion concentration to a level suitable for crystallization. [000109] This may be achieved by controlled evaporation, resulting in: • increase in copper concentration (e.g., 190–250 g/L), • increase in solution density (e.g., 2.14–2.28 g/mL), and • attainment of supersaturation conditions required for nucleation. [000110] The concentration step is carefully controlled to avoid premature precipitation or impurity incorporation. [000111] Crystallization of Copper Sulphate Pentahydrate Step (107): In an embodiment, the step (107) comprises crystallizing copper sulphate pentahydrate from the concentrated leachate. [000112] Crystallization may be achieved by: • controlled cooling, and/or • controlled evaporation at temperatures of about 30 °C to 45 °C. [000113] During this step: • supersaturation leads to nucleation of crystals, • crystal growth occurs under controlled conditions, and • impurities remain largely in the mother liquor due to prior suppression. [000114] The resulting crystals are: • well-defined in size and morphology, and • exhibit high purity (≥99.5%, preferably ≥99.9%). [000115] The mother liquor may be partially recycled to earlier stages of the process to enhance recovery and reduce waste. [000116] In an embodiment, the process further comprises step (108) comprises drying the crystallized copper sulphate pentahydrate obtained from step (107) to remove surface moisture and obtain a stable, free-flowing solid product. [000117] In an embodiment, the crystallized product separated from the mother liquor is subjected to drying using conventional drying techniques including tray drying, rotary drying, vacuum drying, or fluidized bed drying. [000118] In another embodiment, drying is carried out under conditions sufficient to remove residual surface moisture without causing decomposition or phase change of copper sulphate pentahydrate. [000119] In a further embodiment, the drying step improves: • product stability, • handling characteristics, and • storage life of the copper sulphate pentahydrate crystals. Example 1: Laboratory-Scale Processing (100 g Feed) [000189] In an example, 100 g of lithium-ion battery current collector scrap, previously washed and comprising predominantly copper along with aluminium, black mass (BM), plastic components, and trace transition metals, was subjected to the process described herein. [000190] The feed material was placed in a reaction vessel, such as a 2 L beaker, and subjected to alkaline treatment using an aqueous basic solution under stirring conditions. Various alkaline reagents including sodium hydroxide (NaOH), potassium hydroxide (KOH), sodium carbonate (Na2CO3), sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3), magnesium hydroxide (Mg(OH)2), calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2), barium hydroxide (Ba(OH)2), and ammonium hydroxide (NH4OH) were evaluated for their effectiveness in removing aluminium. Sodium hydroxide exhibited superior performance in selectively dissolving aluminium. Accordingly, the alkaline treatment was carried out using sodium hydroxide solution under continuous stirring for about 10–12 hours at ambient temperature. [000191] During this step, aluminium present in the scrap reacted with the alkaline solution to form soluble sodium aluminate species, while copper remained substantially undissolved in metallic form. The reaction mixture was subsequently subjected to solid–liquid separation, such as filtration, to remove the alkaline liquor containing dissolved aluminium. [000192] The remaining solid fraction, comprising copper scrap along with residual black mass (BM) and plastic components, was then subjected to leaching studies using different acids, including sulphuric acid, nitric acid, hydrochloric acid, acetic acid, and oxalic acid. Among these, sulphuric acid was found to be most suitable for selective copper dissolution. [000193] Further, oxidative leaching was carried out by adding sulphuric acid in an amount of about 80–90 mL, followed by addition of an oxidizing agent. Various oxidizing agents including hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), oxygen (O2), potassium permanganate (KMnO4), potassium dichromate (K2Cr2O7), perchloric acid (HClO4), and sodium hypochlorite (NaClO) were evaluated. Observed that hydrogen peroxide exhibited superior performance in promoting selective dissolution of copper. Accordingly, hydrogen peroxide was added in an amount of about 70–80 mL to the acidic slurry. [000194] The reaction mixture was maintained under stirring for about 1–2 hours, during which copper was oxidized and dissolved as Cu²⁺ ions forming copper sulphate in solution. The process conditions were such that dissolution of impurity metals was minimized. [000195] Following leaching, the reaction mixture was subjected to filtration to separate the copper-containing leachate from the solid residue. The solid residue, comprising black mass (BM), plastic materials, and undissolved impurities, was further washed with hot demineralized (DM) water to recover any entrained copper-containing solution. [000196] The combined filtrate and washings constituted the copper sulphate leachate. [000205] The feed material was subjected to an alkaline treatment step in a suitable reactor vessel configured for bulk processing. [000208] The conditioned solid material was then subjected to oxidative leaching using sulphuric acid in the presence of hydrogen peroxide. The leaching operation was carried out in a leaching reactor equipped with agitation and controlled reagent dosing systems. [000209] During this step, sulphuric acid was introduced to form an acidic slurry, followed by controlled addition of hydrogen peroxide as an oxidizing agent. [000217] The mother liquor remaining after crystallization was partially recycled back to the leaching or evaporation stages to improve overall copper recovery and reduce effluent generation. patents.abstract: An integrated hydrometallurgical process for recovery of metals from spent lithium-ion battery black mass is disclosed. The process comprises pre-treatment including removal of interfering species, followed by leaching to dissolve metal values, solid-liquid separation to remove insoluble components, and sequential recovery of metals through electrowinning, controlled precipitation, and solvent extraction. Manganese is recovered as manganese dioxide, cobalt is recovered as metal powder through precipitation and reduction, lithium is recovered as lithium carbonate, copper and zinc are recovered as metallic products, and magnesium is recovered as a carbonate compound. The process further includes regeneration of chemical reagents from spent process streams using a membrane-based electro-separation system, enabling reuse of acids and bases within the process. The integrated configuration allows selective multi-metal recovery with high efficiency while minimizing chemical consumption and operating under a closed-loop system with substantially zero liquid discharge.
patents.complete_specification: Description:FIELD OF THE INVENTION [0001] The present invention relates to the field of recycling of spent lithium-ion batteries. More particularly, the invention relates to an integrated hydrometallurgical process for selective recovery of metals including lithium, cobalt, manganese, copper and zinc from battery black mass through a combination of leaching, solvent extraction, electrowinning, precipitation, and reduction processes, along with reagent regeneration to enable closed-loop operation. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION [0002] Background description includes information that may be useful in understanding the present invention. It is not an admission that any of the information provided herein is prior art or relevant to the presently claimed invention or that any publication specifically or implicitly referenced is prior art. [0003] With the increasing demand for electric vehicles, portable electronics, and energy storage systems, the usage of lithium-ion batteries has grown significantly in recent years. This widespread adoption has led to a corresponding increase in the generation of spent lithium-ion batteries, which contain substantial quantities of valuable metals such as lithium, cobalt, manganese, copper, and zinc. [0004] Recovery of these metals is essential not only from an economic perspective but also for environmental sustainability. However, conventional recycling techniques, including pyrometallurgical and hydrometallurgical processes, suffer from several limitations. These include high energy consumption, excessive use of chemical reagents, generation of large volumes of secondary waste streams, and incomplete recovery of valuable metals. In particular, separation of closely associated metals such as cobalt and manganese remains a significant technical challenge, and lithium is often lost in downstream raffinate streams. [0005] Existing hydrometallurgical processes typically involve acid leaching followed by precipitation or solvent extraction. However, such processes generally lack integration between unit operations and do not provide for efficient regeneration and reuse of reagents. As a result, these processes require substantial amounts of fresh chemicals and generate environmentally burdensome effluents. [0006] In general, conventional processes are limited to partial recovery of metals and are not designed for efficient multi-metal recovery from complex black mass compositions. Furthermore, such processes do not incorporate reagent recycling mechanisms, leading to continuous consumption of fresh chemicals. Lithium, in particular, is frequently not recovered effectively and is often lost in raffinate streams. Additionally, conventional processes generate large volumes of wastewater due to the absence of closed-loop operation. The process design in such systems is typically fragmented, involving multiple independent unit operations rather than a unified and integrated flowsheet. [0007] Accordingly, there exists a need for an improved hydrometallurgical process that enables integrated recovery of multiple metals from spent lithium-ion battery black mass, ensures efficient reagent utilization through regeneration and reuse, minimizes wastewater generation through closed-loop operation, and provides a single, integrated process flowsheet for improved operational efficiency, sustainability, and economic viability. OBJECTS OF THE PRESENT INVENTION [0008] Some of the objects of the present invention, which at least one embodiment herein satisfies are as listed herein below. [0009] An object of the present invention is to provide an integrated hydrometallurgical process for recovery of metals from spent lithium-ion battery black mass. [00010] Another object of the present invention is to provide a process for selective recovery of lithium, cobalt, manganese, copper, and zinc in high purity forms. [00011] Still another object of the present invention is to provide a process that enables sequential and selective separation of metals to improve recovery efficiency and product quality. [00012] Yet another object of the present invention is to provide a process that minimizes chemical consumption through internal regeneration and reuse of reagents. [00013] A further object of the present invention is to provide a process incorporating reagent regeneration using a membrane-based electrochemical system. [00014] Another object of the present invention is to provide a process capable of producing value-added products including metallic copper, manganese dioxide, cobalt metal, lithium carbonate, and metallic zinc. [00015] Still another object of the present invention is to provide a process that operates under a closed-loop configuration with substantially zero liquid discharge. [00016] Yet another object of the present invention is to provide a process that reduces environmental impact associated with recycling of spent lithium-ion batteries. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION [00017] This summary is provided to introduce a selection of concepts in a simplified form that is further described below in the detailed description section. This summary is not intended to identify key features or essential features of the claimed subject matter, nor is it intended to be used as an aid in determining the scope of the claimed subject matter. [00018] In an aspect, the present invention provides an integrated hydrometallurgical process for recovery of metals from spent lithium-ion battery black mass. [00019] In an embodiment, the process comprises a sequence of steps including pre-treatment to remove interfering species, leaching of metal values into an aqueous phase, separation of insoluble components, selective recovery of metals through electrochemical, precipitation, and liquid-liquid extraction techniques, and conversion of recovered metals into value-added products. [00020] In another embodiment, the process includes sequential separation of metals through controlled pH adjustment and selective extraction, enabling efficient isolation of individual metals from complex mixtures. [00021] In a further embodiment, the process comprises multiple recovery pathways including electrowinning, solvent extraction, precipitation, oxidation, and reduction, thereby enabling recovery of metals in different forms depending on desired end use. [00022] In an embodiment, the process further comprises a reagent regeneration stage configured to recover and recycle chemical reagents from spent process streams. [00023] In another embodiment, the regenerated reagents are reused in upstream process steps, thereby reducing the requirement for fresh chemical inputs. [00024] In a further embodiment, the process is configured as an integrated system wherein intermediate streams are internally recycled and reused. [00025] In an embodiment, the process enables recovery of lithium, cobalt, manganese, copper and zinc with high efficiency while minimizing waste generation. [00026] In another embodiment, the process operates under a closed-loop configuration with substantially zero liquid discharge. [00027] Various objects, features, aspects and advantages of the inventive subject matter will become more apparent from the following detailed description of preferred embodiments. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF DRAWINGS [00028] The accompanying drawings are included to provide a further understanding of the present disclosure and are incorporated in and constitute a part of this specification. The drawings illustrate the steps of the present disclosure and, together with the description, serve to explain the principles of the present disclosure. [00029] FIG. 1 illustrates a schematic flow diagram of an integrated hydrometallurgical process for recovery of metals from spent lithium-ion battery black mass, comprising magnesium washing, leaching, solid-liquid separation, copper electrowinning, impurity precipitation, manganese solvent extraction and oxidation, cobalt solvent extraction and recovery, lithium precipitation, zinc recovery, and reagent regeneration through bipolar membrane electrodialysis, along with associated process streams and recycle loops.
