patents.abstract: The present invention provides a positive electrode for a lithium-ion secondary battery which can suppress the generation of cracks and wrinkles in a positive electrode active material layer. This positive electrode for a lithium-ion secondary battery is characterized by comprising a current collector and a positive electrode active material layer provided on the current collector, wherein: the positive electrode active material layer contains lithium iron phosphate particles, a latex-derived aqueous polymer binder, and carboxymethyl cellulose sodium or carboxymethyl cellulose calcium; the aqueous polymer binder and the carboxymethyl cellulose sodium or carboxymethyl cellulose calcium form a binder composite; and the elastic modulus of the binder composite is in the range of 30-100 MPa.
patents.complete_specification: TECHNICAL FIELD [0001] The present invention relates to a positive electrode for a lithium-ion 5 secondary battery and a lithium-ion secondary battery. BACKGROUND ART [0002] A positive electrode active material layer of a lithium ion battery is 10 usually produced by applying a slurry containing positive electrode active material particles, a PVdF-based binder, N-methylpyrrolidone, and a conductive agent onto a current collector, and drying the applied layer. However, Nmethylpyrrolidone is included in a list of restricted substances under the REACH Regulation due to concerns about its toxicity. 15 As a method for producing a positive electrode active material layer without using N-methylpyrrolidone, there is known a method in which a slurry including positive electrode active material particles, an aqueous binder, a conductive agent, and water is applied onto a current collector and the resulting coating layer is dried (see, for example, Patent Literature 1). 20 PRIOR ART DOCUMENT PATENT DOCUMENT [0003] Patent Document 1: Jpn. Pat. Appln. KOKAI Publication No. 2017-25 091789 SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION PROBLEMS TO BE SOLVED BY THE INVENTION [0004] 30 However, when a conventional positive electrode active material slurry using water as a dispersion medium is thickly applied onto a current collector and 3 the coating layer is dried, cracks and wrinkles occur in the positive electrode active material layer (such as a positive electrode active material layer having a thickness of 150 μm or more). When cracks occur in the positive electrode active material layer, the positive electrode active material layer is prone to peel from the 5 current collector, which is disadvantageous for producing a battery. Further, when wrinkles occur in the positive electrode active material layer, distortion occurs in the positive electrode, which is disadvantageous for producing a battery. The present invention has been made in view of such circumstances and provides a positive electrode for a lithium-ion secondary battery that can suppress 10 the occurrence of a crack or wrinkle in the positive electrode active material layer. SOLUTIONS TO THE PROBLEMS [0005] The present invention provides a positive electrode for a lithium-ion 15 secondary battery, the positive electrode including a current collector and a positive electrode active material layer provided on the current collector, the positive electrode active material layer including lithium iron phosphate particles, an aqueous polymer binder derived from latex, and CMC (sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or calcium carboxymethyl cellulose), the aqueous polymer binder and 20 the CMC constituting a binder composite, and the binder composite having an elastic modulus within a range of 30 to 100 MPa. In addition, the present invention also provides a lithium-ion secondary battery that includes the positive electrode of the present invention, a negative electrode, a separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte. 25 EFFECTS OF THE INVENTION [0006] According to the present invention, occurrence of a crack or wrinkle in the positive electrode active material layer can be suppressed, and peeling of the 4 positive electrode active material layer from the current collector can also be suppressed. According to the present invention, the thickness of the positive electrode active material layer can be increased, whereby the amount of positive electrode 5 active material included in the lithium-ion secondary battery can be increased, resulting in an increase in battery capacity. The lithium-ion secondary battery including the positive electrode of the present invention can exhibit a large battery capacity. This has been demonstrated by experiments conducted by the present inventors. 10 BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS [0007] FIG. 1 (a) is a schematic plan view of a positive electrode for a lithiumion secondary battery according to an embodiment of the present invention, and 15 FIG. 1 (b) is a schematic cross-sectional view of the positive electrode taken along a broken line A-A in FIG. 1 (a). FIG. 2 is a schematic cross-sectional view of a lithium-ion secondary battery according to an embodiment of the present invention. FIG. 3 is a schematic structural view of an electrode assembly included 20 in the lithium-ion secondary battery according to an embodiment of the present invention. EMBODIMENT OF THE INVENTION [0008] 25 Hereinafter, an embodiment of the present invention will be described with reference to the drawings. The configuration shown in the drawings and the following description is just an example, and the scope of the present invention is not limited to the configuration shown in the drawings or the following description. 5 A positive electrode 5 for a lithium-ion secondary battery according to the present embodiment includes a current collector 3 and a positive electrode active material layer 2 provided on the current collector 3, the positive electrode active material layer 2 includes lithium iron phosphate particles, an aqueous 5 polymer binder derived from latex, and CMC (sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or calcium carboxymethyl cellulose), the aqueous polymer binder and the CMC constitute a binder composite, and the binder composite has an elastic modulus within a range of 30 to 100 MPa. A lithium-ion secondary battery 30 according to the present embodiment 10 includes the positive electrode 5 according to the present embodiment, a negative electrode 32, a separator 34, and a non-aqueous electrolyte 15. [0009] The positive electrode 5 for a lithium-ion secondary battery is the positive electrode 5 included in the lithium-ion secondary battery 30 or the 15 positive electrode 5 used for producing the lithium-ion secondary battery 30. The positive electrode 5 for a lithium-ion secondary battery includes the positive electrode current collector 3 and the porous positive electrode active material layer 2 provided on the positive electrode current collector 3. The positive electrode current collector 3 is a sheet serving as a substrate 20 on which the positive electrode active material layer 2 is to be provided, and the positive electrode current collector 3 is a conductor that electrically connects a positive electrode connection member 13 and the positive electrode active material layer 2 to each other. The positive electrode current collector 3 is, for example, an aluminum foil. The positive electrode connection member 13 is 25 electrically connected to an external connection terminal 18a. The positive electrode active material layer 2 may be provided on one side of the positive electrode current collector 3 or may be provided on both sides of the positive electrode current collector 3. 6 [0010] The positive electrode active material layer 2 is a layer containing a positive electrode active material. A thickness of the positive electrode active material layer 2 (after pressing) may be 150 μm or more. This can increase the 5 amount of the positive electrode active material included in the positive electrode 5, thereby increasing battery capacity of the lithium-ion secondary battery 30. [0011] The positive electrode active material layer 2 includes the lithium iron 10 phosphate particles serving as a positive electrode active material, the latexderived aqueous polymer binder, and CMC. In addition, the positive electrode active material layer 2 can include a conductive agent. The aqueous polymer binder and CMC constitute the binder composite. The lithium iron phosphate particles are particles of lithium iron 15 phosphate (LiFePO4) serving as the positive electrode active material. The lithium iron phosphate particles may have a conductive film on the surface. This can improve conductivity of the surfaces of the fine particles on which an intercalation reaction is progressing, and can reduce the internal resistance of the positive electrode 5. The conductive film is, for example, a carbon film. The lithium iron 20 phosphate particles may be included in the positive electrode active material layer 2 as secondary particles. The secondary particles of lithium iron phosphate can have an average particle size of 10 μm or more and 60 μm or less. The average particle size can be calculated by measuring particle sizes of 100 secondary particles randomly selected in a cross-sectional photograph of the 25 positive electrode active material layer 2 and averaging these particle sizes. [0012] The conductive agent is, for example, fine particles of furnace black, acetylene black, hard carbon, and soft carbon. By containing the conductive agent, 7 the positive electrode active material layer 2 can improve conductivity and reduce the internal resistance of the positive electrode 5. [0013] The latex-derived aqueous polymer binder is a polymer binder that can 5 be colloidally dispersed in an aqueous dispersion medium. The aqueous polymer binder constitutes the binder composite together with CMC. The aqueous polymer binder is, for example, an acrylic polymer binder, styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR), or the like. By using such an aqueous polymer binder, it is possible to use water or an aqueous solution as the dispersion medium for the positive electrode 10 active material slurry used for forming the positive electrode active material layer 2. A glass transition temperature Tg of a polymer compound serving as the aqueous polymer binder is, for example, 20°C or less, preferably 10°C or less, and more preferably 0°C or less. This allows the aqueous polymer binder to exhibit flexibility. 15 Inclusion of the aqueous polymer binder in the positive electrode active material layer 2 can suppress peeling of the positive electrode active material layer 2 from the positive electrode current collector 3 and cracking of the positive electrode active material layer 2. [0014] 20 An acrylic rubber included in the acrylic polymer binder has a specific gravity of 1.1. Hardness of the acrylic rubber measured in accordance with JIS standards ranges from 40 to 90. A tensile strength of the acrylic rubber is 70 to 120 kg/cm2 , an elongation of the acrylic rubber is 100 to 600%, and volume resistivity of the acrylic rubber is 108 to 1010 Ω/cm. 25 Styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR) has a specific gravity of 0.94. Hardness of the SBR measured in accordance with JIS standards ranges from 30 to 100. A tensile strength of the SBR is 50 to 200 kg/cm2 , an elongation of the SBR is 100 to 800%, and volume resistivity of the SBR is 1010 to 1015 Ω/cm. 8 [0015] CMC (sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or calcium carboxymethyl cellulose) functions as a binder for the positive electrode active material layer 2 and is also a substance capable of controlling the viscosity of the positive 5 electrode active material slurry used for forming the positive electrode active material layer 2. CMC constitutes the binder composite together with the aqueous polymer binder. By controlling the type and amount of CMC, the flexibility, peel strength, and the like of the positive electrode active material layer 2 can be adjusted. Also, inclusion of CMC in the positive electrode active material slurry 10 can increase the viscosity of the positive electrode active material slurry and enable the positive electrode active material layer 2 to have a uniform thickness. As a result, the positive electrode active material slurry can be applied in a thick coating, and the positive electrode active material layer 2 having a large thickness (for example, a thickness of 150 μm or more (after pressing)) can be formed. 15 [0016] The binder composite composed of the aqueous polymer binder and CMC in the positive electrode active material layer 2 has an elastic modulus ranging from 30 to 100 MPa, and the upper limit is preferably 85 MPa. By setting the elastic modulus of the binder composite within the aforementioned range, a 20 favorable positive electrode active material layer 2 can be formed. When the elastic modulus of the binder composite exceeds 85 MPa, formation of a flexible positive electrode active material layer becomes difficult. Further, when the elastic modulus of the binder composite is less than 30 MPa, problems arise in maintaining the shape of the positive electrode active material layer 2. When the 25 elastic modulus of the binder composite was 25 MPa, portions of the electrode after drying that were in contact with each other were transferred during roll winding, resulting in non-uniform thickness of the positive electrode active material layer 2. 9 The elastic modulus of the binder composite composed of the aqueous polymer binder and CMC included in the positive electrode active material layer 2 can be measured, for example, by preparing a binder composite having the same composition as that contained in the positive electrode active material layer 2 and 5 performing a tensile test on the prepared binder composite. [0017] The binder composite in the positive electrode active material layer 2 exhibits an elongation in the elastic region of 10% or more. By setting the elongation in the elastic region to this range 10% or more, a favorable positive 10 electrode active material layer 2 can be formed. When the elongation is less than 10%, cracking and peeling are likely to occur. Although there is no particular upper limit for the elongation, it is preferably 30% or less. [0018] The positive electrode active material layer 2 can be formed, for 15 example, by mixing and kneading the lithium iron phosphate particles, the conductive agent, a latex of the polymer binder (an aqueous emulsion in which a polymer serving as a binder is dispersed in a colloidal state), CMC, and water to prepare the positive electrode active material slurry, applying the slurry onto the positive electrode current collector 3, and drying the coating layer. Further, the 20 positive electrode active material layer 2 may be pressed. In the pressing treatment, for example, pressure may be applied to the positive electrode active material layer 2 such that a porosity of the positive electrode active material layer 2 falls within a range of 10% to 40%. [0019] 25 A negative electrode 32 is an electrode including a porous negative electrode active material layer 36. The negative electrode active material layer 36 is, for example, a porous layer including a negative electrode active material provided on a sheet-shaped negative electrode current collector 38. The negative electrode current collector 38 is electrically connected to a negative electrode 10 connection member 14. The negative electrode connection member 14 is electrically connected to an external connection terminal 18b. The negative electrode current collector 38 is, for example, a copper foil. The negative electrode active material is a substance that is directly 5 involved in the transfer of electrons accompanying charge transfer in the negative electrode. The negative electrode active material is, for example, graphite, partially graphitized carbon, hard carbon, soft carbon, lithium titanate (LTO), or a Sn alloy. The negative electrode active material layer 36 can include one or more of these negative electrode active materials, either alone or in combination. 10 [0020] The separator 34 has a sheet shape and is disposed between the positive electrode 5 and the negative electrode 32. Further, the separator 34 can configure, together with the positive electrodes 5 and the negative electrodes 32, an electrode assembly 22 as shown in FIG. 3. By providing the separator 34, it is possible to 15 prevent a short-circuit current from flowing between the positive electrode 5 and the negative electrode 32. There is no particular limitation on the separator 34 if a short-circuit current can be prevented from flowing and if ions conducting between the positive electrode and the negative electrode can pass through the separator 10, and a 20 microporous film of polyolefin, a cellulose sheet, or an aramid sheet can be used, for example. In addition, the separator 34 may be a nonwoven fabric including at least one of cellulose fiber, polyester fiber, polypropylene fiber, polyacrylonitrile fiber, and polyethylene terephthalate fiber. [0021] 25 As shown in FIG. 3, an electrode assembly 22 may have a structure in which a plurality of positive electrodes 5 and a plurality of negative electrodes 32 are stacked such that the positive electrodes 5 and the negative electrodes 32 are alternately disposed. In addition, the electrode assembly 22 may have a structure 11 in which the separator 34 is disposed between the adjacent positive electrode 5 and negative electrode 32. [0022] As the solvent for the non-aqueous electrolyte 15, carbonates, lactones, 5 ethers, esters, ionic liquids, and the like can be used, and two or more of these solvents can also be mixed and used. In particular, a cyclic carbonate and a chain carbonate of these solvents are preferably mixed and used. The non-aqueous electrolyte 15 is, for example, a solution in which a lithium salt solute such as LiCF3SO3, LiAsF6, LiClO4, LiBF4, LiPF6, LiBOB, LiN(CF3SO2)2, or 10 LiN(C2F5SO2) is dissolved in an organic solvent. If necessary, additives such as VC (vinylene carbonate), PS (propane sultone), VEC (vinyl ethyl carbonate), PRS (propene sultone), and a flame retardant may be blended alone or in combination of two or more. [0023] 15 A battery case 11 is a battery outer casing that houses the electrode assembly 22 (including the positive electrode 5, the negative electrode 32, and the separator 34) and the non-aqueous electrolyte 15. The battery case 11 may be formed in a pouch shape by welding a laminate film at a welding portion. In this case, the lithium-ion secondary battery 30 is a pouch battery. Alternatively, the 20 battery case 11 may be a metal case or a hard resin case. The battery case 11 may have a lid member 12. [0024] Measurement of Elastic Modulus and Elongation, and Production of Positive Electrode 25 (Test Method) The elastic modulus and elongation of the binder composite were measured in accordance with JIS K 7127 (tensile test). A sample piece prepared was set on the arms of a tensile testing machine having an arm spacing of 5 to 10 mm, and a tensile test was performed at a pulling 12 speed of 5 mm/min. Based on the measurement results, a graph was prepared using load as the vertical axis and displacement as the horizontal axis, and the vertical and horizontal axes were converted into stress (load/cross-sectional area) and elongation (displacement/arm spacing), respectively, to obtain an S–S curve. 5 The elastic modulus was calculated from the initial slope of the S–S curve, and the elongation in the elastic region was determined from the point of deviation from linearity of the curve. [0025] (Production of Sample Pieces) 10 A binder, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), and pure water (dispersion medium) were kneaded to prepare binder composite solutions for Samples 1 to 9, 14, and 15. Further, CMC and a dispersion medium were kneaded to prepare binder solutions for Samples 10 to 13. The kneaded binder composite solution or binder solution was applied onto a PET sheet using a bar coater (Gap: 15 1 mm), and the coating layer was dried at 95°C to produce a binder composite or a binder body. The drying condition for the coating layer is preferably close to the drying condition for the coating layer of the positive electrode active material slurry, and is preferably 80 to 110°C. The binder composite or the binder body used in the present measurement was obtained by drying the coating film at 95°C 20 and then further drying the coating film under vacuum for 8 hours. The dried binder composite or binder body was peeled from the PET sheet and cut into an appropriate size to produce a sample piece. Tables 1 and 2 show the types of the binder and CMC and the weight ratio between the binder and CMC after drying. Tables 1 and 2 also show the width, length, and thickness values of the sample 25 piece. The effective sample length is the arm spacing at the time when a tensile load starts to be applied to the sample piece. The sample piece including only the binder and not including CMC could not be produced. 13 [0026] (Positive Electrode) Positive electrodes of Samples 1 to 15 corresponding to the binder composites or binder bodies of Samples 1 to 15 were produced. Specifically, 5 lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) powder (90 parts by weight), a conductive agent (10 parts by weight of acetylene black), CMC, the binder, and pure water (dispersion medium) were kneaded to prepare positive electrode active material slurries for Samples 1 to 9, 14, and 15. Further, lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4) powder (90 parts by weight), the conductive agent (10 parts by weight of 10 acetylene black), CMC, and pure water (dispersion medium) were kneaded to prepare positive electrode active material slurries for Samples 10 to 13. As the binder and CMC, those shown in Tables 1 and 2 were used. Further, the CMC and the binder were added to the mixture such that the ratio (a:b) of the weight a of the solid content of CMC to the weight b of the solid content of the binder was the 15 weight ratio shown in Tables 1 and 2. The prepared positive electrode active material slurry was applied onto aluminum foil (current collector), and the coating film was dried to prepare the positive electrodes of Samples 1 to 15. [0027] [Table 1] 14 15 [0028] [Table 2] [0029] 5 As the CMC, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) BSH6 manufactured by DKS Co. Ltd. (degree of etherification: 0.65 to 0.75; viscosity of a 1% aqueous CMC solution at 25°C: 3000 to 4000 mPa*s; abbreviation: BSH6), CMC BSH12 manufactured by DKS Co. Ltd. (average degree of polymerization: 10 1600 to 1800; average molecular weight: 330,000 to 360,000; degree of etherification: 0.65 to 0.75; viscosity of a 1% aqueous CMC solution at 25°C: 6000 to 8000 mPa*s; abbreviation: BSH12), CMC EP manufactured by DKS Co. Ltd. (degree of etherification: 0.90 to 0.96; viscosity of a 1% aqueous CMC solution at 25°C: 2500 mPa*s or more; 15 abbreviation: EP), or CMC F350HC manufactured by Nippon Paper Industries Co., Ltd. (average degree of polymerization: 1400 (F300HC); average molecular weight: 330,000 (F300HC); degree of etherification: 0.8 to 1.0; viscosity of a 1% aqueous CMC solution at 25°C: 2500 to 4000 mPa*s; abbreviation: F350HC) was used. 20 [0030] As the binder, an acrylic polymer binder AXA391 manufactured by Zeon Corporation (latex; active ingredient concentration: 40 wt%; glass transition temperature (Tg): 16 −35°C; pH: 7 to 9; B-type viscosity: 5 to 50 cP; average particle size: 180 μm; particle size distribution: peak at 170 μm (100 to 500 μm); abbreviation: AXA391), an acrylic polymer binder BEVEL012 manufactured by TOYO INK CO., 5 LTD. (latex; active ingredient concentration: 40.3 wt; glass transition temperature (Tg): −25°C; particle size distribution: peaks at 15 μm and 0.16 μm; abbreviation: BEVEL012), a styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR) XG4015 manufactured by NIPPON A&L INC. (latex; active ingredient concentration: 48.3 wt%; glass transition temperature: 10 −10°C; pH: 7.3; B-type viscosity: 68 cP; particle size distribution: peak at 150 μm (100 to 250 μm); abbreviation: XG4015), or an SBR AL1002 manufactured by NIPPON A&L INC. (latex; active ingredient concentration: 48.3 wt%; glass transition temperature: 45°C; pH: 6.4; B-type viscosity: 148 cP; particle size distribution: peak at 130 μm (80 to 15 200 μm); abbreviation: AL1002) was used. [0031] (Sample 1: Working Example) The binder composite formed using the slurry of Sample 1 including XG4015 (SBR) as the binder and BSH6 as CMC had an elastic modulus in the 20 range of 30 MPa to 85 MPa, and an elongation in the elastic region of 10% or more. In addition, a positive electrode active material layer (thickness: 200 μm) was produced using the positive electrode active material slurry of Sample 1 corresponding to the binder composite of Sample 1. As a result, no cracks or wrinkles were observed in the positive electrode active material layer. 25 [0032] (Samples 2 and 3: Comparative Examples) The binder composite formed using the slurry of Sample 2 or 3 including XG4015 (SBR) as the binder and F350HC or EP as CMC had an elastic modulus of 100 MPa or more, and an elongation in the elastic region of 10% or less. In 17 addition, a positive electrode active material layer (thickness: 200 μm) was produced using the positive electrode active material slurry of Sample 2 or 3 corresponding to the binder composite of Sample 2 or 3, respectively. As a result, cracks were observed in the positive electrode active material layer. This is 5 considered to be attributable to the excessively high elastic modulus and excessively low elongation of the binder composite. In addition, agglomerates were observed in the positive electrode active material layers formed using the slurries of Samples 1 to 3. [0033] 10 (Samples 4, 5, and 6: Working Examples) The binder composite formed using the slurry of Sample 4, 5, or 6 including BEVEL012 (acrylic polymer binder) as the binder and BSH6, F350HC, or EP as CMC had an elastic modulus in the range of 30 MPa to 85 MPa, and an elongation in the elastic region of 10% or more. In addition, positive electrode 15 active material layers (thickness: 200 μm) were produced using the positive electrode active material slurries of Samples 4, 5, and 6 corresponding to the binder composites of Sample 4, 5, and 6, respectively. As a result, no cracks or wrinkles were observed in the positive electrode active material layers. In addition, there was little variation in the thicknesses of the positive 20 electrode active material layers formed using the slurries of Samples 4 to 6. [0034] (Samples 7, 8, and 9: Working Examples) The binder composite formed using the slurry of Sample 7, 8, or 9 including AXA391 (acrylic polymer binder) as the binder and BSH6, F350HC, or 25 EP as CMC had an elastic modulus in the range of 30 MPa to 85 MPa, and an elongation in the elastic region of 10% or more. In addition, positive electrode active material layers (thickness: 200 μm) were produced using the positive electrode active material slurries of Samples 7, 8, and 9 corresponding to the 18 binder composites of Samples 7, 8, and 9, respectively. As a result, no cracks or wrinkles were observed in the positive electrode active material layers. In addition, there was little variation in the thicknesses of the positive electrode active material layers formed using the slurries of Samples 7 to 9. 5 [0035] (Samples 10, 11, 12, and 13: Comparative Examples) The binder body formed using the slurry of Sample 10, 11, 12, or 13, which included no binder and included BSH6, F350HC, EP, or BSH12 as CMC, had an elastic modulus of 100 MPa or more. In addition, positive electrode active 10 material layers (thickness: 200 μm) were produced using the positive electrode active material slurries of Samples 10, 11, 12 and 13 corresponding to the binder composites of Samples 10, 11, 12 and 13, respectively. As a result, cracks were observed in the positive electrode active material layers. This is considered to be attributable to the excessively high elastic modulus of the binder composite. 15 [0036] (Sample 14: Comparative Example) The binder composite formed using the slurry of Sample 14, which was prepared such that the ratio (a:b) of the solid-content weight a of BSH6 as CMC to the solid-content weight b of AXA391 as the binder was 1:1, had an elastic 20 modulus of 100 MPa or more and an elongation of 10% or more. In addition, a positive electrode active material layer (thickness: 200 μm) was produced using the positive electrode active material slurry of Sample 14 corresponding to the binder composite of Sample 14. As a result, cracks were observed in the positive electrode active material layer. This is considered to be attributable to the 25 excessively high elastic modulus of the binder composite. [0037] (Sample 15: Comparative Example) The binder composite formed using the slurry of Sample 15 including AL1002 (SBR) as the binder and BSH6 as CMC had an elastic modulus of 19 100 MPa or more, and an elongation in the elastic region of 10% or less. In addition, a positive electrode active material layer (thickness: 200 μm) was produced using the positive electrode active material slurry of Sample 15 corresponding to the binder composite of Sample 15. As a result, cracks were 5 observed in the positive electrode active material layer. This is considered to be attributable to the excessively high elastic modulus and excessively low elongation of the binder composite. [0038] In addition, in the sample in which the elastic modulus of the binder 10 composite was 25 MPa, when the corresponding positive electrode after drying was wound using a roll, the contacting positive electrode active material layer was transferred, resulting in non-uniform thickness of the positive electrode active material layer. [0039] 15 Production of Lithium-Ion Secondary Battery The first positive electrode active material powder (lithium iron phosphate; particle size of secondary particles: 16 to 20 μm), the second positive electrode active material powder (lithium iron phosphate; particle size of secondary particles: 2 to 3 μm), CMC (BSH6), and the acrylic polymer binder 20 (aqueous binder, AXA391) were mixed so as to have the respective solid-content compositions shown in Table 3. Water was added to the mixed power and kneaded to prepare positive electrode active material slurries of Working Examples 1 to 7 and Comparative Examples 1 to 4. The positive electrode active material slurries were each applied onto an aluminum foil (positive electrode 25 current collector sheet), and the coating films were dried to form positive electrode active material layers having a thickness of approximately 200 μm on the positive electrode current collector sheets, thereby producing positive electrodes of Working Examples 1 to 7 and Comparative Examples 1 to 4. Table 3 also shows the total percentage of CMC and the aqueous binder in the positive 20 electrode active material layer or in the solid-content composition, as well as the weight proportion (b/a) of the binder (b) relative to CMC (a). [0040] [Table 3] 5 [0041] Next, the produced positive electrode, a polyolefin separator, a carbonbased negative electrode, and a non-aqueous electrolyte (a 1M LiPF6 electrolyte (carbonate-based solvent)) were placed in a coin cell case to produce lithium-ion secondary batteries (coin cells) of Working Examples 1 to 7 and Comparative 10 Examples 1 to 4. Specifically, a 1C charge–discharge cycle was repeated five 21 times with an upper cutoff voltage of 3.6 V and a lower cutoff voltage of 2.0 V, and the battery capacity (discharge capacity) was calculated based on the discharge in the fifth cycle. The calculated battery capacity is shown in Table 3. From Table 3, it was found that when the total of the percentage of the 5 aqueous binder and the percentage of CMC in the positive electrode active material layer is set to 1.0 wt% or more and 1.8 wt% or less, the lithium-ion battery exhibits a battery capacity of 130 mAh or more. It was also found that favorable battery characteristics were obtained by setting the proportion (b/a) of the mass (b) of the aqueous binder relative to the mass (a) of CMC included in the 10 positive electrode active material layer to 2.0 or more and 3.5 or less. patents.abstract: The present invention provides a positive electrode for lithium ion secondary batteries, the positive electrode being able to have a thick and uniform thickness. A positive electrode for lithium ion secondary batteries according to the present invention comprises a current collector and a positive electrode active material layer that is provided on the current collector. The positive electrode active material layer is characterized by containing positive electrode active material particles, a latex-derived polymer binder, carboxymethyl cellulose sodium or carboxymethyl cellulose calcium, and a mannose-based water-soluble polymer.
patents.complete_specification: TECHNICAL FIELD [0001] The present invention relates to a positive electrode for a lithium ion 5 secondary battery, a lithium ion secondary battery, and a positive electrode active material slurry. BACKGROUND ART [0002] 10 A positive electrode active material layer of a lithium ion battery is usually fabricated by applying a slurry containing positive electrode active material particles, a PVdF binder, N-methylpyrrolidone, and a conductive agent onto a current collector, and drying the applied layer. However, N-methylpyrrolidone is included in the list of substances restricted under REACH due to its toxicity 15 concerns. As a method of fabricating a positive electrode active material layer without using N-methylpyrrolidone, a method is known in which a slurry containing positive electrode active material particles, an aqueous binder, a conductive agent, and water is applied onto a current collector, and the applied 20 layer is dried (for example, see Patent Document 1). PRIOR ART DOCUMENT PATENT DOCUMENT [0003] 25 Patent Document 1: Japanese Patent Laid-Open Publication No. 2017-091789 30 3 SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION PROBLEMS TO BE SOLVED BY THE INVENTION [0004] 5 However, since the conventional positive electrode active material slurry using water as a dispersion medium has a low viscosity, when a thick applied layer is intended to be formed, the positive electrode active material slurry flows in the applied layer, and an applied layer and a positive electrode active material layer having a large and uniform thickness cannot be formed. In addition, 10 cracking may occur in the positive electrode active material layer. The present invention has been made in view of such circumstances, and provides a positive electrode for a lithium ion secondary battery in which a positive electrode active material layer can have a large and uniform thickness. 15 SOLUTIONS TO THE PROBLEMS [0005] The present invention provides a positive electrode for a lithium ion secondary battery, including a current collector and a positive electrode active material layer provided on the current collector, wherein the positive electrode 20 active material layer contains positive electrode active material particles, a latexderived polymer binder, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or calcium carboxymethyl cellulose, and a mannose-based water-soluble polymer. The present invention also provides a lithium ion secondary battery including the positive electrode of the present invention, a negative electrode, a 25 separator, and a non-aqueous electrolyte. The present invention also provides a positive electrode active material slurry containing positive electrode active material particles, a latex-derived polymer binder, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or calcium carboxymethyl cellulose, a mannose-based water-soluble polymer, and water. 4 EFFECTS OF THE INVENTION [0006] Since the mannose-based water-soluble polymer exhibits a high thickening 5 effect even in a small amount, the positive electrode active material slurry of the present invention has high coating stability. Since the positive electrode active material layer of the positive electrode for a lithium ion secondary battery of the present invention can be formed using the positive electrode active material slurry of the present invention, it can have a thick and uniform thickness. Further, the 10 occurrence of cracking in the positive electrode active material layer can be suppressed. As a result, the lithium ion secondary battery of the present invention can have a large battery capacity and high life characteristics. Since the positive electrode active material layer contains only a small amount of the mannose-based water-soluble polymer, the internal resistance can be reduced, and the lithium ion 15 secondary battery of the present invention has excellent output characteristics. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS [0007] FIG. 1(a) is a schematic plan view of a positive electrode for a lithium ion 20 secondary battery of an embodiment of the present invention, and FIG. 1(b) is a schematic cross-sectional view of the positive electrode taken along a dashed line A-A in FIG. 1(a). FIG. 2 is a schematic cross-sectional view of the lithium ion secondary battery of the embodiment of the present invention. 25 FIG. 3(a) is a schematic plan view of a negative electrode included in the lithium ion secondary battery of the embodiment of the present invention, and FIG. 3(b) is a schematic cross-sectional view of the negative electrode taken along a dashed line B-B in FIG. 3(a). 5 FIG. 4 is a schematic structural view of an electrode assembly included in the lithium ion secondary battery of the embodiment of the present invention. FIG. 5 shows discharge curves of lithium ion secondary batteries of Working Examples 1 and 2. 5 EMBODIMENT OF THE INVENTION [0008] An embodiment of the present invention will be described below using the drawings. The configurations shown in the drawings and the following description 10 are examples, and the scope of the present invention is not limited to those shown in the drawings and the following description. A positive electrode 5 for a lithium ion secondary battery of the present embodiment includes a current collector 3 and a positive electrode active material layer 2 provided on the current collector 3, in which the positive electrode active 15 material layer 2 contains positive electrode active material particles, a latexderived polymer binder, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or calcium carboxymethyl cellulose, and a mannose-based water-soluble polymer. A lithium ion secondary battery 30 of the present embodiment includes the positive electrode 5, a negative electrode 32, a separator 34, and a non-aqueous 20 electrolyte 15. A positive electrode active material slurry of the present embodiment contains positive electrode active material particles, a latex-derived polymer binder, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or calcium carboxymethyl cellulose, a mannose-based water-soluble polymer, and water. 25 [0009] The positive electrode 5 for a lithium ion secondary battery is a positive electrode 5 included in the lithium ion secondary battery 30 or is a positive electrode 5 used for producing the lithium ion secondary battery 30. 6 The positive electrode 5 for a lithium ion secondary battery includes a positive electrode current collector 3 and a porous positive electrode active material layer 2 provided on the positive electrode current collector 3. The positive electrode current collector 3 is a sheet serving as a substrate 5 on which the positive electrode active material layer 2 is provided, and is a conductor electrically connecting a positive electrode connection member 13 and the positive electrode active material layer 2 to each other. The positive electrode current collector 3 is, for example, an aluminum foil. The positive electrode connection member 13 is electrically connected to an external connection terminal 10 18a. The positive electrode active material layer 2 may be provided on one side of the positive electrode current collector 3 or may be provided on both sides of the positive electrode current collector 3. [0010] The positive electrode active material layer 2 is a layer containing a 15 positive electrode active material. The thickness (after pressing) of the positive electrode active material layer 2 may be 150 μm or more and 400 μm or less. As a result, the amount of the positive electrode active material contained in the positive electrode 5 increases, and the battery capacity of the lithium ion secondary battery 30 can be increased. 20 [0011] The positive electrode active material layer 2 contains positive electrode active material particles, a latex-derived polymer binder, CMC (sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or calcium carboxymethyl cellulose), and a mannosebased water-soluble polymer. The positive electrode active material layer 2 may 25 contain a conductive agent. Furthermore, the positive electrode active material layer 2 may contain a surfactant. [0012] The positive electrode active material contained in the positive electrode active material layer 2 is a substance directly involved in electron transfer 7 associated with electric charge transfer on the positive electrode 5. The positive electrode active material is, for example, LiCoO2, LiNiO2, LiNixCo1-xO2 (x = 0.01 to 0.99), LiMnO2, LiMn2O4, LiCoxMnyNizO2 (x + y + z = 1), or olivine-type LiFePO4 or LixFe1-yMyPO4, where 0.05 ≦ x ≦ 1.2, 0 ≦ y ≦ 0.8, and M is at 5 least one or more kinds of Mn, Cr, Co, Cu, Ni, V, Mo, Ti, Zn, Al, Ga, Mg, B, and Nb. The positive electrode active material layer 2 may contain one kind of these positive electrode active materials alone or a mixture of plural kinds thereof. The particles of the positive electrode active material (for example, particles of lithium iron phosphate (LiFePO4)) may have a conductive film on the surface thereof. 10 This can improve the conductivity of the surface of the positive electrode active material on which an intercalation reaction is progressing, and can reduce the internal resistance of the positive electrode 5. The conductive film is, for example, a carbon film. The positive electrode active material particles may be contained in the positive electrode active material layer 2 as secondary particles in which 15 primary particles are aggregated. The average particle diameter of the primary particles of the positive electrode active material can be 30 nm or more and 400 nm or less. The average particle diameter can be calculated by measuring the particle diameters of 100 randomly selected particles in a cross-sectional photograph of the positive electrode active material layer 2 and arithmetically 20 averaging these particle diameters. [0013] The positive electrode active material layer 2 can contain first lithium iron phosphate secondary particles and second lithium iron phosphate secondary particles having a smaller particle diameter than that of the first lithium iron 25 phosphate secondary particles. The first lithium iron phosphate secondary particles are lithium iron phosphate secondary particles having a particle diameter of 10 μm or more among a plurality of lithium iron phosphate secondary particles contained in the positive 8 electrode active material layer 2, and have an average particle diameter of 15 μm or more and 22 μm or less. The second lithium iron phosphate secondary particles are lithium iron phosphate secondary particles having a particle diameter of less than 10 μm 5 among a plurality of lithium iron phosphate secondary particles contained in the positive electrode active material layer 2, and have an average particle diameter of 2 μm or more and 7 μm or less. [0014] For example, the average particle diameter of the first lithium iron 10 phosphate can be obtained by measuring the particle diameters of 100 randomly selected lithium iron phosphate secondary particles in a cross-sectional photograph of the positive electrode active material layer 2, and arithmetically averaging the particle diameters of secondary particles having a particle diameter of 10 μm or more among the secondary particles whose particle diameters have 15 been measured, and the average particle diameter of the second lithium iron phosphate can be obtained by arithmetically averaging the particle diameters of secondary particles having a particle diameter of less than 10 μm among the secondary particles whose particle diameters have been measured. [0015] 20 A ratio (b/a) of the mass (b) of the second lithium iron phosphate secondary particles to the mass (a) of the first lithium iron phosphate secondary particles is, for example, (1/9) or more and (3/7) or less (b : a = 1 : 9 to 3 : 7). The mass of the lithium iron phosphate secondary particles can be calculated from the density and the particle diameter of the lithium iron phosphate secondary 25 particles. The density of the lithium iron phosphate secondary particles can be measured and calculated using lithium iron phosphate secondary particles (powder) equivalent to the lithium iron phosphate secondary particles contained in the positive electrode active material layer 2. 9 [0016] Examples of the conductive agent include fine particles of furnace black, acetylene black, carbon black, and coke-based soft carbon. Since the positive electrode active material layer 2 contains a conductive agent, the conductivity of 5 the positive electrode active material layer 2 can be improved, thereby reducing the internal resistance of the positive electrode 5. [0017] The latex-derived polymer binder is a polymer binder (water-based polymer binder) capable of being colloidally dispersed in a water dispersion 10 medium. The polymer binder is, for example, an acrylic polymer binder or styrene butadiene rubber (SBR). By using such a polymer binder, it is possible to use water or an aqueous solution as a dispersion medium of the positive electrode active material slurry used for forming the positive electrode active material layer 2. The glass transition point Tg of the polymer compound serving as the polymer 15 binder is, for example, 20°C or less, preferably 10°C or less, and more preferably 0°C or less. This enables the polymer binder to have flexibility. Because the positive electrode active material layer 2 contains a polymer binder, it is possible to suppress delamination of the positive electrode active material layer 2 from the positive electrode current collector 3 and the formation 20 of cracks in the positive electrode active material layer 2. [0018] A specific gravity of the acrylic rubber contained in the acrylic polymer binder is 1.1, the range of hardness of the acrylic rubber measured according to JIS standards is 40 to 90, the tensile strength of the acrylic rubber is 70 to 120 kg/cm2 25 , the elongation of the acrylic rubber is 100 to 600%, and the volume resistance of the acrylic rubber is 108 to 1010 Ω/cm. The styrene butadiene rubber (SBR) has a specific gravity of 0.94, the range of hardness of SBR measured according to JIS standards is from 30 to 100, 10 the tensile strength of SBR is from 50 to 200 kg/cm2 , the elongation of SBR is from 100 to 800%, and the volume resistance of SBR is from 1010 to 1015 Ω/cm. [0019] The CMC (sodium carboxymethyl cellulose or calcium carboxymethyl 5 cellulose) has a function of increasing the viscosity of the positive electrode active material slurry used for forming the positive electrode active material layer 2. The CMC may also function as a binder for the positive electrode active material layer 2. Since the positive electrode active material slurry contains CMC, the viscosity of the positive electrode active material slurry can be increased, and the positive 10 electrode active material layer 2 can have a uniform thickness. In addition, the positive electrode active material slurry can be thickly applied, and a thick positive electrode active material layer 2 (having a thickness of, for example, 150 μm or more (after pressing)) can be formed. [0020] 15 The mannose-based water-soluble polymer has a function of increasing the viscosity of the positive electrode active material slurry used for forming the positive electrode active material layer 2. Since the positive electrode active material slurry contains the mannose-based water-soluble polymer, the viscosity of the positive electrode active material slurry can be increased, and the positive 20 electrode active material layer 2 can have a uniform thickness. In addition, the positive electrode active material slurry can be thickly applied, and a thick positive electrode active material layer 2 (having a thickness of, for example, 150 μm or more (after pressing)) can be formed. The mannose-based water-soluble polymer is a polysaccharide containing mannose as a constituent component, and 25 examples thereof include α-mannan, β-mannan, glucomannan (for example, konjac mannan), galactomannan (for example, guar gum, fenugreek gum, tara gum, locust bean gum, cassia gum, etc.), etc. 11 [0021] A ratio (b/a) of the mass (b) of the mannose-based water-soluble polymer contained in the positive electrode active material layer 2 to the mass (a) of the positive electrode active material particles contained in the positive electrode 5 active material layer 2 is, for example, (0.05/98.3) or more and (0.25/98) or less. Thus, the positive electrode active material slurry can have high coating stability, and the positive electrode active material layer 2 can have a large and uniform thickness. As a result, the lithium ion secondary battery 30 can have a large battery capacity and high life characteristics. Since the positive electrode active 10 material layer 2 contains only a small amount of the mannose-based water-soluble polymer, the internal resistance can be reduced, and the lithium ion secondary battery 30 has excellent output characteristics. [0022] A ratio of the total mass ((b + c)/a) of the mass (b) of the mannose-based 15 water-soluble polymer contained in the positive electrode active material layer 2 and the mass (c) of the CMC contained in the positive electrode active material layer 2 to the mass (a) of the positive electrode active material particles contained in the positive electrode active material layer 2 is, for example, (0.45/98.3) or more and (0.85/98) or less. Thus, the positive electrode active material slurry can 20 have high coating stability, and the positive electrode active material layer 2 can have a large and uniform thickness. As a result, the lithium ion secondary battery 30 can have a large battery capacity and high life characteristics. Since the positive electrode active material layer 2 contains only a small amount of the mannose-based water-soluble polymer and CMC, the internal resistance can be 25 reduced, and the lithium ion secondary battery 30 has excellent output characteristics. [0023] For example, a positive electrode active material slurry is prepared by mixing and kneading lithium iron phosphate secondary particles, a latex of a 12 polymer binder (an emulsion in which a polymer compound serving as a binder is colloidally dispersed in water), CMC, a mannose-based water-soluble polymer, and water or an aqueous solution, the slurry is applied onto the positive electrode current collector 3, and the applied layer is dried to form the positive electrode 5 active material layer 2. A small amount of a surfactant may be added to the positive electrode active material slurry. The positive electrode active material layer 2 may be subjected to a press treatment. In the press treatment, for example, a pressure can be applied to the positive electrode active material layer 2 so that the porosity of the positive electrode active material layer 2 falls within a range of 10 20% to 40%. The positive electrode active material slurry can have a viscosity of, for example, 4000 mPa·s or more and 15000 mPa·s or less. As a result, the positive electrode active material layer 2 having a large and uniform thickness can be formed. The viscosity of the positive electrode active material slurry may be a 15 viscosity measured using a B-type viscometer under the condition of a rotation speed of 10 rpm. [0024] For example, the positive electrode active material layer 2 can contain 95 wt% or more and 98.5 wt% or less of the lithium iron phosphate particles, 1.0 20 wt% or more and 1.5 wt% or less of the latex-derived polymer binder, 0.3 wt% or more and 0.7 wt% or less of the CMC, and 0.01 wt% or more and 0.3 wt% or less of the mannose-based water-soluble polymer. The positive electrode active material slurry can be prepared by mixing the respective materials so that the positive electrode active material layer 2 has such a solid content composition. 25 The solid content percentage of the positive electrode active material slurry can be, for example, 55 wt% or more and 67 wt% or less. [0025] The negative electrode 32 is an electrode having a porous negative electrode active material layer 36. The negative electrode active material layer 36 13 is, for example, a porous layer which is provided on a sheet-like negative electrode current collector 38 and contains a negative electrode active material. The negative electrode current collector 38 is electrically connected to a negative electrode connection member 14. Further, the negative electrode connection 5 member 14 is electrically connected to an external connection terminal 18b. The negative electrode current collector 38 is, for example, a copper foil. The negative electrode active material is a substance directly involved in electron transfer associated with electric charge transfer on the negative electrode. Examples of the negative electrode active material include graphite, partially 10 graphitized carbon, hard carbon, soft carbon, lithium titanate (LTO), and an Sn alloy. The negative electrode active material layer 36 can contain one kind of these negative electrode active materials alone or a mixture of plural kinds thereof. [0026] 15 The separator 34 has a sheet shape and is disposed between the positive electrodes 5 and the negative electrodes 32. Further, the separator 34 can configure, together with the positive electrodes 5 and the negative electrodes 32, an electrode assembly 22 as shown in FIG. 4. By providing the separator 34, it is possible to prevent a short-circuit current from flowing between the positive 20 electrodes 5 and the negative electrodes 32. There is no particular limitation on the separator 34 if the short-circuit current can be prevented from flowing and if ions conducting between the positive electrodes and the negative electrodes can pass through the separator 34, and a microporous film of polyolefin, a cellulose sheet, or an aramid sheet can be used, 25 for example. The separator 34 may be a nonwoven fabric containing at least one of a cellulose fiber, a polyester fiber, a polypropylene fiber, a polyacrylonitrile fiber, and a polyethylene terephthalate fiber. 14 [0027] As shown in FIG. 4, the electrode assembly 22 can have a structure in which a plurality of positive electrodes 5 and a plurality of negative electrodes 32 are laminated so that the positive electrodes 5 and the negative electrodes 32 are 5 alternately disposed. The electrode assembly 22 can have a structure in which the separator 34 is disposed between the positive electrode 5 and the negative electrode 32 adjacent to each other. [0028] For the non-aqueous electrolyte 15, carbonates, lactones, ethers, esters, 10 ionic liquids, or the like may be used as solvents, and two or more kinds of these solvents may be mixed and used. In particular, a cyclic carbonate and a chain carbonate of these solvents are preferably mixed and used. The non-aqueous electrolyte 15 is, for example, a solution in which a solute of a lithium salt such as LiCF3SO3, LiAsF6, LiClO4, LiBF4, LiPF6, LiBOB, LiN(CF3SO2)2, or 15 LiN(C2F5SO2) is dissolved in an organic solvent. Further, if necessary, additives such as VC (vinylene carbonate), PS (propane sultone), VEC (vinyl ethyl carbonate), PRS (propene sultone) and a flame retardant may be blended, either individually or in a mixture of plural kinds thereof. [0029] 20 A battery case 11 is a battery casing that houses the electrode assembly 22 (including the positive electrode 5, the negative electrode 32, and the separator 34) and the non-aqueous electrolyte 15. The battery case 11 may be made in a pouch shape made by welding a laminate film at a welded part. In this case, the lithium ion secondary battery 30 is a pouch battery. Alternatively, the battery case 25 11 may be a metal case or a hard resin case. The battery case 11 may have a lid member 12. 15 [0030] Preparation of positive electrode active material slurry Lithium iron phosphate powder, an acrylic polymer binder liquid (latex dispersed aqueous solution AXA391, active ingredient concentration: 40 wt%, 5 glass transition point Tg:-35°C, pH: 7 to 9, B-type viscosity: 5 to 50 cP, average particle diameter: 180 μm, particle diameter distribution: peak at 170 μm (100 to 500 μm)), sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC, BSH6 (degree of etherification: 0.65 to 0.75, viscosity of 1% CMC aqueous solution at 25°C: 3000 to 4000 mPa·s) manufactured by Dai-ichi Kogyo Seiyaku Co., Ltd.), konjac 10 mannan, guar gum, xanthan gum, and glucose (starch) shown in the solid content compositions of Working Examples 1 to 3 and Comparative Examples 1 to 4 in Table 1 were mixed so as to obtain the solid content compositions shown in Table 1. The components indicated by horizontal bars in Table 1 were not mixed. Then, water was added to the mixtures and kneaded so as to obtain the solid content 15 percentages shown in Table 1, thereby preparing positive electrode active material slurries of Working Examples 1 to 3 and Comparative Examples 1 to 4. [0031] [Table 1] 16 [0032] Viscosity measurement The viscosity of each of the positive electrode active material slurries of Working Examples 1 to 3 and Comparative Examples 1 and 2 was measured 5 using a B-type viscometer (TV-22 manufactured by Toki Sangyo Co., Ltd.) (spindle rotor: H, No. 4, rotation speed: 10 rpm). Measurement results are shown in Table 1. It was found that the positive electrode active material slurries of Working Examples 1 to 3 had a viscosity of 4000 mPa·s or more and 15000 mPa·s or less, and had a viscosity suitable for coating. 10 [0033] Evaluation of spinnability The spinnability of each of the positive electrode active material slurries of Working Examples 1 to 3 and Comparative Examples 1 and 2 was evaluated. Specifically, a 100 ml beaker containing the positive electrode active material 15 slurry was tilted so that the positive electrode active material slurry dripped from the pouring port (flow rate: about 0.5 ml/sec), and whether or not stringing occurred was observed. Further, a medicine spoon was put into a 100 ml beaker containing the positive electrode active material slurry, and when the medicine spoon was lifted, whether or not stringing occurred in the positive electrode active 20 material slurry attached to the medicine spoon was observed. Evaluation results are shown in Table 1. Stringing was observed in the positive electrode active material slurries of Working Examples 1 to 3, but stringing was not observed in the positive electrode active material slurries of Comparative Examples 1 and 2. 25 [0034] Production of lithium ion secondary battery Lithium ion secondary batteries were produced using each of the positive electrode active material slurries of Working Examples 1 and 2. Specifically, the positive electrode active material slurry was applied onto an aluminum foil 17 (positive electrode current collecting sheet), and the applied film was dried and further pressed to form a positive electrode active material layer (length: 142 mm, width: 84.5 mm) having a thickness of 221 μm on one surface of the positive electrode current collecting sheet, thereby fabricating a positive electrode. No 5 cracking occurred in the positive electrode active material layer. [0035] 94 wt% (solid content percentage) of graphite powder, 5 wt% (solid content percentage) of SBR binder, and 1 wt% (solid content percentage) of sodium carboxymethylcellulose were mixed together. Water was added to the 10 mixture and kneaded to prepare a negative electrode active material slurry. The negative electrode active material slurry was applied onto a copper foil (negative electrode current collecting sheet), and the applied film was dried and further pressed to form a negative electrode active material layer (length: 145 mm, width: 86.8 mm) having a thickness of 82.5 μm on one surface of the negative electrode 15 current collecting sheet, thereby fabricating a negative electrode. [0036] Next, the fabricated positive electrode, a separator (three layer separator manufactured by Toray Industries, Inc.), the fabricated negative electrode, and a non-aqueous electrolyte (1.2 M of LiPF6 electrolyte solution (carbonate-based 20 electrolyte solution)) were placed in a battery case to produce the lithium ion secondary batteries of Working Examples 1 and 2. [0037] Discharge curves of the lithium ion secondary batteries of Working Examples 1 and 2 are shown in FIG. 5. The lithium ion secondary batteries of 25 Working Examples 1 and 2 were found to have excellent discharge characteristics.
