The present invention provides a machine learning-based intelligent lithium battery charging and health management system for electric vehicles that is configured to optimize charging operations and improve battery performance throughout its operational lifecycle. The system employs intelligent data acquisition techniques to continuously monitor battery-related parameters including cell voltage, pack voltage, charging current, battery temperature, internal resistance, charge and discharge cycles, ambient environmental conditions, and charging history. These operational parameters are collected in real time through integrated battery sensing modules and are subsequently processed to generate meaningful battery health indicators. By leveraging machine learning algorithms, the disclosed system enables intelligent decision-making for battery charging optimization while reducing the likelihood of battery degradation and performance deterioration. The system comprises a battery data acquisition module configured to collect and organize operational data generated during vehicle operation and charging events. The battery data acquisition module may communicate with battery management controllers and onboard vehicle systems to capture multiple battery performance indicators. The collected data are subjected to preprocessing operations such as normalization, noise filtering, outlier detection, and feature extraction before being supplied to a machine learning analytics engine. The preprocessing mechanism improves the quality and consistency of battery-related information and enables more accurate predictive analytics. The system may further maintain historical battery datasets to facilitate longitudinal battery health assessments and machine learning model training operations. The machine learning analytics engine is configured to estimate battery state-of-charge, state-of-health, remaining useful life, and battery degradation characteristics by utilizing one or more machine learning models. Suitable machine learning techniques may include neural networks, Long Short-Term Memory networks, reinforcement learning algorithms, gradient boosting models, support vector machines, ensemble learning approaches, and hybrid predictive models. The machine learning engine continuously evaluates real-time battery operational parameters and historical battery performance data to identify degradation trends and charging inefficiencies. By learning battery behavior patterns under varying operational conditions, the system dynamically generates predictive outputs that facilitate intelligent charging decisions and battery maintenance recommendations. The intelligent charging optimization module receives predictive outputs generated by the machine learning analytics engine and determines optimal charging parameters for the lithium battery system. The charging optimization module may dynamically regulate charging voltage levels, charging current profiles, charging duration, fast-charging thresholds, and charging cut-off parameters based on battery health conditions and environmental factors. The module further determines appropriate charging strategies that minimize electrochemical stress and improve charging efficiency without compromising battery safety. Adaptive charging profiles generated by the system enable the battery to operate within optimal performance ranges across different battery chemistries, operating temperatures, and vehicle usage patterns. The present invention further comprises an intelligent thermal management module configured to monitor and predict battery thermal behavior during charging and discharging operations. Thermal management plays a significant role in extending battery lifespan and preventing battery-related failures. The disclosed thermal management module utilizes predictive machine learning models to identify thermal abnormalities and forecast temperature variations under anticipated charging conditions. Upon detection of undesirable thermal conditions, the system may initiate corrective actions including charging rate adjustments, cooling system activation, and charging schedule modifications. The thermal management functionality significantly enhances battery safety by mitigating thermal stress and reducing the possibility of overheating or thermal runaway events. The disclosed system further incorporates a predictive battery health management module that continuously evaluates battery degradation patterns and estimates remaining useful battery life. The predictive battery health management module generates maintenance recommendations and battery health reports based on operational history and machine learning-driven analytics. The system may identify capacity fade trends, charging inefficiencies, abnormal cell behavior, and battery aging characteristics before significant performance degradation occurs. Predictive maintenance capabilities enable electric vehicle manufacturers, fleet operators, and end users to implement proactive battery management strategies that reduce maintenance costs and improve overall vehicle reliability. The present invention may be implemented using cloud computing platforms, edge computing devices, onboard vehicle processors, or hybrid computational architectures. Cloud-based deployments facilitate fleet-level battery analytics and enable continuous machine learning model improvements using aggregated battery performance datasets collected from multiple electric vehicles. Edge-based deployments support real-time charging decisions and reduced computational latency during vehicle operation. The adaptive learning capabilities of the disclosed invention enable continuous refinement of battery charging strategies based on user behavior, environmental conditions, battery chemistry variations, and evolving battery degradation characteristics. Consequently, the invention provides an intelligent and scalable battery charging and health management framework suitable for next-generation electric mobility applications. In one embodiment, the machine learning-based intelligent lithium battery charging and health management system utilizes Long Short-Term Memory neural networks for predicting battery degradation and estimating remaining useful life. The system continuously monitors charging cycles, temperature variations, voltage fluctuations, and charging behaviors to generate predictive battery health metrics. During charging operations, the intelligent charging optimization module dynamically adjusts charging current and charging voltage profiles to minimize battery stress and improve charging efficiency. The system is particularly advantageous for electric vehicles employing fast-charging technologies, wherein adaptive charging decisions significantly contribute to enhanced battery lifespan and improved operational safety. In another embodiment, the disclosed system employs reinforcement learning algorithms to determine personalized charging strategies based on battery usage patterns and environmental operating conditions. The machine learning engine learns optimal charging behavior by continuously evaluating historical charging data and battery performance characteristics. The intelligent charging module adapts charging parameters for different battery health states and ambient temperatures while maintaining battery performance within predefined safety limits. The predictive thermal management mechanism proactively identifies thermal anomalies and implements corrective measures to improve battery reliability and reduce charging-related degradation under varying vehicle operating conditions. In yet another embodiment, the intelligent lithium battery charging and health management system is implemented within a cloud-edge hybrid computing architecture for electric vehicle fleet management applications. Battery operational data collected from multiple electric vehicles are securely transmitted to cloud-based analytics platforms for fleet-level battery health assessments and machine learning model optimization. Edge computing components deployed within individual vehicles perform real-time charging optimization and anomaly detection functions. The system generates predictive maintenance alerts, battery replacement recommendations, and fleet charging optimization strategies, thereby enabling improved battery utilization, reduced maintenance costs, and enhanced operational efficiency across large-scale electric vehicle deployments. patents.abstract: The present invention relates to an application-integrated real-time battery monitoring and protection system for lithium-ion batteries comprising a sensor data acquisition unit, a microcontroller unit, a relay-based charging disconnect module, local audio-visual alert units, and a wireless communication module. Battery voltage and temperature are continuously acquired and compared against predefined safety thresholds by the microcontroller unit, which TENT TCE CH autonomously actuates a relay to interrupt the charging circuit and triggers a buzzer and lightemitting diode indicator whenever an overvoltage, over-temperature or other unsafe condition is detected, independently of network availability. A local display unit presents real-time voltage, temperature, State-of-Charge and charging-status information, while a Wi-Fi communication module periodically transmits the processed parameters to a remote server and companion mobile application. The mobile application renders the received data as real-time readouts and graphical trends, generates push notifications upon fault detection, and stores historical data in a database for long-term performance analysis and predictive maintenance, thereby providing an integrated, low-cost solution combining dependable hardware-level protection with remote IoT-based monitoring for electric vehicle, renewable energy storage and portable electronic applications.
patents.complete_specification: TITLE OF THE INVENTION: APPLICATION-INTEGRATED REAL-TIME BATTERY MONITORING AND AUTOMATED PROTECTION SYSTEM WITH RELAY-BASED CHARGING DISCONNECT AND MOBILE ALERT NOTIFICATION FOR LITHIUM-ION BATTERIES FIELD OF THE INVENTION: The present invention relates to battery management technology, embedded microcontrollerbased monitoring systems, and Internet of Things (IoT) enabled electrical safety systems. More particularly, the invention relates to an application-integrated real-time battery monitoring and protection system employing a microcontroller unit to continuously acquire voltage, temperature and charging-status parameters of a lithium-ion battery pack, to execute automated threshold-based protection through a relay-controlled charging disconnect mechanism, and to transmit processed battery data wirelessly to a remote server and companion mobile application for real-time visualisation, historical logging and alert notification. BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION: The growing adoption of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles, renewable energy storage installations and portable electronic devices has increased the demand for reliable battery management systems capable of ensuring safe charging and discharging operation. Lithiumion cells are sensitive to overvoltage, over-temperature and abnormal charging conditions, and deviation beyond safe operating limits can result in accelerated degradation, reduced service life or hazardous thermal events. Conventional battery monitoring arrangements are largely confined to local, hardware-only implementations that display operating parameters on a panel-mounted indicator without providing any facility for remote observation, historical data logging or timely notification to a user who is not physically present at the installation. Where wireless or cloud-connected monitoring has been proposed, such arrangements have generally emphasised data acquisition and visualisation alone, without incorporating a correspondingly robust, hardware-level automatic protection mechanism capable of interrupting the charging path independently of 17, Wi-Fl Communication Module (500) network availability. As a result, existing solutions either provide adequate local protection without remote visibility, or provide remote visibility without dependable autonomous protection, but rarely both within a single, integrated, low-cost architecture. There therefore exists a need for a compact and cost-effective battery management architecture that-combines— continuous local sensing-of—voltage, temperature and charging status, autonomous, network-independent protective disconnection of the charging circuit upon detection of an unsafe condition; local audio-visual alerting; and wireless transmission of processed battery parameters to a remote server and companion mobile application for realtime monitoring, State-of-Charge visualisation, historical data review and push-based alert notification. DRAWING: Battery Pack (100) Sensor Data Acquisition Unit (200) Voltage Sensing Circuit (210) Temperature Sensor Circuit (220) Charging Input Status Detector (230) alicrocontrollor Unit / ESP32 ( 00) Safety Threshold Comparator (Voltage/ Temperature Logic) (310) Protection Control IS Data Formatting Logic (320) Relay-Based Charging Disconnect Module Buzzer Alert Unit LED Status Indicator Local Display Unit (I2C LCD) (400) (420) (430) (440) P.. I BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS FIG. 1: Illustrates a block diagram of the Application-Integrated Real-Time Battery Monitoring and Protection System showing the interconnection among the Battery Pack (100), Sensor Data Acquisition Unit (200) comprising a Voltage Sensing Circuit (210), Temperature Sensor Circuit (220) and Charging Input Status Detector (230), Microcontroller Unit (300) comprising a Safety Threshold Comparator (310) and Protection Control and Data Formatting Logic (320), Relay-Based Charging Disconnect Module (400), Charger Input (410), Buzzer Alert Unit (420), Light-Emitting Diode Status Indicator (430), Local Display Unit (440), Wi-Fi Communication Module (500), Remote Web / Cloud Server (510), Mobile Application (520), and System History Database (530). The figure depicts the data flow from physical battery telemetry acquisition to microcontrollerbased safety evaluation, autonomous relay protection, local alerting, and wireless transmission to a remote server and mobile application for real-time monitoring and historical logging. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWING: The drawing illustrates the overall architecture of an application-integrated real-time battery monitoring and protection system. At the top of the architecture, a Battery Pack (100) supplies electrical power and is the subject of continuous monitoring during charging and discharging operation. Operational parameters of the Battery Pack (100) are captured by a Sensor Data Acquisition Unit (200), which comprises a Voltage Sensing Circuit (210) implemented as a resistive divider network for measuring battery terminal voltage, a Temperature Sensor Circuit (220) for measuring cell temperature, and a Charging Input Status Detector (230) for identifying the presence of an external charging source. The acquired signals are supplied to a Microcontroller Unit (300), which comprises a Safety Threshold Comparator (310) configured to compare the measured voltage and temperature values with predefined safety limits, and a Protection Control and Data Formatting Logic (320) configured to generate control signals and structure sensor readings for local display and wireless transmission. Where the Safety Threshold Comparator (310) determines that a measured parameter has exceeded its corresponding safety limit, the Protection Control Logic (320) actuates a Relay-Based Charging Disconnect Module (400), which physically interrupts the Charger Input (410) from the Battery Pack (100), thereby halting the charging process. Concurrently, the Microcontroller Unit (300) activates a Buzzer Alert Unit (420) to provide an audible warning and a Light-Emitting Diode Status Indicator (430) to provide a visual indication of the fault condition. A Local Display Unit (440), implemented as an inter-integrated-circuit liquid crystal display, continuously presents real-time voltage, temperature, State-of-Charge and charging-status information, enabling on-site verification without requiring network access. The Microcontroller Unit (300) is further connected to a Wi-Fi Communication Module (500), which periodically transmits the processed battery parameters to a Remote Web / Cloud Server (510) over a wireless network connection. The Remote Web / Cloud Server (510) forwards the received data to a Mobile Application (520), which displays real-time readouts, graphical trend visualisations and push-based alert notifications to the user, and further stores the received data in a System History Database (530) for historical analysis and predictive maintenance. The drawing therefore represents a closed-loop battery monitoring and protection architecture integrating local hardware-level sensing and protection with wireless data transmission, remote visualisation and cloud-based historical logging. SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION: The present invention discloses an application-integrated real-time battery monitoring and protection system comprising a Battery Pack, a Sensor Data Acquisition Unit, a Microcontroller Unit, a Relay-Based Charging Disconnect Module, a Buzzer Alert Unit, a Light-Emitting Diode Status Indicator, a Local Display Unit, a Wi-Fi Communication Module, a Remote Web / Cloud Server and a Mobile Application. Voltage and temperature parameters are continuously captured from the battery pack and compared against predefined safety thresholds by the microcontroller unit. Upon detection of an overvoltage, over-temperature or other unsafe condition, the microcontroller unit autonomously actuates a relay to disconnect the charging circuit and simultaneously triggers audible and visual local alerts, this protective action occurring independently of network connectivity. The processed battery parameters, together with an estimated State-of-Charge value, are transmitted wirelessly to a remote server and companion mobile application, enabling real-time visualisation, graphical trend analysis, push-based fault notification and historical data logging. The system thereby integrates dependable local hardware-level protection with remote IoTbased monitoring within a single, compact and low-cost architecture suitable for lithium-ion battery installations in electric vehicles, renewable energy storage and portable electronic devices. DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION: The system comprises a Battery Pack (100), which represents a rechargeable electrochemical energy storage unit, including but not limited to a lithium-ion cell, and which generates realtime electrical output during charging and discharging operation. A Sensor Data Acquisition Unit (200) is operatively connected to the Battery Pack (100) and is configured to capture a battery terminal voltage through a Voltage Sensing Circuit (210) comprising a resistive divider network scaled to a level compatible with an analog-to-digital converter input of a Microcontroller Unit (300), a battery temperature through a Temperature Sensor Circuit (220) communicating over a single-wire digital protocol, and a charging-source presence signal through a Charging Input Status Detector (230). The Microcontroller Unit (300) which may be implemented using a Wi-Fi-enabled system-onchip, receives the captured signals from the Sensor Data Acquisition Unit (200) and serves as the central processing element of the system. Within the Microcontroller Unit (300), a Safety Threshold Comparator (310) continuously evaluates the measured voltage and temperature values against predefined safety thresholds representing an overvoltage limit and an overtemperature limit respectively. Upon determinirig that a measured parameter has exceeded its corresponding threshold, a Protection Control and Data Formatting Logic (320) generates a control signal that-actuates a Relay-Based Charging Disconnect Module (400). The Relay-Based Charging Disconnect Module (400) is operatively interposed between a Charger Input (410) and the Battery Pack (100), and physically opens the charging circuit to prevent continued charging under an unsafe condition, this actuation occurring independently of the availability of a wireless network connection so as to provide dependable protection at all times. The Protection Control and Data Formatting Logic (320) is further configured to activate a Buzzer Alert Unit (420) to produce an audible alert and a Light-Emitting Diode Status Indicator (430) to produce a visual alert whenever a fault condition, including overvoltage, overtemperature or overcurrent, is detected, thereby providing redundant local warning to a user in the vicinity of the system. A Local Display Unit (440), such as a sixteen-by-two character inter-integrated-circuit liquid crystal display, is operatively connected to the Microcontroller Unit (300) and is configured to continuously present the measured voltage, temperature, estimated State-of-Charge and charging status, thereby permitting immediate on-site verification of battery condition without requiring an active network connection. A Wi-Fi Communication Module (500) integrated with the Microcontroller Unit (300) establishes a connection with a local wireless network and periodically transmits the processed battery parameters, formatted as a structured data request, to a Remote Web / Cloud Server (510). The Remote Web / Cloud Server (510) receives, stores and forwards the transmitted battery parameters to a Mobile Application (520) executing on a user device, the Mobile Application (520) being configured to render the received parameters as real-time numerical indicators and graphical trend charts, and to generate a push notification upon receipt of a fault indication from the Microcontroller Unit (300). A System History Database (530) is operatively connected to the Remote Web / Cloud Server (510) and persistently stores historical telemetry data, fault events and State-of-Charge trends, thereby supporting long-term performance analysis and predictive maintenance through the Mobile Application (520). The Microcontroller Unit (300) may further be configured to estimate a State-of-Charge value of the Battery Pack (100) based on the measured voltage, and in certain embodiments a measured or estimated current parameter, using coulomb-counting or open-circuit-voltage based estimation techniques, and to transmit the estimated State-of-Charge value together with •the other battery parameters for display on the Local Display Unit (440) and the Mobile Application (520). Claims: 1. An application-integrated real-time battery monitoring and protection system comprising a sensor data acquisition unit configured to measure voltage and temperature of a battery pack, a microcontroller unit configured to compare the measured parameters against predefined safety thresholds, a relay-based charging disconnect module operatively controlled by the microcontroller unit to interrupt a charging circuit upon detection of an unsafe condition, and a wireless communication module configured to transmit processed battery parameters to a remote server and a mobile application. 2. The system as claimed in claim 1, wherein the sensor data acquisition unit comprises a resistive voltage divider circuit connected to an analog input of the microcontroller unit for measuring battery terminal voltage, and a digital temperature sensor communicating with the microcontroller unit over a single-wire protocol. 3. The system as claimed in claim 1, wherein the microcontroller unit is configured to autonomously actuate the relay-based charging disconnect module independently of the F 11 HE , i availability of a wireless network connection, so as to provide protection during loss of connectivity. 4. The system as claimed in claim 1, further comprising a buzzer alert unit and a lightemitting diode status indicator, each operatively controlled by the microcontroller unit to generate an audible and a visual warning respectively upon detection of an overvoltage, over-temperature or other unsafe operating condition. 5. The system as claimed in claim 1, further comprising a local display unit operatively connected to the microcontroller unit and configured to continuously present real-time voltage, temperature, State-of-Charge and charging-status information without requiring network access. 6. The system as claimed in claim 1, wherein the wireless communication module transmits the processed battery parameters to the remote server at periodic intervals using a hypertext transfer protocol request, and wherein the mobile application is configured to display the received parameters as real-time numerical readouts and timeseries graphs, and to generate a push notification upon receipt of a fault indication. 7. The system as claimed in claim 1, wherein the microcontroller unit is further configured to estimate a State-of-Charge value of the battery pack based on the measured voltage and current parameters, and to transmit the estimated State-of-Charge value to the mobile application for display. 8. The system as claimed in claim 1, wherein the system is configured to operate continuously to log historical telemetry data, diagnostic events and fault occurrences in a database accessible through the mobile application for trend analysis and predictive maintenance.

patents.abstract: A lithium iron phosphate precursor, the preparation of which includes: uniformly mixing a metal oxide, a dispersant, a carbon source, a lithium source, and a first lithium iron phosphate in an aqueous solution, followed by a first grinding to obtain a first precursor with a median particle diameter (D50) of 0.35 to 0.39 μm; then adding a second lithium iron phosphate to the first precursor, uniformly mixing, and performing a second grinding to obtain the lithium iron phosphate precursor with a median particle diameter (D50) of 0.35 to 0.39 μm. The overall process provided by the present invention is simple and does not require repeated replacement of materials, reaction environments, or equipment, reflecting the advantages of a continuous process. In addition, the lithium iron phosphate battery cathode material produced from this precursor exhibits high compaction density characteristics. Figure 1

patents.abstract: Provided is lithium secondary battery electrode binder capable of suppressing an increase in internal resistance due to charging and discharging. A lithium secondary battery electrode binder according to an embodiment of the present invention includes: (A) a polyisocyanate component including at least one selected from the group consisting of diphenylmethane diisocyanate and modified bodies thereof; (B) a polyol component including a hydrogenated polybutadiene polyol; (C) an active hydrogen group-containing carboxylic acid; and (D) an aqueous dispersion of a salt of a polyurethane obtained by reacting water as a chain extender. The salt of the polyurethane does not substantially contain a structure derived from an amine-based chain extender.

patents.abstract: Disclosed are a lithium iron phosphate precursor, a lithium iron phosphate material, a preparation method therefor, and a use thereof. The lithium iron phosphate material comprises a flower cluster structure, the flower cluster structure comprises secondary particles, and the secondary particles are formed by agglomerating primary particles by means of a coating layer; the material of the primary particles is lithium iron phosphate. The lithium iron phosphate material of the present invention has good electrochemical properties and processing properties when used in batteries.

patents.abstract: Provided is a metal ion recovery device and a metal ion recovery method with which it is possible to use an ion-permeable membrane stably for a long period of time. A lithium recovery device 1 comprises: a treatment tank 2 that accommodates a stock solution 100, which is an aqueous solution and contains lithium, and a recovery liquid 200, which is an aqueous solution; an ion-permeable membrane 3 that is disposed so as to partition the stock solution 100 and the recovery liquid 200 in the treatment tank 2, and that is mainly composed of an ion conductor of lithium; a positive electrode 4 that is provided on one main surface of the ion-permeable membrane 3; a negative electrode 5 that is provided on another main surface of the ion-permeable membrane 3; and a current collector 6 that is provided between the ion-permeable membrane 3 and the positive electrode 4, or between the ion-permeable membrane 3 and the negative electrode 5. The contact area between the ion-permeable membrane 3 and the current collector 6 is 5% or less of the total area of the main surfaces of the ion-permeable membrane 3.

patents.abstract: In a lithium recovery device 1, a treatment tank 7 is partitioned into three chambers in the order of chambers 11, 12, 13 by means of an ion conductive film 31 and a lithium ion conductive electrolyte film 2. A power supply 5 is connected between electrodes 41, 42 respectively provided inside the chambers 11, 13 located at both ends, with a first electrode chamber 11 side as a positive side. Water S1 is accommodated in the first electrode chamber 11, a non-aqueous solution FS having Li is accommodated in the Li supply chamber 12, and an aqueous solution RS for Li recovery is accommodated in the Li recovery chamber 13. When a voltage is applied by the power supply 5, H+ passes through the ion conductive film 31 from the water S1 and moves to the Li-containing non-aqueous solution FS. In the Li-containing non-aqueous solution FS supplied with H+, in order to keep charge balance, Li+ moves into the lithium ion conductive electrolyte film 2, and Li+ in the lithium ion conductive electrolyte film 2 moves to the aqueous solution RS for Li recovery.

patents.abstract: The present invention relates to a lithium-containing aqueous sulfuric acid solution and a method for preparing same. This method for preparing the aqueous sulfuric acid solution comprises the steps of: obtaining a valuable metal recovery composition from waste batteries, the valuable metal recovery composition containing valuable metal alloys, lithium compounds, copper (Cu), and graphite; separating graphite from the valuable metal recovery composition; performing sulfuric acid leaching of valuable metals, lithium compounds, and copper (Cu) in the valuable metal recovery composition; recovering the valuable metals and the copper (Cu) through solid-liquid separation in a leached lithium-containing aqueous sulfuric acid solution; and removing residual impurities from the leached lithium-containing aqueous sulfuric acid solution after the recovery step.
